Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md` — ## 11. Downstream Derivation and Retained Questions. Standing: Established Information Unit boundary; unresolved downstream realisation preserved.
This conceptual model does **not yet establish**:
- complete Information Unit types or detailed structures; - complete Identity, Metadata or Context attributes; - Data Objects, schemas or Java classes; - persistence envelopes, cache structures or transport messages; - API representations or FHIR mappings; - Application Component allocations.
Detailed Information Unit structures are expected to become clearer through downstream Data Object dissemination, Application Architecture decomposition, Integration Architecture, Technology Architecture and implementation design. Those derivations SHALL respect the semantic boundary and release governance defined here rather than invent missing Information Architecture.
The complete managed-state model, Episode responsibility, Observation/Finding derivation, assurance/evidence and capacity information structures, Digital Twin information structures and residual candidate-family approvals remain outside this model's established decisions.
### 11.1 Adjudicated Search Management Boundary
The 2026-10-10 [two-case search adjudication](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md) resolves the former generic search-management question:
- **Harmonia-managed search** produces a managed metadata-based **Search Result Set**, governed within its own Information Unit boundary. Membership references the Information Unit Versions comprising that result, without copying their content, creating new Versions of them or another authority. - **External search** is intentionally performed within an **Ergo activity**. Returned information is acquired and persisted within that activity's governed context and applicable Information Unit boundary; no additional generic management-acceptance transition is required because the origin is external.
Search metadata categories and `0..*` Version-reference membership establish information meaning, not a complete schema. API/result representation, reference encoding, storage/cache and manifestation mechanics remain downstream. Snapshot/export and detailed Audit / Assurance remain separate concerns. Result encoding, projection or cache treatment SHALL NOT redefine this boundary. [AX-17](../../motivation/principle/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) preserves genuinely unestablished details without retaining the resolved generic acceptance question.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 1. Rejection of Universal Lifecycles. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
A foundational principle of the Harmonia Information Architecture is the explicit rejection of an artificial, universal lifecycle applied indiscriminately across all information assets:
> **Harmonia does NOT impose a single universal lifecycle across Information Concepts. Lifecycles are concept-specific and governed by the business meaning and responsibilities of the owning Capability.**
Different categories of healthcare and operational information progress through fundamentally different states: - A **Catalogue Definition** progresses through publication and versioning lifecycles (*Draft* $\to$ *Active* $\to$ *Deprecated* $\to$ *Retired*). - A **FulfillmentTask** represents a particular undertaking and carries applicable execution progression (illustratively, *Proposed* $\to$ *Accepted* $\to$ *In-Progress* $\to$ *Completed* / *Failed*). This is not a universal transition model; multiple/concurrent undertakings may exist for one ActionableTask where its work semantics allow them. - A **Clinical Document** progresses through legal authoring states (*Draft* $\to$ *Preliminary* $\to$ *Final* $\to$ *Amended* $\to$ *Superseded*). This is a scoped lifecycle illustration: `Final ≠ automatically Final Signed`. Signing, finalisation, authorship, attestation, approval, authentication, verification, authority and legal qualification remain distinct; locally established signing requirements are preserved without making them universal. Amendment and supersession are not mandatory for every document, and consumer processing does not define originating validity or authority. - A **Clinical Assertion / Finding** progresses through epistemic verification (*Suspected* $\to$ *Confirmed* $\to$ *Refuted* / *Entered-in-Error*). - An **Encounter** progresses through admission, movement, and discharge stages (*Planned* $\to$ *Arrived* $\to$ *In-Care* $\to$ *Discharged*).
```mermaid graph TD subgraph DefLC ["Definition Lifecycle"] D1["Draft"] --> D2["Active"] --> D3["Deprecated"] --> D4["Retired"] end
subgraph TaskLC ["FulfillmentTask Execution — Illustrative"] T1["Proposed"] --> T2["Accepted"] --> T3["In-Progress"] --> T4["Completed"] T3 --> T5["Failed"] end
subgraph DocLC ["Clinical Document Lifecycle"] DC1["Draft"] --> DC2["Preliminary"] --> DC3["Final"] --> DC4["Amended"] --> DC5["Superseded"] end
subgraph AssertLC ["Assertion Verification Lifecycle"] A1["Suspected"] --> A2["Confirmed"] A1 --> A3["Refuted"] A2 --> A4["Entered-in-Error"] end ```
The [bounded Task / Work model](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/task-work.md) separates the archetype, work instance, undertaking and governed ActionableTask resolution. An undertaking has its own execution state and may produce output; it does not independently own TaskOutcome. Completion alone does not inherently satisfy its parent: the ActionableTask's explicit outcome policy governs participation and resulting outputs. ExecutionConcurrency, OutcomeConcurrency.Mode and Outcome.OutputRules.Mode remain orthogonal and SHALL NOT be collapsed into a single lifecycle, state or concurrency mechanism. This lifecycle guidance does not adjudicate TaskOutcome lifecycle/identity or the unresolved ReportedTask meaning.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 2. Lifecycle Transition Governance. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
Where an Information Concept is stateful, transitions between states are **governed semantic events**:
```mermaid graph LR S1["Prior State (S1)"] -->|"Transition Event<br/>+ Triggering Activity<br/>+ Authorising Authority<br/>+ Provenance & Timestamp<br/>+ Justification / Reason"| S2["Target State (S2)"] ```
### 2.1 Transition Requirements Every material lifecycle transition SHALL support: 1. **Triggering Context**: The business interaction, clinical activity, or workflow rule that initiated the transition. 2. **Authorising Authority**: The clinician, system, or administrative authority empowered to effect the change. 3. **Transition Provenance**: Timestamp, location, and non-repudiation audit capture. 4. **Justification / Reason**: Explicit rationale, especially for abnormal, exceptional, or erratum transitions (e.g. *Entered-in-Error*, *Emergency Cancellation*).
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 3. Immutability of History & Non-Destructive Progression. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
In accordance with healthcare safety and legal compliance: - **No Physical Destruction / Deletion**: Information Concepts, once asserted or recorded into durable truth, are never subjected to physical destructive deletion. - **State Invalidation via Explicit Supersession / Error Status**: Corrections and retractions are represented as new, append-only assertion events (*Superseded*, *Entered-in-Error*, *Refuted*) that preserve the historical record alongside the rationale for correction. - **Bi-Temporal Integrity**: Information architecture supports reconstructing what was known at any specific past historical point in time (*as-of query*), distinguishing when an event occurred from when it was recorded or amended.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/information-lifecycle.md` — ## 4. Information Unit Context and Managed-State Boundary. Standing: Canonical information governance; concept-specific lifecycles retained.
Lifecycle and Temporal Context are conceptual management concerns within an [Information Unit's Context](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#65-context). The Unit boundary does not impose a universal lifecycle, new lifecycle states or temporal model. Authoritative representation/Version progression remains distinct from valid Active Generation under AX-05. Documenting these concerns does not complete managed-state, history, snapshot or evidence/retention reconciliation, or equate information lifecycle with real-world activity or workflow progression.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/authority-custody-provenance.md` — ## 6. Information Unit Management Boundary. Standing: Canonical information governance; originating authority preserved.
The [canonical Harmonia-managed information definition](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) concerns explicit responsibility to maintain a governed representation and its management context over time. This acceptance remains distinct from originating information authority, domain authority, custody, persistence, transport, presentation and consumption. Externally originated information may be managed without transferring its originating authority to Harmonia; AX-18 applies.
The [Information Unit](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) associates the Governed Representation with Management Context within a governed boundary. Its conceptual [Context concerns](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#65-context) preserve Provenance versus Authority and authoritative Version versus Active Generation. A supplying source need not be the originating authority of every represented assertion/relationship. Recognising the Unit and the information within it is a [platform/framework obligation](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md), not a provenance schema, universal durable-evidence requirement or transfer of source responsibility. The wider evidence/retention and authority vocabulary questions remain for separate reconciliation.

Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/observable-information-and-domain-meaning.md` — ## 1. Authority and Architectural Boundary. Standing: Adjudicated observable-information boundary; runtime AI optional.
The authorised 2026-10-10 Domain04 reconciliation establishes this semantic-agnosticism boundary and incorporates the general runtime-AI adjunct position previously held in legacy execution-model documentation. It defines the relationship between governed information, developer-defined behaviour and domain interpretation. It establishes no new Application Architecture, execution engine, AI orchestration, governance mechanism or implementation.
[AX-01](../../motivation/principle/e9bd61acaaea4577bc4086a5639e52c3.md) retains Harmonia's health-information purpose. [AX-04](../../motivation/principle/54508cda80484a6caf95b901780eaf7d.md) retains its own architectural semantics; [AX-12](../../motivation/principle/ce85889bd9b34f79a53d4c907ceb19d4.md) supports developer access to governed information and models. [AX-06](../../motivation/principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md), [AX-07](../../motivation/principle/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) and [AX-08](../../motivation/principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md) preserve authority, security and meaningful evidence. [AX-14](../../motivation/principle/d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) preserves the distinctions below; [AX-17](../../motivation/principle/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) prohibits inferred architecture, and [AX-18](../../motivation/principle/b8cafe3cf5904d2bb9a9767260fddf78.md) prevents observation or participation from conferring domain authority.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/observable-information-and-domain-meaning.md` — ## 2. Observability and Encapsulated Domain Meaning. Standing: Adjudicated observable-information boundary; runtime AI optional.
Harmonia's concept of reality is bounded by its observability of that reality through the information available to it. Observation and management of information do not imply semantic comprehension of all encapsulated domain content. Missing observation supplies neither a domain fact nor a certain operational outcome; [AX-15](../../motivation/principle/ef8abbaec37e4890ad78b9f263e67906.md) continues to govern operational uncertainty.
Harmonia may observe, carry, associate, apply, append, transform, persist, route, forward and respond to information according to explicitly established models, rules, Behaviours, Praxis and developer-defined logic without independently deriving the domain meaning of that information.
**Harmonia is not intrinsically an inferential agent.** Meaning acted upon is supplied through established models, explicit rules/behaviour, developer-defined processing or intentionally invoked services. The Harmonia Platform does not independently infer that meaning, nor intrinsically require comprehension of encapsulated business, clinical or other domain content.
This boundary does not remove Harmonia's own semantics. Harmonia necessarily understands the governed architectural semantics required to manage its own information and execution constructs, including authority, lifecycle, security, provenance and work/undertaking distinctions. Established semantic models, terminology rules and conformance responsibilities remain applicable; their existence does not make the Platform intrinsically comprehend every content item it carries.
For the [bounded Task model](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/task-work.md), an `ActionableTaskArchetype` can establish content expectations without specifying the content's structural representation or requiring domain comprehension. The domain content of `Task.Output(s)` contained / represented by `TaskOutcome` may remain semantically opaque while the governed ActionableTask resolution and its undertaking references remain explicit. The ActionableTask's `Outcome.OutputRules.Mode = Derived` applies explicitly defined rules to participating outputs without requiring Harmonia to infer their domain meaning. This information semantic prescribes no derivation implementation mechanism and does not make runtime AI intrinsic to Harmonia.

element.name: [CT3] Assurance Conclusion Determination
element.documentation:
Establish the legitimately supported conclusion, including insufficiency, qualification and unresolved concerns where applicable.
Assurance Conclusion Determination establishes what confidence is legitimately supported by the assessment. It preserves qualifications and unresolved concerns rather than forcing incomplete evidence into a positive or negative result. Within Assurance Evaluation it is the responsibility that gives the conclusion its standing, distinct from gathering or assessing the supporting material.
**Boundary**
Insufficiency proves neither assurance nor non-assurance, and the conclusion does not manage the subject's operational response.

element.name: Specimen Transport Process
element.documentation:
• Owning Capability: Clinical Logistics Coordination
• Process Purpose: Governs the physical courier chain-of-custody, transport, and delivery of pathology bio-specimens, blood products, and surgical biopsies.
• State Progression Lifecycle: Specimen Packaged → Courier Dispatched → Chain-of-Custody Signed → In-Transit (Monitored) → Lab Ingress Received → Specimen Accepted
• Key State Dispositions:
• Specimen Packaged: Clinical unit packages bio-sample with barcode manifest.
• Courier Dispatched: Courier route assigned for pickup.
• Chain-of-Custody Signed: Courier scans barcode and accepts legal custody.
• In-Transit (Monitored): Specimen in transit under temperature/time constraints.
• Lab Ingress Received: Central pathology specimen reception logs physical receipt.
• Specimen Accepted: Specimen integrity verified and passed to analytical track.
---
## History
### Process Overview — predecessor explanation
Specimen transport preserves the movement and custody account connecting collection context with laboratory receipt. It makes the journey of the material explainable rather than reducing it to a sent/received pair. Delivery remains distinct from specimen acceptance, diagnostic performance and the eventual professional interpretation of its evidence.

\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Logistics Coordination}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the physical courier chain-of-custody, transport, and delivery of pathology bio-specimens, blood products, and surgical biopsies.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Specimen Packaged → Courier Dispatched → Chain-of-Custody Signed → In-Transit (Monitored) → Lab Ingress Received → Specimen Accepted



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Packaged}}: Clinical unit packages bio-sample with barcode manifest.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Courier Dispatched}}: Courier route assigned for pickup.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Chain-of-Custody Signed}}: Courier scans barcode and accepts legal custody.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit (Monitored)}}: Specimen in transit under temperature/\allowbreak{}time constraints.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Lab Ingress Received}}: Central pathology specimen reception logs physical receipt.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Accepted}}: Specimen integrity verified and passed to analytical track.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

element.name: [CT1] Health Service Assurance
element.documentation:
Establish and maintain justified confidence that health services can be, and are being, delivered in accordance with applicable expectations, obligations, constraints and required levels of performance.
Health Service Assurance establishes justified confidence in the ability to deliver health services appropriately. Specification defines how confidence will be established; evaluation determines what the available evidence supports. Its subject is macro-level service delivery, with workforce, clinical, information, security and other concerns contributing evidence or criteria without becoming separate assurance trees.
Where independent governed assurance is required, the subject cannot control its own evaluation or conclusion. Independence concerns control of the assurance judgement rather than requiring a separate organisation or technology installation.
**Intent**
Distinguish justified confidence, qualified conclusions and insufficient evidence so that assurance communicates what is actually supported.
**Boundary**
Assurance manages its own evaluation and does not assign, remediate or progress the subject activity. Harmonia does not thereby assume responsibility for clinical adequacy or professional practice.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Approved independent governed assurance materially supports service confidence. The three established assurance BECs provide bounded support; they are not remapped to the newer BC descendants and are not assigned implementation components.
## Qualified relationship assertions
These source predicates retain their recorded standing and currentness. Their native mapping remains unestablished; they are not inferred ArchiMate edges. The complete original assertions and qualifications are retained in this element’s metadata.

element.name: [CT3] Care Appointment Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage a scheduled opportunity for care.
Care Appointment Management establishes a scheduled opportunity for care and maintains that opportunity as arrangements change. Within scheduling and capacity it supplies the temporal commitment around which participants can organise, while leaving the actual availability of places and resources distinguishable. A scheduled opportunity is useful coordination information even before attendance or care occurs.
**Boundary**
A booking does not establish attendance, intervention performance or satisfaction of diagnostic-service-specific scheduling constraints.

element.name: [CT2] Organisation Administration
element.documentation:
Organisation Administration maintains the identity, profiles, structural relationships and contact context of participating healthcare organisations. It enables a legal or operational entity to be distinguished from a department, network relationship or communication channel. This supports consistent interpretation of providers and destinations across information flows rather than allowing each interface to create an incompatible organisational account.
**Overview**
Organisation Administration maintains the identity, profiles, structural relationships and contact context of participating healthcare organisations. It enables a legal or operational entity to be distinguished from a department, network relationship or communication channel. This supports consistent interpretation of providers and destinations across information flows rather than allowing each interface to create an incompatible organisational account.
**Intent**
Organisation Administration maintains the identity, profiles, structural relationships and contact context of participating healthcare organisations. It enables a legal or operational entity to be distinguished from a department, network relationship or communication channel. This supports consistent interpretation of providers and destinations across information flows rather than allowing each interface to create an incompatible organisational account.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Representing organisational structure does not acquire corporate authority or ownership of every service offered by the organisation.

element.name: [CT2] Work Allocation & Dispatch
element.documentation:
Work Allocation & Dispatch progresses authorised operational work from a recognised requirement through matching, dispatch, acknowledgement and oversight. It distinguishes an instantiated work item from its assignment and from evidence of performance, allowing stalled activity to be identified and escalated. Examples such as cleaning or transport concern real-world support work, not technical message queues.
**Overview**
Work Allocation & Dispatch progresses authorised operational work from a recognised requirement through matching, dispatch, acknowledgement and oversight. It distinguishes an instantiated work item from its assignment and from evidence of performance, allowing stalled activity to be identified and escalated. Examples such as cleaning or transport concern real-world support work, not technical message queues.
**Intent**
Work Allocation & Dispatch progresses authorised operational work from a recognised requirement through matching, dispatch, acknowledgement and oversight. It distinguishes an instantiated work item from its assignment and from evidence of performance, allowing stalled activity to be identified and escalated. Examples such as cleaning or transport concern real-world support work, not technical message queues.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Intent — predecessor explanation
Make operational work progression accountable from requirement to reported outcome within applicable policy and role constraints.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
This assignment responsibility does not confer clinical work allocation, qualification or privilege. A technical receipt has only its interaction contract's meaning.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Governed operational work progression is a substantive platform responsibility supporting the Core classification.

element.name: [CT3] Care Intake Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage the intake context through which an individual seeks or enters care.
Care Intake Management establishes the access context through which a person seeks or enters care. It makes the entry circumstance manageable without assuming that every intake follows a referral or already satisfies eligibility conditions. Within Care Access Management, intake is the responsibility for entry context rather than a decision that all subsequent care arrangements are complete.
**Boundary**
An intake record does not establish acceptance of a referral, care responsibility or delivery of care.

element.name: [CT1] Governed Information Operations
element.documentation:

**Overview**
Entity integrity, context, lifecycle, information maintenance, discovery and semantic conformance are constituent reusable abilities; none is an implementation subsystem.
**Intent**

**Boundary**
Information management and semantic governance do not grant originating domain authority or erase active/durable state separation.

element.name: [CT3] Information Model Compliance
element.documentation:
Address organisational conformity to applicable information-model requirements.
Information Model Compliance addresses conformity to applicable model requirements. It makes actual organisational use accountable to the adopted semantic frame rather than treating model availability or user education as proof of conformity. Within standards governance it concerns the requirements for use, not the separate task of discovering or adopting models.
**Boundary**
Conformity does not redefine the model or absorb governance oversight of the wider adoption arrangements.

element.name: [CT2] Care Coordination & Transition
element.documentation:
Coordinate care participation, actual responsibility transition and discharge.
Care Coordination & Transition supports continuity by keeping participation, actual responsibility assumption and discharge progression distinct. Care teams may collaborate while responsibility is shared or changes, but physical transit and information exchange do not themselves establish who has accepted care. The capability therefore addresses continuity of accountable participation as well as the practical circumstances of departure.
**Intent**
Avoid gaps in care continuity caused by treating a movement or communication as an accepted responsibility transition.
**Boundary**
Harmonia may assemble handover information without managing clinical handover. Arrival, discharge readiness and physical departure are not equivalent to responsibility acceptance.

element.name: [CT3] Semantic Mapping Governance
element.documentation:
Govern mappings between applicable semantic artefacts without collapsing their source meanings or authorities.
Semantic Mapping Governance maintains mappings between applicable semantic artefacts while preserving the meaning and authority of each side. Its purpose is intelligible correspondence rather than assumed equivalence. A governed mapping can support exchange or interpretation without suggesting that the mapped artefacts have become the same concept or share one authority.
**Boundary**
A mapping does not erase source distinctions or give a consuming system authority to redefine either source.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Device Lifecycle Management
element.documentation:
Govern introduction, continued service, review, replacement, withdrawal, decommissioning and retirement within the overall device estate.
Clinical Device Lifecycle Management governs whether devices enter, remain in or leave the managed estate. Introduction, review, replacement, withdrawal and retirement concern the device's overall service disposition. This gives technology management a longer-lived responsibility than the device's current loan, release or data-exchange session.
**Boundary**
Lifecycle disposition differs from monitoring and restoring device condition; the maintenance-membership discrepancy remains unresolved.

element.name: [Topic] ReferralOutcome
element.documentation:
**Description** Information describing the outcome or resolution of a Referral, including the resulting disposition and relevant information returned to participants involved in the referral.
**Status: RESOLVED — APPROVED. G2-Q01 is resolved; G2 remains open.**
Referral Disposition is **not retained as an independent Information Concept**. The assurance and governance requirement previously represented by that B candidate is instead represented by **Referral Outcome**.
> **Referral Outcome is the governed information concerning what ultimately became of a Referral, sufficient to support assurance, governance and traceability over the Referral and its progression.**
**Semantic classification:** Outcome; provenance-bearing information with Assertion characteristics where a source reports what became of the Referral. This is not ServiceOutcome equivalence or a downstream representation category.
Referral Outcome exists principally to support the ability to account for Referrals within the applicable governance/assurance scope. Where established and appropriate, it may include the resulting outcome, basis/reason, source/originator, authority, temporal context and relationships to relevant resulting activity or information. No canonical Referral Outcome value set is established.
```text Referral ≠ Referral Progression Event ≠ Referral Outcome Referral Outcome ≠ Responsibility Assumption ≠ Transfer of Care ≠ HealthcareServiceDelivery ≠ ServiceOutcome Referral information semantics ≠ Referral Administration workflow progression ```
Referral Outcome may reference or relate to those Concepts where appropriate; its existence establishes none of them. Recording that a Referral was accepted, progressed or otherwise reached an outcome does not itself prove that care responsibility was actually assumed or transferred. G1 K1's intent/disposition/responsibility/Transfer of Care distinctions remain intact. Outcome is not equated with acceptance.
**Referral Progression Event:** Retained as historical information concerning significant occurrences in the administrative/business progression of a Referral. Not every Event represents a Referral Outcome, and the historical progression record is not collapsed into the final/current Outcome.
**Assurance / governance coverage — RF-IR5:** Harmonia must support assurance that Referrals within the applicable governance scope can be accounted for through sufficient progression and outcome information to establish what became of them. This requirement is applied to established Referral Administration / Manage Referral Progression / Referral Status & Outcome Service responsibility without allocating a new owner, Feature, Service or Collection.
```text Referral population within governance scope → progression/outcome evidence → assurance coverage ```
An inability to establish what became of a Referral is itself an assurance gap. No Referral Outcome is manufactured to make coverage appear complete. Where the outcome is not known, its absence is preserved explicitly.
**Workflow closure / finalisation:** This belongs to the progression of the Business Process / Referral Administration activity, not intrinsic Referral disposition information. The workflow may reach a state in which no further Referral Administration activity is required. This does not require a Referral Finalisation or Referral Closure Information Concept, a terminal state intrinsic to Referral, or Referral Outcome to double as workflow state. No workflow terminal states are defined and the Business Process state machine is not reproduced as the Information Concept lifecycle.
**Authority, temporal meaning and provenance:** Harmonia governs the outcome information for assurance and traceability; it does not infer substantive authority from recording or possessing it. Outcome may require provenance sufficient to establish what outcome was understood, source/originator, authority where relevant, when established/effective, and rationale/qualification where relevant. These are not all universally mandatory attributes. Detailed governance-scope criteria, evidence sufficiency, authority eligibility and contextual provenance/temporal qualification remain unestablished where existing architecture supplies no detail.
**Review history and consequence:** Q01 retains its original B question. The former Referral Disposition candidate proposed an independent Assertion for an attributable decision/reported disposition, with acceptance, decline, redirection and context-specific waitlisting examples. Architectural review rejects that separate Concept and reframes its assurance/governance purpose as Referral Outcome. Recipient-decision meanings and the canonical upstream Referral Disposition Log label are not erased. Q01 is resolved, without answering acceptance's clinical responsibility effects or the precise Referral–delivery/outcome relationships under Q05. Responsibility Assumption Assertion remains a non-authoritative D suggestion.
**Persistence boundary:** Only the Referral family, this review record and the necessary Referral navigation text are reconciled. Q02–Q07 and the complete G2-D01–D03 record remain unchanged. Frozen upstream architecture, Foundation, Package1 and initial historical report/diff are not modified. No other G2 question, G3, later Package2 family, FHIR mapping or downstream representation is commenced. G1 remains CLOSED; G2 is not CLOSED.
Source standing: Explicitly APPROVED G2-D04; no promotion of Referral family/package or independent Referral Disposition.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Rostering
element.documentation:
Clinical Rostering provides the Adjacent context of planned workforce availability. It is distinct from consuming roster projections for operational views or resolving who is currently on call. The present architecture retains the context without establishing a Harmonia Feature decomposition for authoring or managing the authoritative roster.
**Overview**
Clinical Rostering provides the Adjacent context of planned workforce availability. It is distinct from consuming roster projections for operational views or resolving who is currently on call. The present architecture retains the context without establishing a Harmonia Feature decomposition for authoring or managing the authoritative roster.
**Intent**
Clinical Rostering provides the Adjacent context of planned workforce availability. It is distinct from consuming roster projections for operational views or resolving who is currently on call. The present architecture retains the context without establishing a Harmonia Feature decomposition for authoring or managing the authoritative roster.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
A projected roster does not confer qualification, privilege, deployment or ownership of the originating schedule.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Roster information can inform operations while the formal Adjacent classification preserves its external management.

element.name: Petasos
element.documentation: - **Role/responsibility:** **Harmonia's durable message/event queue-management component**, a first-class shared messaging/event capability. Petasos manages creation, operation and operational state/status of its durable queues. [U09](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u09) extends the U05 handoff boundary, preserving AX-10. - **Purpose-defined queues:** purposes include inter-Ergon information flow, defined communication/event sharing, notification/event sharing and other architecturally established Harmonia event-sharing services. Queue purpose is architecturally defined; queues are not arbitrary generic queues. Final taxonomy, names, registration/configuration and topology remain unresolved. - **Features:** queue management and durable Parcel communication/event handling; persistent handoff obligations, bounded backlog, destination mechanics and handoff redelivery/recovery/dead-letter and designated replay responsibilities remain. Detailed delivery/ordering/duplicate/replay/recovery contracts are not newly selected; CDG-16/17/19/34/37/44 retain uncertainty. #### PetasosParcel and information ownership Every Petasos queue carries the single common datatype **PetasosParcel**. It represents the queued Harmonia communication/event and is conceptually analogous to **FHIR Communication**, without established literal equivalence. No schema or mapping to historical PetasosMessage/ErgonEvent is inferred. ```text PetasosParcel pass-by-value; the queued communication/event Referenced Information predominantly pass-by-reference; remains managed by its authoritative component ``` **PetasosParcel is passed by value.** Petasos does not transport only references and does not duplicate all associated information into the Parcel. Petasos owns Parcel messaging/event semantics and queue operations; references confer no ownership of the referenced information. For the **ActionableTask handoff special case**, ActionableTask/Pragma and payload remain managed through Mneme. A Parcel may reference that ActionableTask and is itself queued by value. Petasos does not transport another consumer's FulfillmentTask; each consumer undertaking the ActionableTask establishes its own distinct FulfillmentTask. The established no-payload-copy rule for this case does not make all Parcels reference-only. [Handoff view](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md#persistent-handoff). - **Persistence:** durable queues/Parcels and handoff recovery state are Petasos responsibility; referenced managed-information durable establishment remains Mnemosyne. Queue persistence mechanisms are not selected and queues do not become automatically permanent audit evidence. - **Operational observation:** Petasos owns queue operational state/status. Energeia may **observe/report** relevant state, without acquiring queue management or autonomous queue control. Detailed metrics/state structures remain unresolved. - **Themis collaboration:** for a governed FORWARD action, Petasos is the host/ enforcement location because it controls the queue operation. Applicable enforcement SHALL use **Themis-owned PEP capability** and relevant **PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context**. Themis owns authorisation/enforcement semantics; Petasos owns the operation. Detailed protocol remains unresolved. - **Other collaborations/exclusions:** serves Ergon, ingress, execution, publication, Agora and architecturally established communication/notification services. It is not subordinate to Ponos, ActionableTask-only, a reference transport helper or merely a generic enterprise broker abstraction. Mneme owns Publishing/Subscription/Pattern semantic selection; Ponos owns execution. - **Standing:** U09 resolves queue responsibility and common datatype/pass semantics; [CDG-44](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#petasos-detailed-contracts) retains schema, queue and interaction detail. Internal middleware remains Domain05; external protocols remain Domain06. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Persistent handoff without information ownership. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. > **Mneme determines semantic eligibility and eligible recipient/consumer > relationships under Publishing, Subscription and Pattern semantics. Petasos > establishes and manages the concrete persistent handoff obligation to the > destination and reliably effects that handoff. Ponos manages execution.** Eligible consumer relationships express semantic selection. They do not assign queue binding, destination mechanics or concrete handoff state to Mneme. Petasos is Harmonia's durable message/event queue-management component. It creates, operates and owns the operational state/status of **purpose-defined queues** for inter-Ergon flow and other architecturally established communication, notification and event sharing. Every queue carries **PetasosParcel by value**; associated information is predominantly by reference to governed information managed elsewhere. Parcel is conceptually analogous to FHIR Communication; literal equivalence and detailed schema are not established. For the ActionableTask handoff special case, governed ActionableTask/Pragma and Information Unit payload remain managed through Mneme. A by-value Parcel may carry references and communication/handoff metadata required for resolution and recovery. Petasos acquires no management authority over the referenced information and does not copy the managed ActionableTask payload in this pattern. ```text Mneme manages ActionableTask / Pragma and payload --> semantic selection / eligibility Petasos persistently manages handoff obligation --> queues PetasosParcel by value, referring to ActionableTask Consumer resolves governed information through Mneme --> establishes its own distinct FulfillmentTask undertaking Ponos manages execution / progression --> Ergon supplies bounded behaviour within Ergo's contract ``` **Petasos distributes the opportunity to undertake work, not another consumer's FulfillmentTask**, in this pattern. Each consumer undertaking the ActionableTask establishes a distinct FulfillmentTask; no undertaking is transported on its behalf. The Ergo framework works with **Mneme Context Load** to materialise anticipated values before **Context Loader** exposes them to business logic. **Context Unloader** returns changed working values and new Content as **Pragma Output** across that boundary; **Mneme Context Save** manages subsequent consequences. The Unloader is not persistence. Bounded Adhoc Resource Access/Search remains supported; Mnemosyne establishes/reports durable state. [U10/U11 lifecycle](49c9eb2bef0c47b8b5328621d5fc5479.md). Handoff acceptance, information commit, undertaking completion, work resolution and external acknowledgement remain distinct. ActionableTask handoff is one Petasos use case. Communication/Notification Events and other established event-sharing purposes use the common PetasosParcel datatype without becoming ActionableTasks or losing their own semantics. The no-payload-copy rule above SHALL NOT be generalised to reference-only Petasos transport or to copying all referenced information into every Parcel. Final purpose taxonomy, names, Parcel schema and detailed delivery contracts remain [CDG-44](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#petasos-detailed-contracts). Petasos owns queue operational state/status; Energeia may observe/report it, without acquiring queue management or autonomous control. For governed FORWARD, Petasos hosts enforcement because it controls the operation, using **Themis-owned PEP capability and relevant PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context**. Themis owns semantics; Petasos owns the queue operation. Detailed protocols/state metrics remain unresolved. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Distinct state and recovery responsibilities. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | State / concern | Responsibility and boundary | | :--- | :--- | | **Pragma / managed-information state** | Governed information managed through Mneme; authoritative durable establishment/preservation through Mnemosyne. May record a governed observation concerning delivery without owning the handoff obligation. | | **Petasos queue/handoff/delivery state** | Queue operational state/status and operational state of a particular persistent handoff obligation, including delivery attempt, redelivery/recovery and dead-letter handoff semantics. | | **FulfillmentTask undertaking state** | Information representing a particular identifiable undertaking, distinct from ActionableTask and other undertakings. Consumer establishment and Mneme Context/Pragma management do not collapse into runtime execution state. | | **Pylai Diadromí interaction state** | Transient and non-recoverable; loss terminates the interaction and appropriate client retry creates a new Diadromí. Controller keeps no recoverable state. Retained observations/evidence do not restore it or prove earlier effects did not occur. | | **Ponos execution/progression state** | Runtime execution, scheduling/concurrency, execution failure and execution retry/re-attempt or activity progression semantics. | | **Digital Twin input/Behaviour progression** | U19: at most one input at a time; interested Behaviours execute sequentially with the applicable sequence stable for that input. Sequence changes apply to subsequent inputs. ContinueBehaviourOnFailure contains failure to the current execution, leaving the Behaviour active and other interested Behaviours and queue processing unaffected. StopBehaviourOnFailure stops the failing Behaviour immediately, lets remaining interested Behaviours complete the current input, then halts the Twin. StopDigitalTwinOnFailure terminates the failing Behaviour and halts the Twin immediately, preventing remaining current-input and subsequent queued processing. Stopped Twins retain queued inputs pending governed administrative resume; generic retry/redelivery does not automatically resume them. Stopped-Behaviour recovery remains deferred. | Pragma “destination-specific delivery observations” means governed information recording observations concerning delivery. **Operational ownership of the delivery/handoff obligation remains with Petasos.** REC-002 destination granularity is preserved; the exact relationship among Petasos observations, Pragma/checkpoints, Task outputs and parent progression remains unresolved. No observation is silently treated as a completion or TaskOutcome algorithm. Ponos execution retry and Petasos handoff redelivery are different operations. Detailed acknowledgements, retry/recovery, duplicates, replay, ordering and continuation contracts remain unresolved. An uncertain previous effect remains uncertain under AX-15; technical failure alone proves neither success nor non-occurrence. No safe re-attempt algorithm is invented here. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Fan-out: established principle and retained detail. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. The supplied Publish/Subscribe DesignNote §§11–13/21 **partially adjudicates** the fan-out question: - A single Pragma may match multiple Subscriptions. The common managed Pragma and payload remain within Mneme; Petasos may manage multiple independent handoff obligations/queue entries carrying PetasosParcels by value, referring to it. Payload duplication is not inherently required. - For ActionableTask processing, each consumer that undertakes the work creates/morphs its **distinct FulfillmentTask**. Selection or handoff alone does not establish an undertaking. This preserves Domain04's [ActionableTask → FulfillmentTask [0..*] distinction](../data-object/topic/30f4deffcd694f07bf54b2b192695d4f.md). Semantic interest fan-out and execution concurrency are orthogonal. Multiple independent **Ergon types** interested in an ActionableTask each receive a separate FulfillmentTask. Separately, **ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency** may permit multiple instances of the **same Ergon type** to undertake it concurrently, each through its own FulfillmentTask. This does not change outcome participation or TaskOutcome ownership. Twin input interest matching analogously produces an identifiable **BehaviourStimulus / BehaviourEffector per interested Behaviour**, without establishing inheritance, identical information types or execution through ActionableTask/FulfillmentTask. Interested Behaviours execute sequentially within one Twin; concurrency is across independent Twins. Each loads its Praxis-defined Context fresh after the preceding Behaviour completes/saves. [U19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u19). **Detailed fan-out identity/lifecycle semantics remain unresolved:** reference, copy and version binding; exact morph/derivation mechanics; Pragma identity for undertaking representations; targetDestination and per-consumer processing state; concurrent processing and mutable-state isolation; lineage/causation; Journey correlation/reconstruction and assurance. No copy-per-subscriber or shared mutable processing-state model follows. Domain04 execution concurrency, outcome participation, output rules and TaskOutcome ownership remain unchanged. [CDG-37](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#pubsub-fanout) retains the remaining question. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F13 | Durable message/event queue creation, operation and status; persistent handoff/backlog/recovery | [Petasos C10](component-register.md#c10), first-class shared messaging/event capability for architecturally defined purposes | Every queue carries PetasosParcel by value; associated information predominantly by reference. ActionableTask Parcel references Mneme-managed work; each undertaking establishes its own FulfillmentTask | U05/U09, AX-10. Inter-Ergon, communication/notification and other established event sharing; no final taxonomy or broker topology. Petasos owns queue state; Energeia observes/reports. Governed FORWARD uses local Themis PEP/PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context. Detail CDG-16/19/34/37/44. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | F13 | Durable message/event queue creation, operation and status; persistent handoff/backlog/recovery | [Petasos C10](195e5f10db8e419391354197b5d7a8cc.md), first-class shared messaging/event capability for architecturally defined purposes | Every queue carries PetasosParcel by value; associated information predominantly by reference. ActionableTask Parcel references Mneme-managed work; each undertaking establishes its own FulfillmentTask | U05/U09, AX-10. Inter-Ergon, communication/notification and other established event sharing; no final taxonomy or broker topology. Petasos owns queue state; Energeia observes/reports. Governed FORWARD uses local Themis PEP/PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context. Detail CDG-16/19/34/37/44. | ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F14 | Designated deliberate replay | Petasos transition anchor and governed executing activity; Kleio evidence where policy requires | New linked processing attempt; original transition remains unchanged | L13 ADR-015. element.name: [CT3] Organisational Structure
element.documentation:
Managing parent-child hierarchies, departments, and corporate relationships.
**Overview**
Departments, divisions and regional networks need qualified structural relationships that can be traversed and understood over time. Structural membership is distinct from physical location and from authority to manage another organisation.
**Intent**
Make organisational relationships navigable without confusing structure with ownership or physical containment.
**Boundary**
Structural relationships do not acquire ownership of every related organisation or service.

element.documentation:
Administer qualified device-to-subject/place allocation, location, utilisation and operational readiness information, including the time at which an association applies.
**Overview**
Administer qualified device-to-subject/place allocation, location, utilisation and operational readiness information, including the time at which an association applies. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Administer qualified device-to-subject/place allocation, location, utilisation and operational readiness information, including the time at which an association applies.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: [Feature] Operational Credential Check
element.documentation:
Validate that a practitioner possesses active credentials and required competency certs prior to dispatching specialized work.
The qualification checkpoint considers active professional credentials and competency evidence before specialised dispatch. Its historical credential terminology does not make it the operational badge or physical-access responsibility of Credential Management, nor does a qualification check alone establish all required privilege.

element.name: Mneme
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** **Harmonia's Context and Pragma Manager**. Mneme manages the information context of activity through Pragma/Context, providing controlled, concurrent and seamless access to existing values and management of new Content. [U10](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u10) refines AX-05/11 active representation/coordination. - **Principal exposed services:** **Context Load, Context Save, Adhoc Resource Access, Adhoc Search** — four services. [Lifecycle](49c9eb2bef0c47b8b5328621d5fc5479.md) distinguishes Mneme materialisation/save from Ergo Loader/Unloader boundaries. Likely resource sets are non-exhaustive; bounded runtime acquisition is supported. - **Internal responsibilities:** Pragma Management C28 retains PragmaFactory and Publishing/Subscription/Pattern semantic eligibility/selection. Context management composes authoritative resource values into a versioned temporal snapshot; Resource Harmonisation Manager C40 manages exceptional delivery conditions. C11 supporting contracts do not add exposed services. - **Information:** Context D26 is the working value environment; Pragma C07 is the input/output envelope. Changed Context values and new Content expressed as Pragma Output D28 remain distinct. Mneme manages their subsequent consequences. - **Persistence:** active state is reconstructable; Mnemosyne alone establishes durable state and authoritatively reports persistence outcomes. Working changes, cache retention/replication and output production confer no durable authority. Context/resource versions and active generation remain distinct. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** Ergo framework anticipates/loads; Ergon primarily acts on Context values and may acquire Adhoc information. Resource harmonisation uses new governed Harmonisation Ergon work through common Ponos execution, not originating-Ergon conflict resolution. Adhoc Search uses Mnemosyne Search Management. Petasos retains handoff; Themis owns enforcement. Mneme is not a generic repository, execution framework, durable version authority or raw database/cache access path. - **Standing:** U10 adjudicates Context/Pragma responsibility; detailed representation, concurrency/access/Output and harmonisation contracts remain CDG-45/46; older cache/write-behind and access variants remain CDG-10/11/16/27/31.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Mneme — Context and Pragma Manager. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
> **Mneme manages the information context of Harmonia activity — principally > through Pragma and Context — providing controlled, concurrent and seamless > access to existing resource values and management of the new Content produced > by that activity.**
Mneme is Harmonia's **Context and Pragma Manager**. Distributed active representation, observation, coordination, reconstruction and convergence support this responsibility under AX-05/11; they do not make Mneme a generic repository or persistence authority. Pragma Management retains its adjudicated PragmaFactory and Publishing/Subscription/Pattern responsibilities. Semantic selection remains distinct from Petasos handoff and Ponos execution.
Mneme exposes **four principal services**:
| Exposed service | Architectural meaning | | :--- | :--- | | **Context Load** | Materialise a managed Context from authoritative resource values for anticipated activity requirements. | | **Context Save** | Return resulting Context state to Mneme management for appropriate subsequent information handling, alongside distinguishable Pragma Outputs. | | **Adhoc Resource Access** | Governed runtime acquisition of resource information outside the anticipated loaded Context where the bounded activity requires it. | | **Adhoc Search** | Activity/context-facing governed search, using Mnemosyne's underlying authoritative persistence Search Management. |
Resource Harmonisation Manager is an **internal responsibility**, not a fifth exposed service. Historical read/write facades and supporting contracts are not additional principal services; their detailed relationship to this surface remains unresolved. No additional exposed Mneme services are established here.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Retained uncertainty and existing adjudications. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
[CDG-45–48](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#context-and-pragma-contracts) retain the new detailed gaps: Context and access representation/concurrency, exceptional harmonisation, persistence oversight/compartments/outcome contracts, and Search/Research Metadata. Transaction boundaries, rollback/retry, shard routing/topology/replication, service-health metrics, semantic compartment-applicability source, compartment representation/validation, PEP interaction and logging schemas remain unresolved.
Kleio essential capture/immutable history and cross-target harmonisation SEP, Themis distributed enforcement/default-deny, Petasos queues/Parcel/handoff, Energeia Praxis/Journey ownership, DigitalTwin/Dokimasia specialisations and terminal rules, and Pathway/control/observed-evidence distinctions are preserved. Kleio's [mandatory capture authority](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#kleio-capture-authority) is intrinsic platform authority governed by Harmonia policy under AX-07. The audited Identity is evidence, not capture authority. Insufficient capture authority fails the governed operation closed; Mneme/Mnemosyne gain no equivalent authority. Those A2/A3 corrections did not themselves establish A4 acceptance. Current A4 acceptance and the bounded B1 scope are recorded in the [orientation](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/README.md).
## Source-qualified contribution

Context Load preferred/performance-optimised; bounded runtime acquisition permitted, potentially more expensive. No fifth service or exhaustive preload; detail CDG-45. |``. element.name: [CT3] Clinical Quality Evidence Management
element.documentation:
Manage the body of applicable evidence used for clinical-quality consideration without owning its originating activity.
Clinical Quality Evidence Management maintains the body of material applicable to quality consideration. Its purpose is to retain evidence in a form and context that can support review without treating availability as proof of quality. The originating activity and its authority remain distinguishable from the later quality purpose for which its information is used.
**Boundary**
Evidentiary use transfers neither source ownership nor authority to determine the activity being reviewed.

element.name: [CT3] Assurance Evidence Assessment
element.documentation:
Evaluate available evidence against the established assurance approach and criteria.
Assurance Evidence Assessment evaluates available evidence against the established approach and criteria. It produces the assessed basis from which a legitimate conclusion may be determined, retaining qualifications and evidentiary limits. The responsibility is evaluative rather than the operational production of the source information or remediation of what it reveals.
**Boundary**
Assessment is distinct from conclusion determination; unavailable or insufficient evidence must remain explicit.

element.name: [CT3] Assurance Criteria Administration
element.documentation:
The capability to establish and manage reusable, governed and temporally identifiable assurance criteria through which subjects may be evaluated.
Definition — reviewed candidate
Administer reusable governed assurance criteria and their version-specific and temporal applicability without changing governing requirement authority.
**Overview**
Administer reusable governed assurance criteria and their version-specific and temporal applicability without changing governing requirement authority.
**Intent**
Administer reusable governed assurance criteria and their version-specific and temporal applicability without changing governing requirement authority.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Assurance Criteria Management maintains reusable evaluative criteria with governed standing and temporal applicability. Version and effective context matter because a conclusion must be understood against the criteria applicable to the subject and time being assessed. Criteria may operationalise governing requirements, but their management is not authority to change those requirements.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Modelling criteria does not inherently approve them. Detailed criterion states and approval workflows remain unresolved, and criteria need not all originate in formal Governance.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Formal relevance remains Unresolved. Established assurance support explains the enabling purpose without classifying it by inference or allocating software responsibility.

element.name: [Feature] Confidentiality Flag Enforcement
element.documentation:
Enforce restricted access flags (e.g., VIP, sensitive diagnosis, restricted record) across query and presentation interfaces.
Confidentiality enforcement makes a restricted-record condition effective across discovery and presentation paths. Its purpose is consistent governed treatment of sensitive information, rather than a flag displayed in one interface while other paths disclose the same content without restriction.

element.name: Healthcare Directory Stewards & Registrars
element.documentation:
### Profile & Role Healthcare Directory Stewards and Registrars are the specialized operational custodians responsible for maintaining authoritative regional registries of healthcare providers, individual clinicians, clinical organizations, and electronic service delivery endpoints.
### Core Responsibilities - Curating authoritative master directories of healthcare practitioners, qualifications, active credentials, and organizational affiliations. - Verifying and maintaining electronic service delivery endpoints (secure messaging addresses, FHIR endpoints, MLLP port mappings). - Managing provider registry updates, deprecations, practitioner relocations, and retirement events.
### Principal Architectural Concerns - **Secure Endpoint Governance**: Ensuring clinical messages and notifications are routed exclusively to authenticated, currently authorized practitioner endpoints. - **Accurate Practitioner Role Representation**: Distinguishing between an individual clinician, their legal practitioner role, their accredited specialty, and their specific institutional practice location. - **Reliable Directory Change Propagation**: Ensuring directory updates (e.g., changes in clinic address or revocation of practitioner credentials) propagate through integration workflows rapidly and deterministically.

element.name: [Feature] Directory Contact Management
element.documentation:
Manage verified phone, email, and administrative contact channels for healthcare facilities.
Contact management provides verified administrative and clinical communication channels for organisations. It supports reaching the appropriate participant while distinguishing a directory contact from the role-specific destination and authority relevant to a particular clinical exchange.

element.name: [Topic] TaskDefinition
element.documentation:
**Description** Information defining a reusable form of actionable work, including the characteristics, expectations and constraints applicable when instances of that work are created.
**ActionableTaskArchetype** is the reusable definition/archetype for a kind of actionable work. It describes the meaning and constraints of work that may subsequently be instantiated. It SHALL NOT be treated as an instance of work.
Its semantics may include, where applicable:
- the expected nature of the work; - permissible parameters and constraints; - prerequisites and performer requirements; - completion or satisfaction expectations; and - expectations concerning information/content consumed, manipulated or produced by the work.
An archetype may establish expectations concerning encapsulated content without defining that content's structural representation or requiring Harmonia to comprehend its domain semantics. The [observable-information boundary](../../../business/business-object/10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) applies.

element.name: [CT3] Classification Utilisation Oversight
element.documentation:
Oversee appropriate organisational application of classifications.
Classification Utilisation Oversight evaluates appropriate organisational application of classifications. It addresses whether information is treated consistently with the governed sensitivity meaning, rather than assuming that an established classification scheme guarantees correct use. This retains a distinct responsibility for practice alongside definition governance.
**Boundary**
Oversight neither creates classification definitions nor establishes a new localisation peer.

element.name: Statutory Health Information Privacy & Protection
element.documentation:
### Context & Pressure Health records contain the most sensitive category of personal data recognized under law (medical histories, psychiatric evaluations, sexual health diagnoses, genetic profiles). Healthcare networks are subject to rigorous statutory privacy regimes (e.g., the Australian *Privacy Act 1988*, My Health Records Act, HIPAA, GDPR).
Statutory authorities enforce severe civil penalties, mandatory breach reporting, and reputational sanctions for unauthorized disclosure, eavesdropping, or accidental data leakage.
### Architectural Imperative Harmonia must implement intrinsic, default-deny security and privacy controls across all operations. Sensitive Protected Health Information (PHI) must never be emitted into non-clinical logging streams, telemetry systems, or debug channels. Access must require explicit cryptographic authentication and fine-grained authorization.
- **Primary Stakeholders**: [Patients & Care Recipients](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md), [Platform Operations & Integration Engineers](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md) - **External Constraint**: [Applicable Health-Information Privacy and Data-Protection Obligations](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/external-constraints.md) - **Key Assessments**: [Implicit Perimeter Trust](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md), [PHI Leakage through Operational Logging](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md) - **Governing Axioms**: [AX-07 (Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations)](../principle/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md), [AX-08 (Evidence Records Meaning)](../principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md)

element.documentation:
Instantiate, dispatch, supervise and progress authorised operational undertakings with explicit outcome standing.
**Overview**
Reusable execution control respects work-unit archetype, participation and uncertain effects rather than equating dispatch with completion.
**Intent**
Progress accountable operational work without equating dispatch, execution and successful outcome.
**Boundary**
Does not own underlying clinical-work meaning, clinical decisions or originator business authority.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Quality Criteria Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage measures, indicators, expectations and criteria against which clinical quality is considered.
Clinical Quality Criteria Management establishes the measures, indicators and expectations used to consider clinical quality. It makes the basis of a later judgement explicit so that evidence can be assessed against an identifiable expectation rather than an unstated standard. Criteria are distinct from the measurements or findings produced when they are applied.
**Boundary**
Managing criteria does not originate the underlying evidence or establish a quality conclusion.

element.name: [CT3] Communications & Publicity
element.documentation:
Manage organisational communication/publication arrangements relevant to information availability/distribution.
Communications & Publicity manages organisational publication and communication arrangements relevant to information availability and distribution. It provides enterprise communication context without being identical to clinical record exchange or digitally mediated participant interaction. The governed decomposition retains that broad support role without adding specific publicity or communications functions.
**Boundary**
Organisational communication does not originate the clinical facts or governed conclusions it may convey.

element.name: [CT1] Health Service Governance
element.documentation:
Establish and maintain the obligations, authorities, constraints, policies and governance framework under which health-service activity must operate, and define how adherence will be assessed, checked and reported.
Health Service Governance establishes the normative envelope within which health-service activity operates: what obligations apply, who may decide, what constraints bind decisions and how adherence will be assessed and reported. Its framework and compliance branches distinguish the authoritative requirements from the arrangements used to judge satisfaction. Governance therefore shapes legitimate activity without becoming the manager of every governed operation.
**Intent**
Make obligations, decision authority and compliance expectations explicit and traceable.
**Boundary**
Operational management chooses and progresses means within the governing envelope; assurance evaluates evidence. Neither responsibility is absorbed merely because governance defines its constraints.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Formal relevance remains Unresolved. The requirements plainly constrain managed activity, but the RAD has not assigned enough platform participation or enabling derivation to adjudicate its relevance classification.

element.name: [CT2] Outpatient Operations
element.documentation:
Outpatient Operations integrates arrival events and follow-up requirements generated as clinics progress. It connects a person's operational presence with the relevant service context and makes post-clinic booking or diagnostic needs available for subsequent activity. The responsibility retains outpatient-specific capacity semantics without requiring a separate arrival Function where approved reusable composition suffices.
**Overview**
Outpatient Operations integrates arrival events and follow-up requirements generated as clinics progress. It connects a person's operational presence with the relevant service context and makes post-clinic booking or diagnostic needs available for subsequent activity. The responsibility retains outpatient-specific capacity semantics without requiring a separate arrival Function where approved reusable composition suffices.
**Intent**
Outpatient Operations integrates arrival events and follow-up requirements generated as clinics progress. It connects a person's operational presence with the relevant service context and makes post-clinic booking or diagnostic needs available for subsequent activity. The responsibility retains outpatient-specific capacity semantics without requiring a separate arrival Function where approved reusable composition suffices.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
An arrival does not establish consultation completion, and a captured follow-up requirement does not perform the clinical activity.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Arrival and clinic-outcome information materially connect outpatient progression to care coordination.

element.name: [Feature] Controlled Administrative Recovery
element.documentation:
Perform authorised recovery as identifiable governed activity through normal execution and evidence boundaries.
**Overview**
Operators may need to resume, reconcile or repair an operational concern. That is first-class work with permission and outcome standing, rather than direct mutation through a console.
**Boundary**
Administrative interaction grants no raw cache/database or subsystem-internal bypass.

element.name: AX-08 Evidence Records Meaning, Not Machinery
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
Provenance and audit evidence SHALL describe information-significant, security-significant and business-significant events, assertions and decisions.
Internal implementation mechanics SHALL NOT ordinarily become provenance or audit evidence merely because they occurred.
#### Rationale
A durable evidence repository should explain what happened to information and why, rather than become a permanent distributed debug log.
#### Consequences
Authoritative state acceptance, significant information transformations, stewardship decisions and security-significant actions MAY require durable evidence.
Cache misses, cache rebalancing, CAS retries, connection retries, reconstruction and ordinary infrastructure mechanics normally belong in logging, metrics or transient diagnostics.
Kleio preserves durable evidence.
#### Maxim
Preserve the meaningful fact, not every mechanism that produced it.

element.name: [CT2] Credential Management
element.documentation:
Administer definitions of clinical-service credentials and their required applicability without granting professional privilege or managing physical badges.
**Overview**
Administer definitions of clinical-service credentials and their required applicability without granting professional privilege or managing physical badges. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Administer definitions of clinical-service credentials and their required applicability without granting professional privilege or managing physical badges.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: Coordinated Progression of Operational Activities and Associated Entity State
element.documentation:
### Goal Statement Harmonia shall coordinate multi-stage operational activities through explicit, observable state transitions that remain strictly synchronized with the governed state of the associated real-world clinical entity.
### Rationale & Context Healthcare integration activities (such as ADT distribution, lab order dispatch, and multi-destination fan-out) involve multi-stage distributed operations. Treating integration simply as a stream of fire-and-forget message transfers causes destination divergence and unmonitored failures (as diagnosed in [Unmonitored Destination Failure](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md)).
### Architectural Boundary & Intent - **Beyond Conventional Workflow Engines**: Avoid language implying that Harmonia is merely a generic workflow engine. Harmonia does not simply execute arbitrary BPMN scripts; it coordinates distributed integration activities in lockstep with the real-world lifecycle of clinical entities (e.g., patient admission state, lab specimen lifecycle, encounter status). - Requires explicit, observable progression state across multi-stage activities ([`REQ-FND-002`](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/requirements-constraints/foundational-requirements.md)). - Governed by [AX-16 (Operational Activity & Entity State Progress Together)](../principle/de7e90f46127455a9ec9ad3b9b48ba54.md).

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Device Feature & Release Management
element.documentation:
Manage functional/release state, including applicable software, firmware, configuration and enabled device characteristics.
This capability governs the functional state of a device, including applicable software, firmware, configuration and enabled characteristics. Two instances of the same model may therefore have materially different capabilities in service. The responsibility makes those differences intelligible without reducing device governance to physical inventory or location.
**Boundary**
Release state is distinct from maintenance condition, deployment and professional authority to use the device.

element.name: [CT3] Location Structure
element.documentation:
Modeling the physical architecture of healthcare campuses.
**Overview**
Campus, building, floor, ward and room relationships explain physical containment. The structure provides navigation and context without determining organisational reporting lines or current operational capacity.
**Intent**
Allow a particular place to be interpreted within its physical surroundings.
**Boundary**
Physical containment differs from organisational structure and operational responsibility.

element.name: [CT2] Emergency Department Operations
element.documentation:
This capability maintains the operational context of emergency places, waits and length-of-stay milestones. It supports understanding of occupancy and impediments in the department while keeping capacity's emergency-service meaning intact. Its concern differs from Emergency Care's clinical presentation context, even though both can refer to the same patient encounter.
