element.name: Calliope
element.documentation: - **Role/responsibility:** management/governance of foundational models, definitions and mutable datasets, including first-class Security and Assurance Nomenclature and authoritative review of ontology sets for Harmonia use. [U13](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u13), [canonical Calliope view](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md). - **Distinct submodules:** **Calliope-Models C41** supplies design/build-time Models, Metadata Types, Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types, Filter Elements, core Harmonia element libraries and security/assurance definitions. **Calliope-DataSets C42** manages runtime mutable ValueSets, CodeSets, Structured Metadata and applicable governed ontology content. No common lifecycle or undifferentiated metadata repository is inferred. - **Authority:** development representations support type-safe human/IDE/AI-assisted programming; current membership/content uses runtime authority. Models/build definitions establish structural access contracts; DataSets do not bootstrap them. Definition ownership confers neither runtime execution nor originating clinical authority. - **Persistence/collaboration:** DataSets uses established Mneme/Mnemosyne responsibilities; Calliope is not a Persistence Manager. Governed workflow may reuse Ponos/Ergo/Praxis, without another engine or detailed management UI. Themis decides/enforces, Dokimasia assures and Kleio audits. - **Standing:** U13 settles the two responsibilities, not their packaging, runtime ontology boundary or representation/workflow mechanisms (CDG-24/49). Existing pure-library dependency constraints apply to Models; U15 resolves the [realisation boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md#calliope-realisation). General converter-support versus activity allocation remains CDG-05; no terminology product is selected. #### Controlled authorisation nomenclature [U12](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u12) establishes these **release-bounded ValueSets**: | ValueSet | Architectural shorthand / meaning | | :--- | :--- | | `Application.Function.AuthorisationPoint.Names` | **Function.Name**: architecturally significant application AuthorisationPoints at which enforcement is meaningful. An AuthorisationPoint identifies a governed function; it is not itself a permission. | | `Application.Function.AllowedAction.Names` | **Function.Scope**: the bounded set of actions applicable at AuthorisationPoints. Existing concepts include **ACCESS**, **CHANGE** and **FORWARD**; these are not asserted to be the complete final ValueSet. | | `Information.Compartments` | Governed information compartments; an applicable dimension is expressed as **Information.Compartment**. | | `Information.Classification` | Governed information classifications. | `Application.Function.AuthorisationPoint.Names` SHALL be comprehensive enough to satisfy business security requirements for the release while constrained enough to avoid unnecessary management, development and support burden. Complete release-specific contents remain [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#identity-deferred-design). **Calliope defines/governs the nomenclature. Themis owns policy association, resolution and enforcement.** ValueSet membership alone grants no authority and does not establish every Cartesian combination as meaningful or permitted. The controlled vocabularies fall within [Calliope-DataSets](466ad8f75a954c0581b5bba090443849.md); their structural definitions/contracts belong to Calliope-Models. This allocation does not reopen U12 or permit unrestricted runtime changes to release-bounded content; detailed release/change rules remain deferred. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Calliope and Pylai use of established responsibilities. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. [Calliope-DataSets](53bf6815c7a54ed0abde9b1aad311843.md) owns governed mutable content and uses established Mneme/Mnemosyne access/persistence; this adds no persistence manager or Mneme service. Models/build definitions supply structural contracts independently of runtime DataSet availability. [PylaiServer READ/SEARCH](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-server-controller) uses Diadromí-Controller → Mneme Adhoc Resource Access / Adhoc Search → Mnemosyne as needed. Mneme remains the Context and Pragma Manager with four exposed services, not a generic Information Manager or external interoperability service. No ActionableTask/Praxis/Ergon is fabricated for this read-oriented pattern. [PylaiPathway ingress](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-pathway-ingress) establishes initial Task.input/Context through a specialised Ergo ContextLoader; semantic mapping remains in BusinessLogic. EgressHoros returns communication state/outcome before ContextUnloader completes. Neither Loader/Unloader nor Pylai establishes durable truth. Protocol success, engine success and authoritative Harmonia persistence outcome remain distinct, including uncertainty. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md` — ## Responsibility and decomposition. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. Calliope manages and governs Harmonia's foundational Models, Metadata Types, Criteria Definitions, Topics, Filter Types, Filter Elements, ValueSets, CodeSets, Structured Metadata, core Harmonia element libraries, and Security and Assurance Nomenclature. It also owns authoritative review/governance of ontology sets for Harmonia use. That review does not make Harmonia the originating authority for externally governed ontologies. The B1 conceptual [`Metabolē.Context.ActivityContext` vocabulary](../../business/business-object/c34b4929f71946708d37dbe6c1da920a.md) is governed consistently with this shared definition/model/nomenclature responsibility. It classifies the broad activity, separately from a request action or authorisation permission. The initial examples are not an exhaustive enum; this establishes no physical Models/DataSets allocation. Runtime policy resolution, authorisation decisions and enforcement remain Themis responsibilities. ```text Calliope +-- Calliope-Models design/build-time governed knowledge `-- Calliope-DataSets runtime management of mutable governed content ``` These are distinct logical submodules with different lifecycles and dependency characteristics. They SHALL NOT be collapsed into one undifferentiated metadata repository. Their names establish no Maven artefacts, processes, databases or deployment boundaries. The [realisation boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md#calliope-realisation) separates Models' library dependencies from DataSets' runtime collaboration. ### Library dependency and runtime management > **Calliope-Models provides development/build-time library dependencies. > Calliope-DataSets provides runtime management and authoritative access to > mutable governed datasets.** The existence of DataSets does not alter Models' library/dependency semantics and does not make Calliope a persistence manager. Repository pure-library and zero-higher-layer-dependency constraints apply to Models; they do not restrict all logical Calliope responsibilities to libraries. DataSets collaborates through established Mneme/Mnemosyne access and persistence. No new static dependency or physical allocation is inferred from that runtime collaboration. ```text Calliope +-- Calliope-Models | design / code / build-time model and library dependency `-- Calliope-DataSets runtime governed dataset management / authoritative content access ↓ Mneme / Mnemosyne access and persistence Concept / structural contract → Calliope-Models Current governed membership/content → Calliope-DataSets ``` > **Build-time representation and runtime authority are complementary, not > competing, responsibilities.** Strategy's library/local-evaluation statements concern Models. Calliope is not a mandatory mediator of every runtime transaction; current governed content may require DataSets runtime resolution. Packaging, APIs and other mechanisms remain [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#calliope-contracts). ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md` — ## Build-time knowledge and runtime authority. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. > **Build-time Calliope knowledge assists software development; runtime Calliope > authority determines validity and current governed membership/content.** Calliope SHALL provide development-time representations of known runtime-managed DataSets, CodeSets and ValueSets sufficient for efficient human, IDE-assisted and AI-assisted software development. Such representations can support type safety, code completion, documentation, static analysis and testing, with stable identity, meaning, constraints, known build-time values and runtime-resolution contracts. > **Development-time knowledge SHALL NOT be treated as authoritative evidence of > current runtime membership or content.** > **Development-time representation SHALL NOT require developers to sacrifice > normal type-safe/code-assisted programming merely because a dataset is runtime > mutable.** A runtime value is not invalid merely because an earlier build did not know it. Conversely, earlier software need not contain value-specific business behaviour for later additions. Validation/membership uses current governed runtime authority; the generated-code, IDE, AI-tooling and runtime access mechanisms remain deferred. Structural contracts for accessing/managing DataSets SHALL derive from Calliope-Models and the software build/deployment lifecycle. Runtime DataSets provide mutable content under those contracts; they SHALL NOT bootstrap the structural contracts required for their own access. This separates foundational software dependency from runtime collaboration with Mneme, Mnemosyne and Ponos. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md` — ## Security and Assurance Nomenclature. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. Calliope has first-class responsibility for the definition, governance and authoritative representation of shared security, privacy, policy, audit and assurance nomenclature. This is broader than incidental storage of security ValueSets. ```text Calliope defines / governs nomenclature Themis decides / enforces Dokimasia assures Kleio audits ``` | Calliope-Models illustrative definitions | Calliope-DataSets illustrative governed content | | :--- | :--- | | SecurityClassificationType | SecurityClassification ValueSet | | CompartmentMetadataType | Compartment CodeSet / ValueSet | | AssuranceFindingType | AssuranceFindingCategory ValueSet | | CriteriaDefinition / DecisionReasonType | DisclosurePurpose CodeSet / AssuranceSeverity ValueSet | Examples do not establish a final catalogue, schema or release inventory. The four [U12 release-bounded authorisation ValueSets](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-nomenclature) are Calliope-controlled vocabularies: - `Application.Function.AuthorisationPoint.Names`; - `Application.Function.AllowedAction.Names`; - `Information.Compartments`; - `Information.Classification`. Their controlled content belongs to the DataSets responsibility, while their structural definitions/contracts belong to Models. Release-bounded scope does not establish unrestricted runtime mutation of these particular ValueSets; release-specific contents and detailed change/version rules remain deferred. Themis owns their authorisation-policy association, role/Criteria resolution and enforcement. Membership alone grants no authority. U12's Criterion conjunction, additive UNION grants, temporal/revocation and local PEP semantics remain intact. Calliope does not acquire policy decisions, assurance assessment or Audit Capture. Kleio's [mandatory capture authority](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#kleio-capture-authority) is governed intrinsic platform authority, separate from the originating Identity's authorisation and from nomenclature ownership. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md` — ## Deferred design and review boundary. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. The exact runtime ontology-management boundary, originating terminology-authority relationships, ontology-review/update/synchronisation lifecycle, DataSet lifecycle, version/effective-date and historical retention rules remain unresolved. So do the relationship of historical Context to later DataSet versions, detailed DataSet workflow, human-management UI, exact development representations/tooling, runtime APIs, physical packaging, caching, persistence structures and final security/assurance catalogue. Complete release-specific ValueSet contents remain deferred under U12. [CDG-24/49](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#calliope-contracts) distinguishes the now-established runtime management responsibility from these open details and from proposed clinical terminology/authoring services. Domain03 clinical-knowledge behaviour is not automatically allocated wholesale to Calliope. No Domain04 Information Family or capability coverage is inferred by this consolidation. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F02 | Canonical conversion support and interface-specific semantic processing | Calliope reusable support; PylaiPathway Terma-paired developer Ergo.BusinessLogic interprets/maps/transforms Communication Information into Task.output | Raw communication in Task.input; native resources and applicable outputs | U14 settles ingress Loader versus BusinessLogic separation. General converter/activity allocation remains CDG-05; no selected implementation library/route. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | F02 | Canonical conversion support and interface-specific semantic processing | Calliope reusable support; PylaiPathway Terma-paired developer Ergo.BusinessLogic interprets/maps/transforms Communication Information into Task.output | Raw communication in Task.input; native resources and applicable outputs | U14 settles ingress Loader versus BusinessLogic separation. General converter/activity allocation remains CDG-05; no selected implementation library/route. | ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F46 | Shared Security and Assurance Nomenclature | Calliope-Models definitions; Calliope-DataSets controlled content; Themis decides/enforces, Dokimasia assures, Kleio audits | Includes U12 four release-bounded authorisation ValueSets; policy associations/grants remain Themis-owned | U12/U13. Complete release contents and detailed change/version rules deferred. Definition ownership is not operational ownership. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | F46 | Shared Security and Assurance Nomenclature | Calliope-Models definitions; Calliope-DataSets controlled content; Themis decides/enforces, Dokimasia assures, Kleio audits | Includes U12 four release-bounded authorisation ValueSets; policy associations/grants remain Themis-owned | U12/U13. Complete release contents and detailed change/version rules deferred. element.name: [CT3] Healthcare Organisation Identity & Structure Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage identity and structural relationships of participating organisations and organisational units.
This capability establishes the identity and structural relationships of participating organisations and organisational units. It provides the business account of who the participants are and how they relate, which directory representations can then convey. The distinction matters because a represented hierarchy should not create organisational authority merely through document or interface nesting.
**Boundary**
Organisation identity does not substitute for location, practitioner or material Healthcare Service context.

element.name: [Feature] Operating Schedule Specification
element.documentation:
Define temporal availability, clinic operating hours, and on-call service windows.
Operating schedules make temporal availability and exceptions explicit for a service. They distinguish an existing offering from one available at the relevant time, while leaving actual resource readiness and operational capacity as separate concerns.

element.documentation:

element.name: [Feature] Encounter Bed/Location Association
element.documentation:
Dynamically maintain the association between an encounter, care team, and physical bed or ward location.
Encounter association keeps the relevant place and care-team context aligned with the episode as the patient moves. Location changes are meaningful operational facts, but they do not themselves establish a transfer of clinical responsibility.

element.name: Omilia Application Services API
element.documentation:
Omilia.Server exposes an **Application Services API** used by Agora both to request collaboration operations and to receive managed-Room dialogue/activity.
```mermaid flowchart LR Agora["Harmonia.Agora: collaboration control"] -->|"Application Services API: operation requests"| Server["Harmonia.Omilia.Server: collaboration operations"] Server -->|"Application Services API: managed-Room dialogue / activity"| Agora Client["Harmonia.Omilia.Client: collaboration experience"] <-->|"Matrix protocol"| Server ```
Agora decides to create/change a managed Room/Space, add/remove a participant or publish information; Omilia.Server performs the operation. Room activity returns through the same architectural boundary. The exact API contract, technology and mapping to upstream Matrix interfaces remain deferred. Historical Admin, Client-Server and AS-transaction endpoints do not define this new contract.
Workflow/execution collaboration continues through Petasos with **no direct Agora-to-Ponos dependency**. Matrix DTO encapsulation, Themis default-deny governance and zero-PHI Room aliases/names/topics remain repository constraints. Membership or receipt of a notification does not confer information-access rights.
[U19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u19) establishes the administrative interaction boundary: Administrator → Omilia → Agora → Administrative Function → specialised Administrative Ergon → governed subsystem operation. Stopped-Twin resumption uses this pattern, with normal authorisation, Context, execution and Kleio audit controls; Agora and Omilia do not directly resume or manipulate the Twin. The arrows describe semantic progression and retain Petasos execution handoff and Agora's no-direct-Ponos-dependency rule. Iris provides a separate path through Iris-BackEnd and does **not** directly interact with Agora or Omilia. Broader Administrative Function reconciliation is [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#administrative-function-finding).
Identity mapping/provisioning is collaboration integration, not authentication authority. Existing isolation constraints are not relaxed; detailed security, privacy and external/federated interactions remain deferred.

element.name: Ergon
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** a single well-defined software component encapsulating a bounded fine-grained task-completion activity set within the Ergo contract, executed/managed through Ponos. [U01/U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02), [L03/L19](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#l03). - **Features:** specialised transformation/mapping, validation, identifier/reference checking, enrichment, routing, result processing, fan-out or registry-change behaviour. Reuses C05 common facilities; `ErgonBase` is historical contract support, not an architectural inheritance requirement. - **Information:** acts upon or generates Pragma, payload/resource information, outputs, checkpoints and observations through governed contracts. It primarily acts on loaded Context values, may change working values and may generate new Content as **Pragma Output**, distinct from Context mutation. Bounded **Adhoc Resource Access / Adhoc Search** remains permitted for emerging needs. **No discrete Information Architecture representation or Ergon Information Resource exists merely because the component is an Ergon.** Activity is not information about it. - **Output progression:** one or more execution outputs may yield multiple Pragma. The [Pathway-continuation role](../data-object/27ad143e7c784e378556af8a57c438f7.md) identifies information continuing the current Praxis; independently resulting Pragma remain available for governed use, without automatically advancing it. - **Persistence/collaboration:** requests governed information use/change through Mneme; does not own Pragma management or durable state. Erga collects components; Ponos executes them; Petasos effects persistent handoff. Every Ergon exposes IngressEndpoint and EgressEndpoint C29; traversal does not expose internal logic. Praxis relationship detail remains open. The originating Ergon owns no persistence mechanics, shard/database transactions or generic conflict resolution; exceptional harmonisation is new governed work under U10. - **Specialisations:** Behaviour C25, Dokimasia Ergon C26 and, through the latter, AI Assurance Ergon C27. They retain normal Ergo/Ergon facilities, constrained by the specialised role and Dokimasia's terminal rules where applicable. - **Standing/exclusions:** bounded behaviour established for the candidate; competing atomic/pure/idempotent/branching claims remain CDG-05. An ordinary Ergon may intentionally invoke an AI service internally as an implementation choice without becoming AI Assurance Ergon or transferring authority.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Expected resource set and the Ergon information boundary. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
**Praxis manages the definition of Context required by the Ergo framework** for fulfilment of its Pathway. In R1.x/R2.x these requirements are concretely defined. During development/definition, an **Ergo identifies the resource set it is most likely to access**, within the applicable Context definitions. The set is deliberately **not exhaustive**. The Ergo framework applies those definitions and works with Mneme to efficiently load anticipated values before Ergon Business Logic executes; preloading every conceivably accessible resource is not required.
```text Praxis Context definitions / Ergo likely resource declaration ↓ Expected / Likely Resource Set ↓ Mneme Context Load ↓ Context Loader ↓ Ergon Business Logic ↓ Context Unloader ↓ Mneme Context Save ```
| Boundary | Responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | **Mneme Context Load** | Locate/acquire, map, establish authoritative state/version basis, apply controls and compose values to materialise the managed Context. | | **Ergo Context Loader** | Ordinarily exposes the **already-loaded Context** to Ergon Business Logic, without taking over Mneme resource acquisition. U14's [special Pylai ingress](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pylai-external-interoperability.md#pylai-pathway-ingress) instead establishes initial Context/Task.input from Communication Information through established Mneme/persistence responsibilities; it performs no semantic mapping. | | **Ergon Business Logic** | Perform bounded activity, primarily reading and acting upon values within its Context, with governed Adhoc acquisition where required. | | **Context Unloader** | Bring resulting bounded processing back across the business-logic boundary, preserving resulting Context state and Pragma Outputs. It is **not a persistence mechanism**. | | **Mneme Context Save** | Resume Mneme management of resulting Context state and the subsequent information consequences of Pragma Outputs; determine appropriate normal or exceptional handling. |
Context Load is the **preferred, performance-optimised common path**. Ergon Business Logic SHOULD primarily use loaded values. It MAY use **Adhoc Resource Access** and **Adhoc Search** where bounded activity requires runtime acquisition, particularly for interaction with external systems, deep interrogation outside reasonably known boundaries, or dynamically emerging information requirements. Adhoc access may be materially more expensive than Context Load; it remains legitimate. External interactions retain Pylai's established boundary.
Bounded Adhoc acquisition does not establish criteria-driven dynamic Context determination. That direction, together with dynamically configured reusable/ generic Ergo, remains **deferred R3.x direction**; no mechanism or AI-driven selection/configuration is introduced by [U18](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u18).
The originating Ergon SHALL NOT be responsible for persistence mechanics, database/shard selection, transactions, persistence tagging/indexing or generic conflict resolution. No exact loader/unloader API, acquisition/batching strategy, query language, locking/MVCC or Context concurrency algorithm is selected.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 3. External Information Search within an Ergo Activity. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
> **An external search performed by Harmonia is intentionally undertaken > within an Ergo activity. Information returned by that search is acquired > and persisted within the governed context of that activity and does not > require a separate generic management-acceptance transition.**
For the architecture currently in scope, Harmonia does not randomly or autonomously search external sources. The Ergo activity intentionally invokes the search and provides the governed context in which the returned information is obtained and persisted as activity information. Management responsibility attaches within that activity's governed information context and applicable Information Unit boundary; it is not a new acceptance decision merely because the source is external. This establishes no universal Unit per returned item, per external result or per activity.
```text Ergo Activity | +-- intentionally invokes External Search | | | v | Returned Information | | +--------+ | v Governed Ergo Activity / Context | v Persisted Activity Information ```
This is an intentional governed acquisition, not a rule that arbitrary observation, storage or consumption establishes management. The generic `Observed -> Accepted Into Management` transition is unnecessary for this case. Originating authority remains source-qualified; acquisition confers no authority over the underlying domain activity. The diagram expresses information meaning, not proof that every invocation succeeds or persistence has completed; AX-15 continues to preserve uncertain operational outcomes.
### 3.1 External Content and Semantic Opacity
Returned domain content may remain semantically opaque to Harmonia. Ergo logic may inspect, apply, associate, transform, route, persist or otherwise act upon it according to explicitly established behaviour. This does not imply that Harmonia independently infers the content's domain meaning.
The established [observable-information and governed Ergo logic boundary](49c9eb2bef0c47b8b5328621d5fc5479.md) continues to apply. No new execution allocation, intrinsic inference or runtime-AI responsibility is established.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/observable-information-and-domain-meaning.md` — ## 3. Governed Ergo Logic Boundary. Standing: Adjudicated observable-information boundary; runtime AI optional.
The Harmonia Platform is responsible for the governed execution boundary around developer-defined Ergo business logic:
```text Context Loading | v Ergo Logic Process | v Context Unloading ```
This is a conceptual boundary, not a new component allocation, interface, runtime topology or definition of loading/unloading machinery. It does not redesign Ergo/Ergon, Praxis, Pragma, Ponos or Digital Twin.
Developer-defined Ergo logic may understand or deliberately interpret known content sufficiently to perform its intended function. It may inspect content, apply rules, transform or map information, append information to a model, invoke terminology or other domain services, invoke an AI agent/service, calculate results and produce outputs. Such intentional interpretation belongs to that defined logic or invoked service; it does not imply intrinsic domain comprehension by the Harmonia Platform. Platform governance and the applicable work, information and domain-authority boundaries remain in force.

Resource set non-exhaustive; Unloader is not persistence; originating Ergon owns no shard/transaction/generic conflict resolution mechanics. CDG-05/45/53; R3.x dynamic Context and dynamically configured reusable/generic Ergo deferred. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.

## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/guardrails/observable-information-and-domain-meaning.md` — ## 4. Runtime AI as an Optional Adjunct. Standing: Adjudicated observable-information boundary; runtime AI optional.
**Runtime AI is an adjunct execution capability intentionally invoked by developer-defined Ergo business logic.** It is optional: Ergo execution may use deterministic logic, rules/algorithms and governed information/services without AI. Invocation does not make AI intrinsic to Harmonia or imply that the Platform independently derives domain meaning.
Using an AI agent/service does not alter Ergo/Praxis/Digital Twin responsibility, authority, governance or execution semantics. Architectural responsibility remains with the governed Harmonia construct invoking the capability. Invocation alone does not make the AI a Digital Twin, Business Role, Service Guardian, governance authority, independent workflow authority or owner of business responsibility, and transfers no architectural authority to it. AI and assurance do not define Twin identity; the existing [Strategy Digital Twin boundary](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#component-7-digital-twin-entity-centred-operational-coordination-construct) remains controlling.
This general position does not allocate an AI-backed assurance activity or a Dokimasia execution engine, or establish new AI governance, orchestration or implementation. Assurance-specific uses and downstream execution allocation are outside this bounded reconciliation; unestablished matters remain explicit under AX-17.
### 4.1 Runtime AI and AI-Assisted Development
**AI-assisted development** uses AI tooling to design, document, analyse, test or implement Harmonia. Using such tooling to build Harmonia does not make it a participant in runtime business execution.
**Runtime AI** is an AI agent/service intentionally invoked by runtime Ergo business logic to contribute to governed execution. The distinction concerns the purpose of invocation, not the product name. Neither development-time use nor runtime invocation establishes intrinsic Platform intelligence.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Classification Assurance
element.documentation:
Assure appropriate classification according to sensitivity and potential consequences of exposure/mishandling.
This capability evaluates whether classification is appropriate to information sensitivity and the consequences of exposure or mishandling. It examines the application of classification rather than merely the presence of a label. The responsibility supports protection decisions while retaining the distinction between the classification basis and the control applied to a particular request.
**Boundary**
Classification assurance does not define compartment membership or grant permission to access classified information.

element.name: [Feature] Order Outcome Association
element.documentation:
Associate an externally established outcome with the applicable bounded order and its progression.
**Overview**
Execution completion and returned outcome are different checkpoints. This Feature makes the result link explicit without equating an order acknowledgement with an outcome.
**Boundary**
Does not interpret diagnostic findings or declare fulfilment from transport delivery alone.

element.name: [CT2] Health Information Protection
element.documentation:
Govern privacy consequences and adequate protection of the information estate and its environment.
Health Information Protection governs the consequences of information exposure and the safeguards protecting information and its operating environment. Privacy safeguards, estate protection, access-practice monitoring, compartment assurance and classification assurance address different questions. Together they distinguish appropriate arrangements from evidence of how information is actually handled, including physical and printed handling.
**Intent**
Protect information and the people affected by its use, with an intelligible basis for evaluating protective arrangements.
**Boundary**
Compartment assurance does not decide access. Subject-specific protection assurance does not create additional macro-level Health Service Assurance trees.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Material Logistics Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate clinically relevant material movement, custody, availability or disposition needed for care or diagnostic fulfilment.
This capability coordinates clinically relevant material movement and the custody, availability or disposition needed for care or diagnostic fulfilment. It makes the material's operational journey intelligible while retaining why the material matters to the clinical activity. The responsibility differs from moving a patient and from managing the diagnostic meaning of information derived from a specimen.
**Boundary**
Bounded clinical-material logistics does not establish a general procurement, supply-chain or enterprise inventory architecture.

It gives reported milestones an operational coordination context without originating the surgical acts they describe. Theatre-specific capacity remains a business responsibility even when shared information machinery supports several service contexts.

It gives reported milestones an operational coordination context without originating the surgical acts they describe. Theatre-specific capacity remains a business responsibility even when shared information machinery supports several service contexts.

element.name: Distinct Management and Durable Preservation of Information and State
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Approach > **Maintain a clear separation between the governed management of Harmonia information and state and its durable preservation and recovery, allowing runtime management and persistence concerns to evolve independently without compromising information integrity.**
This course of action establishes that: - Runtime management of information, active relationships, context, and state is an operational governance concern requiring high availability, concurrent access, and responsive query navigation. - Authoritative durable state establishment, preservation and recovery atomically establish authoritative state and authoritative version progression, preserve the durable management metadata required to interpret that state, and ensure historical retention, immutability, and state reconstruction. - The distinction is strictly one of **architectural responsibility**, not a crude division between "ephemeral data" and "durable data". Information managed at runtime frequently represents durable healthcare concepts, but runtime management and durable preservation fulfill distinct architectural purposes.
#### Motivational Grounding & Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: - `AX-05` (Active vs Durable State): Application-facing active state access/coordination and authoritative durable state/version establishment remain separate architectural concerns. - `AX-09` (Ephemeral Operational State): Transient execution states are reconstructable and decoupled from durable health records. - `AX-11` (High Availability & Responsiveness): Information access must not be blocked by backend persistence latencies or recovery locks. - `AX-14` (Preserve Distinctions): Preserve the boundary between runtime information governance and storage mechanics. - **Strategic Drivers & Goals**: 24/7 Clinical Operational Continuity, High-Throughput Access, Authoritative Preservation.
#### Capability Realisation & Configuration - **Primary Capabilities**: Shapes `EC-03` (Managed State & Lifecycle) and `EC-04` (Information Management). - **Component Boundary Impact**: Explicitly establishes the seam between **Mneme** (application-facing access and active information/state management) and **Mnemosyne** (authoritative durable state/version establishment, preservation and recovery). Neither component subsumes the other; Mnemosyne does not own operational activity progression, workflow execution, active distributed state, Digital Twin coordination, or application-facing query interfaces. Mneme may reject or coordinate a proposed state progression before persistence; only Mnemosyne establishes the new authoritative durable state. Following authoritative commit, Mneme converges its active representation toward that state. Mneme active-state generation and Mnemosyne authoritative version remain distinct concurrency domains (`AX-05`).
#### Downstream Direction (Domains 03–13) - Application Architecture (Domain 05) must forbid direct presentation/application access to database/JPA layers (enforcing Invariant 8). - Technology Architecture (Domain 07) must allow distributed in-memory data fabrics (for runtime state) and durable relational/document stores (for preservation) to be configured and scaled independently.

element.name: [CT3] Health Information Catalogue and Index Management
element.documentation:
Manage descriptive catalogues/indexes through which information existence and location can be established.
This capability maintains the descriptive aids through which information existence and location can be established. It makes information discoverable without equating the catalogue entry with the content it describes. Within information management it answers where relevant information may be found before the separate question of obtaining it under an authorised context.
**Boundary**
Discoverability does not authorise access, retrieve the content or communicate it to a recipient.

element.name: [CT3] Terminology Utilisation Oversight
element.documentation:
Oversee actual terminology/reference-set use and identify inappropriate, inconsistent or drifting usage.
Terminology Utilisation Oversight considers how terminology and reference sets are actually used. It identifies inappropriate application, inconsistency or semantic drift that the existence of an approved terminology does not prevent. Its purpose is to preserve coherent use without making each consuming capability the owner of terminology meaning.
**Boundary**
Use oversight does not redefine terminology or automatically authorise a local semantic variation.

element.name: [CT3] Population Health Longitudinal Assessment
element.documentation:
Establish population-health state, patterns and change over time from applicable evidence.
This capability establishes population-health state, patterns and change over time from relevant evidence. It interprets information at a population scope rather than treating a collection of individual observations as a population conclusion by itself. Its longitudinal purpose makes the temporal and population basis important to the meaning of the assessment.
**Boundary**
Population assessment is not preventative-programme performance, an individual health conclusion or a service-demand decision.

element.name: Healthcare Interoperability Standards and Specifications
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Definition **Healthcare Interoperability Standards and Specifications** comprise the external, open, normative specifications governing healthcare data structures, clinical resource models, exchange semantics, and conformance criteria across enterprise and regional boundaries.
#### Enduring Strategic Role Harmonia is architected to facilitate vendor-neutral health data exchange across acute, primary, community, and diagnostic healthcare systems. This interoperability cannot be accomplished using proprietary vendor protocols. Harmonia depends directly on consensus-based, open standards to establish: - Standardised structural and semantic representations for clinical entities (encounters, observations, conditions, medications, diagnostic reports). - Conformance validation frameworks to assert that emitted and ingested payloads comply with normative specifications. - Standards-conformant external interaction contracts across the Harmonia boundary.
#### Current Strategic Instance - **HL7® FHIR® Release 5 Core & Australian Profile Specifications**: The principal contemporary instance of this resource is HL7 FHIR Release 5, alongside Australian jurisdictional profile specifications (AU Base and AU Core). - **Technology Independence**: The strategic resource is the **specification and standard itself**, not any specific implementation framework or runtime library (such as HAPI FHIR). The strategic dependency endures regardless of which runtime software serialises or deserialises the specifications.
#### Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: `AX-02` (Boundary Membrane), `AX-03` (Native Standards), `AX-13` (Explicit Management Boundary). - **Enterprise Capabilities**: `EC-08` (Interoperability & Exchange), `EC-13` (Semantic Governance & Conformance). - **Courses of Action**: `COA-01` (Boundary Membrane Sovereignty).

element.name: [Feature] Service Readiness Dependency Assessment
element.documentation:
Associate time- and context-qualified dependency evidence to establish a bounded readiness view for an offering.
**Overview**
An offering may be in operating hours but not deliverable because staffing, equipment, materials or supporting services are missing. A readiness view retains insufficiency and the owners of those dependency assertions.
**Boundary**
Readiness evidence does not originate clinical clearance or transfer resource management.

element.name: [CT1] Diagnostic, Therapeutic & Clinical Support Services
element.documentation:
The specialised clinical services that support direct patient care, including pathology and laboratory testing, diagnostic imaging (radiology), pharmacy and medication dispensing, and allied health therapies.
Specialised services contribute evidence, professional interpretation, medication provision and therapeutic support to individual care. The established decomposition distinguishes diagnostic provision from medication and pharmacy services, while retaining wider therapeutic and allied-health scope as enterprise context. The catalogue deliberately explains the modelled branches without presenting them as an exhaustive inventory of clinical support.
**Intent**
Provide the specialised contributions that treating participants need to assess and care for individuals.
**Boundary**
Producing diagnostic evidence, authorising a report, dispensing medication and administering treatment establish different outcomes and authorities.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Requests, specimen associations, reports and medication events require reliable correlation and exchange. Supporting those information flows does not make Harmonia the diagnostic practitioner, pharmacy or therapy provider.

element.name: [CT3] Care-Place Readiness Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage whether a particular care place is ready for allocation or use.
Care-Place Readiness Management establishes whether a particular place can be allocated or used in its operational context. It connects the place's condition with its intended use so that vacancy can be distinguished from readiness. This is a place-specific responsibility within scheduling and capacity, supporting credible allocation rather than merely counting physical spaces.
**Boundary**
Readiness of one place does not establish collective readiness or usable capacity of the whole service.

element.name: [Topic] Practitioner
element.documentation:
**Definition**: An identifiable individual healthcare workforce or professional entity.
**Description**: Information describing an individual participating professionally in healthcare, independent of a particular organisational position, assignment or service context.
**Semantic Classification**: `Entity`
**Architectural Scope**: Represents the individual professional independently of statutory registration status. A `Practitioner` may be known to Harmonia prior to verification, when registration is pending or not applicable (e.g. unregistered healthcare workers, support staff), or when registration is externally authoritative.
**Boundary Rule**: $\text{Practitioner} \neq \text{Professional Registration}$. Registration is a governed assertion concerning a Practitioner, not the definition of the Practitioner entity itself.

element.name: [CT2] Interaction & Experience
element.documentation:
- **Architectural Scope**: Provide contextual interaction between human actors, Harmonia, and enterprise presentation services, including visualization, alerting, and collaboration integration. - **Functional Responsibilities**: - Mediating presentation interactions via dedicated backend-for-frontend gateways decoupled from internal databases. - Rendering clinical timelines, provider directory management interfaces, and operational console dashboards. - Providing contextual notifications and alerts to human users across web and mobile channels. - Projecting longitudinal record context into secure multidisciplinary collaboration spaces. - **Boundary Note**: Does not absorb the healthcare semantics of Clinical Collaboration or medical documentation. Consumes established identity and security context; does not own authentication, consent, or clinical truth.
Interaction & Experience makes contextual information and governed actions available to human participants through presentation and collaboration integration. Clinical timelines, directory administration and operational dashboards have different purposes, but share a need to retain established identity, security and information context. The recurring responsibility is usable interaction within those boundaries.
**Boundary**
Presentation does not own consent, authentication or clinical truth, and collaboration projection does not absorb clinical documentation semantics.

element.name: Centralised Synchronous Persistence Can Constrain Concurrent Processing
element.documentation:
### Assessment Summary Requiring central synchronous persistence interaction for every unit of active processing can introduce contention, latency, unnecessary I/O and coordination bottlenecks that limit concurrent throughput and scalability.
### Operational Hazard In a high-volume regional integration hub, thousands of clinical messages arrive concurrently from emergency rooms, pathology analyzers, and patient portals. If the architecture forces every active query, routing step, and transient coordination check to execute synchronous disk I/O and transactional row locking against a single central database: - Transaction lock contention and wait states escalate as concurrency increases. - Increased I/O wait times can cause ingress queues to fill and upstream connections to time out. - High-priority emergency point-of-care clinical queries become stalled behind long-running background batch imports. - Scalability is constrained to the physical I/O limits of the central persistence appliance.
*Note on Technology Neutrality*: This assessment diagnoses the fundamental hazards of synchronous persistence contention, latency, and coordination bottlenecks. It is an architectural evaluation of concurrency dynamics; it does not mandate any specific product, cache, database, or queueing technology.
### Architectural Implication & Response - The architecture must decouple active operational coordination from authoritative durable persistence. - High-frequency operational checks and client-facing queries must be served through responsive, concurrent access paths without imposing transactional lock contention on authoritative storage. - **Related Driver**: [Continuous Clinical Service Availability](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md) - **Target Goal**: [Responsive Access to Managed Information](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axioms**: [AX-11 (Responsive & Resilient Information Access)](../principle/8a1e995f16954484a78ae1c5c114d546.md), [AX-05 (Active Coordination ≠ Authoritative State)](../principle/0412a2084f0145babc4f022c71fea65f.md), [AX-09 (Default Ephemerality of Operational State)](../principle/9a5cb9e8876844e58e660f909f7df9fc.md)

element.documentation:
Project qualified observed demand, capacity and utilisation for authorised planning consumers.
**Overview**
Comparisons need service, temporal and context qualifiers so that planned future capacity is not confused with present operational capacity.
**Boundary**
Projection does not establish a planning conclusion or allocate services and staff.

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Distribution Planning
element.documentation:
Determine the distribution of planned capacity across a geographical, organisational, site or service-network footprint.
Health Service Distribution Planning determines how planned capacity should be distributed across a geographical, organisational or service-network footprint. It addresses the placement of the planned response rather than only its aggregate scale. This allows the planning context to distinguish enough total capacity from capacity positioned where it is needed.
**Boundary**
A planned footprint does not establish recognised location records, identifiable offerings or actual resource deployment.

element.name: [Feature] Emergency Treatment Capacity Management
element.documentation:
Represent current emergency treatment capacity under space, staffing and acuity constraints.
**Overview**
Bay state and length of stay contribute evidence but do not alone establish the ability to accept another care demand.
**Boundary**
Local responsibility retains its capacity meaning; Service Capacity Management consumes it without acquiring ownership or imposing one common capacity model.

element.name: Collaborative Reusable Capability Realisation
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Approach > **Realize bounded reusable platform capabilities (context, policy, provenance, EC-12 Operational Assurance) collaboratively across participating components rather than through centralized, bottlenecked runtime services.**
Harmonia requires pervasive platform capabilities—such as security policy evaluation, contextual propagation, operational assurance, and provenance tracking—across all transactions. This course of action establishes that: - **Reusable Capability $\neq$ Centralised Service (Guardrail G1)**: The existence of a reusable enterprise capability does not imply that a single monolithic service must execute it centrally. - Reusable capabilities define bounded responsibilities and common semantic rules. Participating components consume or enforce them through governed contracts without acquiring shared semantic ownership. **Distributed participation does not imply distributed responsibility. Cross-cutting concern does not imply cross-cutting responsibility.** - Centralized choke points and synchronous runtime bottlenecks are strictly avoided, ensuring horizontal scalability and fault isolation.
#### Motivational Grounding & Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: - `AX-04` (Own Semantics / Use Machinery): Maintain sovereign capability rules while delegating execution across components. - `AX-07` (Intrinsic Security): Security and policy evaluation must be pervasive and intrinsic to all operations, not an external proxy. - `AX-11` (High Availability & Responsiveness): Eliminate single points of congestion and failure across the integration fabric. - **Strategic Drivers & Goals**: High Scalability, Fault Tolerance, Zero Bottleneck Architecture, Decentralised Resilience.
#### Capability Realisation & Configuration - **Primary Capabilities**: Shapes `EC-02` (Context Management), `EC-06` (Policy & Control), `EC-07` (Provenance & Traceability), and `EC-12` (Operational Assurance). Assurance here means the established EC-12 operational contribution; no independent Governed Assurance or EC-14 relationship is established. - **Component Boundary Impact**: Prevents components like **Themis** (Policy & Control) from becoming synchronous network choke points for every micro-operation; policy contracts are distributed and evaluated collaboratively.
#### Downstream Direction (Domains 03–13) - Application Architecture (Domain 05) and Technology Architecture (Domain 07) realise reusable responsibilities through governed contracts while preserving bounded ownership, scalability and fault isolation. Existing `themis-api` and `petasos-api` packages are illustrative downstream traceability only; Strategy does not mandate API packaging, local embedding, frameworks or deployment choices.

element.name: [CT3] Population Health Reporting
element.documentation:
Communicate established population-health assessments, surveillance, events, trends and findings.
Population Health Reporting communicates established assessments, surveillance findings, events and trends. Its role is to make population understanding available with its scope intact, rather than replace the assessment or event-identification work underlying it. This supports use of the findings by other abilities without assuming what those abilities must conclude.
**Boundary**
General reporting is distinct from formal notification management and does not establish a response or planning decision.

Notification management neither defines the obligation nor owns operational response, and is distinct from general reporting. Surveillance may provide evidence for preventative problems/cohorts, demand planning, clinical quality or safety without establishing those outcomes. Population assessment differs from preventative-programme performance. Individual observations may contribute population evidence without becoming population conclusions. Epidemiology, outbreak response and public-health scope are deliberately not exhaustively modelled."}]

Exchange is not execution, notification is not outcome, and interaction is not clinical authority.

element.name: [CT3] Binary Content Association & Resolution
element.documentation:
Maintain content associations and custody knowledge sufficient for governed payload resolution, retrieval and assembly.
**Overview**
Document attachments, diagnostic media and operational artefacts share a need to locate usable content while distinguishing logical meaning from physical possession.
**Intent**
Make logical information and its usable payloads consistently associable while retaining custody boundaries.
**Boundary**

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Intervention
element.documentation:
The capability to perform clinical actions intended to alter, maintain or otherwise manage an individual's health state in accordance with an established care intent.
Clinical Intervention is the ability to perform a clinical action under an established care intent. It marks the transition from intended care to care actually performed, whether the action seeks to alter, maintain or otherwise manage health. Its exercise can establish that treatment occurred even when the desired clinical result was not achieved.
**Intent**
Put the intended clinical response into practice through appropriately authorised care.
**Boundary**
Orders and appointments express or arrange future activity; they are not evidence that the intervention occurred. Therapy, medication and procedural examples do not constitute an approved three-child taxonomy: that proposed decomposition remains provisional.
## Qualified relationship assertions
These source predicates retain their recorded standing and currentness. Their native mapping remains unestablished; they are not inferred ArchiMate edges. The complete original assertions and qualifications are retained in this element’s metadata.

element.name: Calliope-DataSets
element.documentation:
Distinct Calliope runtime management/repository responsibility for mutable governed ValueSets, CodeSets, Structured Metadata and applicable ontology content. Owns governed content, not persistence machinery; uses established Mneme/Mnemosyne and, where workflow is required, existing Ponos/Ergo/Praxis. Models/build definitions establish its structural contracts. Detailed ontology boundary, workflow, UI and physical realisation remain [deferred](466ad8f75a954c0581b5bba090443849.md).
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/calliope-models-and-datasets.md` — ## Calliope-DataSets. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
Calliope-DataSets is the runtime repository/management responsibility for mutable governed ValueSets, CodeSets, Structured Metadata and applicable governed ontology content. Its authoritative content may change while Harmonia operates. Governed activities may include update request, review, approval, authoritative update, tagging/classification and making approved content available. This is not an established state machine or a detailed DataSet workflow.
Calliope-DataSets owns the application responsibility for its datasets. It is **not another Persistence Manager**. Governed access uses established Mneme Context/Pragma responsibilities and authoritative persistence remains with Mnemosyne under AX-05:
```text Calliope-DataSets: governed content management ↓ Mneme: Context / Pragma and applicable governed access ↓ Mnemosyne: authoritative durable establishment and reporting ```
Where dataset governance requires workflow, existing Ponos / Ergo / Ergon / Praxis capabilities may be used. No Calliope workflow engine or separate human-interaction framework is introduced. Detailed management UI, Iris/forms design and workflow are deferred.

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Capability Identification
element.documentation:
Identify the ordinary business abilities needed to satisfy the service need across clinical, workforce, facility, technology, information and support concerns.
This capability identifies the ordinary business abilities a proposed service needs across clinical, workforce, facility, information, technology and support concerns. It broadens service modelling beyond a clinical description to the conditions needed for viability. Its contribution is an understanding of required abilities, leaving their fulfilment and governing authority with the appropriate responsibilities.
**Boundary**
The word capability here does not allocate Harmonia CT tiers or establish new catalogue elements.

element.name: [CT3] Diagnostic Service Appointment Management
element.documentation:
Manage the diagnostic-service-specific scheduled opportunity, including preparation, modality, urgency, duration and other service-specific constraints.
Diagnostic Service Appointment Management makes a scheduled diagnostic opportunity credible in the service's own context. Preparation, modality, urgency and duration can materially affect whether an appointment is usable, so the responsibility is richer than recording a generic time slot. It supports service access while remaining separate from performance of the diagnostic activity.
**Boundary**
A diagnostic booking establishes neither evidence acquisition nor a report and is distinct from generic Care Appointment Management.

element.name: [CT1] Health Products & Clinical Technology
element.documentation:
Manage health products and clinical technology in the care environment, with distinct device inventory, functional/release, deployment, utilisation, integration and lifecycle responsibilities. Product procurement and supply context is retained without inferring further Health Product Management decomposition.
This capability manages health products and clinical technology as business concerns in the care environment. Its established clinical-technology branch distinguishes knowledge of the device estate, functional state, deployment, user enablement, integration and lifecycle disposition. Product procurement and supply remain relevant context without a newly inferred Health Product Management decomposition.
**Intent**
Keep the technology context needed for safe service activity and information exchange coherent and governed.
**Boundary**
Device-specific enablement, clinical privilege and use in care are different concerns. The seven established device children do not resolve the separate maintenance-membership discrepancy.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Integration provision and device-data integration materially affect exchanged information and its care context. Supply-chain, maintenance and clinical-use authority are not transferred to Harmonia.

element.name: AX-04 Harmonia Owns the Semantics; Engines Provide the Machinery
element.documentation:
#### Axiom
Harmonia owns the architectural semantics governing information authority, security, lifecycle, concurrency, provenance, auditability, resilience and operational integrity.
Harmonia SHALL preferentially use capabilities supplied by underlying technology engines where those capabilities satisfy Harmonia's architectural invariants rather than reproduce equivalent functionality.
#### Rationale
Harmonia should own its meaning without unnecessarily owning commodity infrastructure machinery.
#### Consequences
HAPI FHIR MAY provide FHIR persistence, indexing, versioning and search.
Infinispan MAY provide distributed caching, entry metadata and atomic coordination primitives.
ActiveMQ Artemis MAY provide durable messaging.
PostgreSQL MAY provide transactional relational persistence.
These technologies implement Harmonia capabilities. They do not define Harmonia's architectural semantics.
#### Maxim
Use the machinery. Own the semantics.
**This does not mean:**
- Harmonia should wrap every engine capability behind a bespoke implementation. - An engine's native behaviour automatically satisfies a Harmonia invariant. - Using HAPI FHIR makes Harmonia a HAPI FHIR application.

Departure notification communicates the physical exit and associated record and place-state context to the applicable participants. It distinguishes departure information from earlier readiness and from the clinical decision, while retaining the separate question of responsibility actually assumed elsewhere.

element.name: [CT2] Patient Clinical Record
element.documentation:
Patient Clinical Record provides a governed longitudinal representation across encounters, providers and source systems. Assembly supplies the timeline, active access supports current care context, and durable preservation retains the history of what Harmonia received, knew or managed. These contributions are complementary: a responsive working view must not become the authority for durable history.
**Overview**
Patient Clinical Record provides a governed longitudinal representation across encounters, providers and source systems. Assembly supplies the timeline, active access supports current care context, and durable preservation retains the history of what Harmonia received, knew or managed. These contributions are complementary: a responsive working view must not become the authority for durable history.
**Intent**
Patient Clinical Record provides a governed longitudinal representation across encounters, providers and source systems. Assembly supplies the timeline, active access supports current care context, and durable preservation retains the history of what Harmonia received, knew or managed. These contributions are complementary: a responsive working view must not become the authority for durable history.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Intent — predecessor explanation
Make cross-institutional information usable over time without erasing source provenance or prior knowledge through correction.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Preservation does not originate clinical facts. Active distributed access and authoritative durable preservation remain separate under AX-05.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Longitudinal assembly, active access and governed durable history are direct information-management responsibilities within the Core boundary.

element.name: [Feature] Discharge Readiness & Coordination Oversight
element.documentation:
Track and aggregate multidisciplinary discharge milestones, home care confirmations, and transit readiness across care teams.
Readiness oversight brings multidisciplinary, home-care and transport confirmations into one coordination view. Aggregation supports the responsible participants' decisions but does not itself confer authority to discharge or establish acceptance of continuing care by another provider.

element.name: [CT3] Preventative Health Programme Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage an organised response to a preventative-health need/objective without absorbing its delivery capabilities.
Preventative Health Programme Management establishes and manages an organised response to a preventative need or objective. It keeps the programme purpose and coordinated activity intelligible while allowing appointments, interventions and other delivery abilities to retain their own responsibilities. Screening and immunisation illustrate programmes rather than creating additional capability tiers.
**Boundary**
Managing the programme does not acquire the clinical or operational authority of the activities delivering it.

This outward notification responsibility is distinct from querying a chronic-care timeline: the latter shares context but has no established equivalence to dispatching the required arrival, admission or discharge notice.

element.name: [CT3] Identity Assurance
element.documentation:
Establish sufficient confidence that a person is who they claim to be through appropriate evidence and processes.
Identity Assurance establishes confidence that a person is who they claim to be using appropriate evidence and processes. It concerns the basis and strength of the identity claim, rather than only successful use of an authentication mechanism. Within identity governance it makes confidence a question that can be considered separately from contextual sufficiency and access authority.
**Boundary**
An assured identity is not automatically sufficient for every context or permitted to perform every action.

element.name: [CT1] Health Research & Innovation
element.documentation:
Provide existing health information for authorised research under applicable constraints and evaluate health innovation; deliberately under-decomposed for R1/R2.
This capability frames the deliberately bounded research and innovation responsibilities material to Harmonia's R1/R2 architecture. Research Information Support concerns provision of existing information for authorised research; Health Innovation concerns evaluation of proposed or emerging innovation. These establish useful enterprise context without implying a complete research organisation or innovation lifecycle.
**Intent**
Support legitimate research information needs and informed consideration of changes to health-service or clinical practice.
**Boundary**
Information provision does not own trials, ethics approval or specialist research analysis. Evaluating innovation does not authorise adoption or implementation.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Governed provision of existing information materially enables authorised research. Innovation evaluation has no separate platform assignment; the CT1 classification must not be inherited by each descendant.

element.name: [Feature] Operational Queue Progression
element.documentation:
Track client queue progression through reception, waiting area, consultation, and billing.
Operational queue progression makes the patient's passage through clinic stages visible. The queue concerns real-world arrival, waiting and consultation context, rather than a broker queue, and does not give Harmonia authority to determine clinical priority or own the clinician's worklist.

element.documentation:
Redacts or masks search results and clinical content based on the caller's verified security context and patient consent directives.

Its capability-scoped standing is retained instead of promoting the behaviour to a Feature simply to obtain traceability symmetry.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Device Loan & Deployment Management
element.documentation:
Manage device loan, issue, assignment, placement, return and deployment.
Clinical Device Loan & Deployment Management manages where devices are placed and the issue, assignment, return or loan context under which they are available. It connects an identifiable device with its operational deployment rather than assuming ownership or inventory presence explains its current use. This supports an intelligible account of the device estate as placements change.
**Boundary**
Deployment is not device-specific user enablement, clinical use or evidence of clinical privilege.

element.documentation:
Establish clinically meaningful risk and expected-course judgements for an individual.
**Overview**
Establish clinically meaningful risk and expected-course judgements for an individual. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Clinical Determination.
**Intent**
Make anticipated clinical risk and course explicit for the individual care concern.
**Boundary**
Risk/prognostic judgement is distinct from operational urgency, source-information authority and platform assurance.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Semantics Governance
element.documentation:
Govern clinical meaning and appropriate organisational use of semantic artefacts.
Clinical Semantics Governance maintains the standing and appropriate use of terminology, classifications and semantic mappings. Terminology provides consistent meaning; classification concerns sensitivity and consequences of exposure or mishandling. The established children distinguish governing artefacts from overseeing actual use and permit controlled terminology localisation where adopted material does not meet legitimate needs.
**Intent**
Keep meaning and classification intelligible across organisational use without concealing semantic drift or local variation.
**Boundary**
Compartmentalisation concerns contextual relationships rather than classification or terminology. Classification Localisation is not an established peer; mappings must preserve the separate meanings and authorities they connect.
## Qualified relationship assertions
These source predicates retain their recorded standing and currentness. Their native mapping remains unestablished; they are not inferred ArchiMate edges. The complete original assertions and qualifications are retained in this element’s metadata.

element.documentation:
Associate validated communication endpoints (secure messaging addresses, direct routing queues) with specific practitioner roles.
Endpoint binding makes a verified communication destination specific to the practitioner's acting role. It supports routing to the intended professional capacity rather than assuming that every address attached to the person is interchangeable across organisations and services.

element.name: AX-07 Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations
element.documentation: #### Axiom Every governed operation SHALL execute within an established security context and SHALL be subject to Harmonia security policy. Security SHALL be enforced by framework and platform boundaries where practicable and SHALL NOT depend solely upon developer knowledge, coding convention or voluntary caller behaviour. #### Rationale Security is part of the semantics of performing an operation, not an optional service invoked by well-behaved code. #### Consequences Themis owns Harmonia security policy evaluation. Trusted identity and security context SHALL be established before governed actions are performed. Security context is operational context and SHALL NOT automatically become persistent information content. Security-significant events MAY become durable audit evidence according to policy. #### Kleio mandatory authoritative audit capture Kleio SHALL perform mandatory authoritative audit capture under intrinsic platform authority associated with its established audit responsibility. That capture SHALL execute within an established security context and remain subject to Harmonia security policy; Themis retains policy evaluation ownership. This is governed platform authority, not a security bypass or policy exception. The Identity associated with the audited activity SHALL remain audit evidence. It is not the authority under which the mandatory AuditEvent is persisted. Kleio SHALL NOT borrow the originating Identity's PEP-Criteria merely to persist evidence of that Identity's activity. Identity-derived authorisation resolved and enforced through Themis remains distinct from Kleio's capture authority. Where authoritative audit capture is required for a governed operation and Kleio cannot exercise that platform authority sufficiently to capture the required evidence, the governed operation SHALL fail closed. This authority is established specifically for Kleio mandatory authoritative audit capture. It SHALL NOT be inferred for other Kleio activities or generalised to other Harmonia components. Any proposed equivalent authority elsewhere is a separate architecture question under AX-17. Detailed authority representation and enforcement mechanisms remain deferred. **This does not mean:** - Every security decision belongs in a FHIR resource. - Every authorization evaluation belongs in the audit repository. - Internal security context should be exposed to external systems.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Risk Response Management
element.documentation:
Manage active response, containment and remediation where risk has materialised, is emerging or requires active intervention.
Clinical Risk Response Management manages active intervention, containment or remediation where a safety risk is emerging, materialised or otherwise demands action. Its purpose is to address the developing situation rather than only reduce future exposure. The responsibility remains clinical-risk-specific while the actual actions may belong to other established abilities.
**Boundary**
It is not a general enterprise incident-management container and does not acquire the clinical authority of responding participants.

element.name: [Feature] Exchange Profile Governance
element.documentation:
Govern the semantic and conformance constraints of an interoperability profile.
**Overview**
An external contract must state which representations and extensions are permitted; validation applies that contract but does not define it.
**Boundary**
Profile governance does not transmit messages or publish internal operational metadata.

element.name: National Healthcare Directory / Endpoint Governance
element.documentation:
### Context & Pressure Healthcare delivery requires seamless coordination between hundreds of clinics, hospitals, diagnostic practices, and thousands of accredited practitioners. Clinical correspondence, diagnostic reports, and e-referrals frequently go astray due to outdated contact details, retired practitioners, or misconfigured electronic messaging endpoints.
National regulatory frameworks (such as the Australian HI Service and AHPRA) publish authoritative registers of practitioners and healthcare organizations. Electronic messaging networks require verified service endpoints to ensure confidential messages are delivered only to legitimate recipients.
### Architectural Imperative Harmonia must govern practitioner credentials and electronic service endpoints through authoritative directory mechanisms. Integration workflows must validate that practitioner identities, roles, and destination addresses are authenticated and currently authorized.
- **Primary Stakeholders**: [Healthcare Directory Stewards & Registrars](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md), [Clinicians & Care Teams](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md) - **External Authorities**: [HI Service](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/external-authorities.md), [AHPRA](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/external-authorities.md) - **Associated Goal**: [Reliable Subject Identity & Referential Integrity](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axiom**: [AX-14 (Preservation of Semantic Distinctions)](../principle/d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md)

element.name: [CT3] Care Appropriateness Review
element.documentation:
Evaluate whether the current intended care remains suitable in the individual’s current context.
Care Appropriateness Review evaluates whether the current care intent remains suitable for the individual in their present context. Its question concerns continuing suitability rather than whether treatment has produced a measurable effect. That distinction permits a review to recognise that effective care may no longer be appropriate to continue.
**Boundary**
An appropriateness judgement can identify a need to reconsider care; establishing revised intent remains Individual Care Planning.
