element.name: Behaviour
element.documentation:
- **Realisation:** each DigitalTwin has **Behaviour [1..*]**. Each Behaviour is realised through **Praxis → Pathway → Ergo [exactly 1]**. A one-Ergo Praxis retains required Context, expected criteria/outcomes, fulfilment semantics and housekeeping; it is neither an orchestrator nor a choreographer. [U19 DesignNote](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md). - **Role/features:** Ergon specialisation for DigitalTwin operation. It inherits/ reuses Context Loading and Context Unloading, process-management mechanisms, Petasos/platform integration, assurance integration, logging/observability, reporting, checkpoint/platform integration and other common Ergo/Ergon facilities. [U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02), [common specialisation principle](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/README.md#specialisation-principle). - **Information/persistence/collaboration:** receives its own identifiable **BehaviourStimulus / BehaviourEffector** derived from an input in which it has registered interest. Operates relative to the Twin's singular represented entity. Its Praxis-defined Context is loaded fresh after the preceding Behaviour completes and saves its consequences; Mneme manages Load/Save and Pragma, Mnemosyne establishes durable state and Petasos handles handoff. - **Execution/output/failure:** interested Behaviours execute sequentially for each input. Outputs may enter normal governed processing, resolving Twin-relative references only where required. Same-Twin Stimulus/Effector outputs join its normal queue without recursive interruption. The developer's `ContinueBehaviourOnFailure` contains failure to the current execution; the Behaviour remains active, other interested Behaviours and normal queue processing continue. `StopBehaviourOnFailure` stops the failing Behaviour immediately, lets remaining interested Behaviours complete the current input, then halts the Twin. `StopDigitalTwinOnFailure` terminates the failing Behaviour and halts the Twin immediately; remaining current-input and subsequent queued processing stop. Sequencing policy is developer-owned through the framework API; the applicable sequence stays stable throughout an input, and configuration changes apply to subsequent inputs. No priority metadata or Pathway orchestration (U19). - **Standing/exclusions:** discrete candidate activity specialisation, not an independent activity framework parallel to Ergo/Ergon. DigitalTwin adds only genuinely Twin-specific behaviour instead of duplicating platform mechanisms; Behaviour acquires no standalone Information Resource merely by being activity.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 2. Digital Twin Behaviour structure. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
```text Digital Twin └── Behaviour [1..*] └── Praxis └── Pathway └── Ergo [exactly 1] ```
A Digital Twin has one or more Behaviours. Each Behaviour is realised through a Praxis and a Pathway containing **exactly one Ergo**. A one-Ergo Praxis is a genuine Praxis: Praxis is not synonymous with multi-step workflow complexity. Its required Context definitions, expected criteria/outcomes, fulfilment semantics and Praxis-level housekeeping still apply.
Praxis defines Pathway fulfilment; it is neither an orchestrator nor a choreographer. Behaviour sequencing is a Twin execution responsibility, not Pathway orchestration. This specialised pattern retains the general [Praxis → Pathway Aggregation [0..1]](../data-object/0f961462340348b290fd844357d54d67.md) and does not require all other Praxes to have a Pathway or exactly one Ergo. The structure describes realisation, not new Composition, process or deployment boundaries.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 7. Fresh Context for each Behaviour. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
Each Behaviour has its own **Praxis-defined Context requirements**. Mneme loads Context fresh when that Behaviour begins, and manages its Context Save:
```text Behaviour A: Context Load → Execute → Context Save ↓ Behaviour B: fresh Context Load → Execute → Context Save ↓ Behaviour C: fresh Context Load → Execute → Context Save ```
On the normal path, Behaviour B's Context is loaded **after A has completed and saved its information consequences**; C's is loaded after B, and so forth. Progression after failure remains subject to section 10. Later Behaviours may therefore observe authoritative information consequences established by earlier Behaviours. There is **no single immutable input-level Context snapshot** shared by all interested Behaviours.
Praxis defines required Context; Mneme retains Context management, materialisation and save. Normal [Loader/Unloader versus Load/Save boundaries](49c9eb2bef0c47b8b5328621d5fc5479.md) apply. Mnemosyne alone establishes authoritative durable state; working changes and Context Save invocation do not manufacture confirmed persistence outcomes. Existing exceptional harmonisation and AX-15 uncertainty semantics remain intact. This note adds no cross-Behaviour transaction, universal globally consistent snapshot or conflict-resolution mechanism.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 8. Behaviour sequence and developer policy. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
**R1.x/R2.x shall support an API** through which developer-supplied executable- domain configuration may establish the execution sequence of loaded Behaviours.
```text Digital Twin executable domain starts → Behaviours loaded → developer sequencing/configuration hook → Behaviour sequence established → Twin ready for input processing ```
The framework owns loading/discovery, exposing the loaded Behaviour set, providing the API to establish or update the sequence, maintaining that sequence and executing interested Behaviours accordingly. **The developer owns sequencing policy.** Where no developer-defined sequence is supplied, execution order is **unspecified**; serial execution and fresh per-Behaviour Context still apply.
> **The Behaviour sequence applicable when processing of a Stimulus or Effector > commences remains stable for the duration of that input. Changes to the > configured Behaviour sequence apply to subsequently processed inputs.**
This constrains execution semantics without prescribing how the sequencing API implements configuration changes.
R1.x/R2.x introduces no priority metadata, dependency graph, Before/After relationships, Criteria-based ordering or adaptive sequencing. Behaviour sequencing is not Pathway orchestration. Richer R3.x sequencing/priority mechanisms and dynamic/Criteria-driven sequencing remain deferred.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 9. Behaviour outputs and egress. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
A Behaviour may generate ordinary Harmonia-governed outputs, including Stimulus, Effector, ActionableTask, Pragma and other governed information appropriate to its processing. Outputs may enter the normal Harmonia processing fabric: **Twin Behaviour processing is not a closed execution loop**.
Outputs **should retain entity-relative references and Context semantics** where this simplifies Behaviour implementation. When output crosses into general Harmonia processing, output processing may need to resolve/dereference those references into the explicit governed representation the receiving context requires:
```text Twin-relative Behaviour execution → Behaviour output → resolve / dereference where required → general Harmonia processing ```
No transformation is required where the output is already sufficiently explicit. This is an internal execution-context boundary; applicable Pylai external interoperability/publication controls still apply if information subsequently leaves Harmonia. The reference-resolution implementation mechanism is deferred.
Output Stimulus or Effector applicable to the **same Twin** enters that Twin's **normal input queue**. It does not recursively interrupt or re-enter processing of the current input, and remains subject to serialisation and any stop disposition.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/design-notes/DesignNote-Digital-Twin-Behaviour-and-Execution-Semantics.md` — ## 10. Behaviour failure dispositions. Standing: Agreed A4.7 decisions U19; whole-candidate acceptance and deferred mechanisms unchanged.
The Behaviour developer defines the failure disposition. R1.x/R2.x establishes three dispositions with distinct effects on the failing Behaviour, the current Stimulus or Effector and subsequent queued inputs:
| Disposition | Failing Behaviour | Other interested Behaviours / current input | Digital Twin / subsequent inputs | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `ContinueBehaviourOnFailure` | Failure applies to the current Behaviour execution. The Behaviour remains active and may process subsequent applicable Stimulus or Effector inputs normally. | Unaffected; continue processing the current input normally. | Continues normal queue processing. | | `StopBehaviourOnFailure` | Stops immediately and undertakes no further processing. | Unaffected by that immediate stop; continue processing the current input. | Halts once the remaining interested Behaviours complete the current input. No subsequent queued input is processed before authorised administrative intervention. | | `StopDigitalTwinOnFailure` | Terminates immediately. | No remaining Behaviour processes the current input. | Stops immediately. No subsequent queued Stimulus or Effector is processed; queued inputs remain pending subject to deferred administrative recovery semantics. |
> **StopBehaviourOnFailure stops the failing Behaviour immediately, permits the > remaining Behaviours to complete the current Twin input, and then halts the > Digital Twin.**
These are increasing scopes of failure containment/escalation:
```text ContinueBehaviourOnFailure → contain failure to the current Behaviour execution
StopBehaviourOnFailure → stop the failing Behaviour immediately → remaining interested Behaviours complete the current input → halt the Digital Twin
StopDigitalTwinOnFailure → halt the entire Digital Twin immediately ```
A pending Twin halt from `StopBehaviourOnFailure` is not undone by another Behaviour's `ContinueBehaviourOnFailure`; `StopDigitalTwinOnFailure` always halts the Twin immediately, including while remaining Behaviours are being processed. Failure does not prove that no information consequences occurred; AX-15 uncertainty remains binding. No default disposition, automatic retry, replay or skip semantics is introduced.

element.name: [CT3] Security & Information-Use Accountability
element.documentation:
Evaluate whether attributed security-relevant activity/information use was appropriate within policy, obligation and authority constraints, and establish accountability.
This capability evaluates attributed activity and information use against applicable policy, obligations and authority constraints. It establishes accountability rather than simply recording participation. Its purpose depends on preserving the circumstances of action so that appropriateness is considered within the relevant mandate instead of inferred from identity or technical success.
**Boundary**
An authenticated actor and a successful operation are not proof of legitimate information use.

element.name: [CT3] Access Control Context Management
element.documentation:
Determine what information, functions, activities or other concerns require control, under what circumstances and how requirements are modelled.
Access Control Context Management establishes what requires control, the circumstances in which control applies and how those requirements are modelled. It gives access governance an explicit subject and context rather than reducing it to assembling runtime attributes. The responsibility can encompass information, functions and activities under physical, procedural or digital arrangements.
**Boundary**
Defining control context does not itself enforce the controls or establish that they operate effectively.

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Resource Management
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Clinical Resource Management integrates location and allocation information for shared clinical equipment. It makes the current operational resource context available rather than treating device inventory as proof that equipment can be used for a particular need. The responsibility supports coordination while retaining the distinction between resource state and a service's capacity.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Equipment tracking does not acquire enterprise asset ownership, maintenance responsibility or clinical authority to use it.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Dynamic equipment context materially supports operational coordination across care environments.

element.name: [CT2] Health Information Exchange Enablement
element.documentation:
As a BEC, Health Information Exchange provides reusable information-movement enablement through submission, retrieval mediation, addressed distribution and syndication. The models distinguish sending to a participant, requesting information, deliberately distributing to named recipients and publishing changes to matching subscribers. Their common responsibility is the exchange context, including routing and delivery state, rather than the business meaning of every payload.
**Overview**
As a BEC, Health Information Exchange provides reusable information-movement enablement through submission, retrieval mediation, addressed distribution and syndication. The models distinguish sending to a participant, requesting information, deliberately distributing to named recipients and publishing changes to matching subscribers. Their common responsibility is the exchange context, including routing and delivery state, rather than the business meaning of every payload.
**Intent**
As a BEC, Health Information Exchange provides reusable information-movement enablement through submission, retrieval mediation, addressed distribution and syndication. The models distinguish sending to a participant, requesting information, deliberately distributing to named recipients and publishing changes to matching subscribers. Their common responsibility is the exchange context, including routing and delivery state, rather than the business meaning of every payload.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
The capability owns exchange transaction state without acquiring clinical-document ownership. Its name collision with the BC remains unresolved; exchange egress ends management of the emitted representation.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Multi-party exchange and per-destination delivery tracking are substantive Core responsibilities, bounded by the external contract and originating information authority.

element.name: Resource Harmonisation Manager
element.documentation:
**Internal Mneme responsibility/capability, not a fifth exposed service or an independent execution framework.** [U10](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u10) establishes the [exceptional delivery path](a6580e0b9f0f40c9a33d731d20110057.md). It identifies/manages conditions that cannot proceed normally and causes appropriate bounded Harmonisation Ergon work; it does not perform domain harmonisation itself.
- **Expected use:** approximately 5% or less at worst of resource-delivery activity, a design expectation, not a hard SLA. Normal handling remains efficient. - **Execution:** new governed work through the established Harmonia work/execution contract reuses Ponos; no resumed originating Ergon, duplicate/embedded execution framework or originating-Ergon generic conflict resolution. - **Information/reuse:** relevant condition/state/Context is preserved for governed handling; a reusable Ergo Library remains a candidate reuse mechanism only. - **Unresolved:** categories, detection/concurrency/harmonisation algorithms, Harmonisation Ergon catalogue, detailed work contracts and repeated-harmonisation terminal/escalation handling (CDG-46). No UI/forms architecture is selected. Kleio cross-target audit harmonisation remains R1.x/R2.x SEP.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Resource Harmonisation Manager — internal exceptional path. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
Mneme's **Resource Harmonisation Manager C40** identifies/manages resource-delivery conditions that cannot proceed normally and causes appropriate bounded harmonisation work to occur. It **does not itself perform domain harmonisation**. Conflicting, discordant, malformed or otherwise unsuitable resulting resource state may require specialised work; no exhaustive categories are established.
```text Mneme resulting resource delivery ├── Normal handling → Mnemosyne persistence as required └── Exceptional condition → Resource Harmonisation Manager → established Harmonia work/execution contract → Ponos execution → appropriate Harmonisation Ergon → resulting information returns to governed management ```
This is expected to represent **approximately 5% or less at worst of resource-delivery activity**, a design expectation **not a hard SLA**. The normal path SHALL remain efficient and SHALL NOT be unnecessarily burdened by expensive exceptional harmonisation processing.
Actual harmonisation SHALL occur through an appropriate **Harmonisation Ergon** using the common Harmonia execution architecture. It is **new governed work**; execution SHALL NOT resume inside the originating Ergon. The originating bounded activity is not made responsible for resolving generic resource conflicts.
Resource Harmonisation Manager SHALL reuse **Ponos execution capability through the established Harmonia work/execution contract**. It SHALL NOT duplicate, embed or assume Ponos execution-framework responsibilities or couple to its implementation internals. A reusable **Ergo Library** is retained only as a candidate reuse mechanism. No Iris, reusable forms or detailed UI architecture is established. Condition detection, harmonisation algorithms/catalogue, work-contract detail and terminal/escalation handling for repeated harmonisation remain unresolved. This path does not override Kleio's separately excluded R1.x/R2.x cross-target audit harmonisation.

Candidate Ergo Library only; CDG-46. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.

element.name: Request Service Assurance
element.documentation:
• Canonical Name: Request Service Assurance.
• Definition: Enables an authorised consumer to request that Service Assurance be performed for an applicable governed subject in accordance with an established Assurance Definition.
• Approved Consumers: Care Coordinator, Service Coordinator, Regulator, Policy Authority, System Steward.
• Associated Interaction: Service Assurance Request (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md#service-assurance-request), with Service Guardian and one authorised requesting Role.
• Process Relationship: Requests Assurance Process Execution (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md#assurance-process-execution) under an applicable established Assurance Definition. It does not require a new Assurance Process Design instance for each request.
• Independence Boundary: The requesting Role identifies the assurance need within its responsibility and authority. Requesting does not grant authority to define or alter the Assurance Definition, alter Assurance Criteria, direct evidence assessment, determine adjudication or control the resulting Assurance Finding / Conclusion. REQ-FND-005 control independence remains applicable, including where a requester performs or manages the subject. Detailed payloads, contracts, initiation mechanics and states remain unresolved.
---
## History
### Service Overview — predecessor explanation
This Service gives approved requesting roles a governed way to seek assurance within their authority. A request expresses the legitimate assurance need; it does not confer control over criteria, evidence assessment or adjudication. The requester can be involved in the subject while the required independence of the conclusion remains intact.
## Qualified relationship assertions
These source predicates retain their recorded standing and currentness. Their native mapping remains unestablished; they are not inferred ArchiMate edges. The complete original assertions and qualifications are retained in this element’s metadata.

It does not require a new Assurance Process Design instance for each request.

**Intent**
Establish and govern semantically meaningful health-information assets suitable for downstream research, population-health reporting and service planning in an adjacent analytical environment.
**Boundary**
Harmonia is adjacent to a Big Data/analytical environment. It establishes governed assets and reporting inputs; it does not become that analytical platform.

element.name: [CT3] Health Status Measurement
element.documentation:
Establish individual health observations or measurements.
Health Status Measurement establishes observations or measurements of an individual's health. Its contribution to assessment is evidence about the measured state, with a purpose distinct from developing a view over time or deciding the clinical meaning of a result. Measurements can inform both present assessment and later monitoring without collapsing those abilities.
**Boundary**
Obtaining a value does not establish a temporal trend or the clinical significance of that value.

element.name: [Feature] Appointment Status Synchronization
element.documentation:
Propagate booking cancellations, reschedules, and attendances across care coordination systems.
Status synchronisation keeps cancellation, rescheduling and attendance information coherent across coordination contexts. The purpose is propagation of the externally established booking change rather than independent scheduling or inference of a clinical outcome from appointment state.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Assessment
element.documentation:
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for clinical assessment services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Overview**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for clinical assessment services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Intent**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for clinical assessment services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Clinical Assessment is retained as an Adjacent Service Delivery context. It identifies the setting of assessment-related information needs without establishing a specialised Harmonia Feature set or replacing the Business Capability Individual Health Assessment. The distinction allows the catalogue to recognise clinical activity while keeping actual examination, interpretation and professional judgement outside the platform's assigned practice.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
No atomic Features are established. The contextual name does not make Harmonia a clinical assessor or establish BC ancestry.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
The Adjacent classification denotes contextual information participation rather than material execution of clinical assessment.

element.name: Assess Service Offering Readiness
element.documentation:
Evaluate applicable dependency evidence to establish a context- and time-qualified service readiness view.
**Overview**
Combines qualified dependency standing without converting missing evidence into ready or assuming that an available resource establishes deliverability.
**Boundary**
Resource ownership and clinical clearance remain external to this coordination.

element.name: [CT1] Care Context Integration Enablement
element.documentation:
Compose governed information and coordination behaviour for materially different care settings, continuity arrangements and specialist clinical purposes.
**Overview**
Emergency presentation, inpatient rounds and outreach visits need different contextual assemblies of the same underlying information. This frame retains those established setting-specific responsibilities as compositions rather than duplicate records or clinical execution authorities.
**Intent**
Give a care participant the appropriate information context for the particular integration purpose without duplicating general information responsibilities.
**Boundary**
Setting, care mode and specialty are overlapping contextual dimensions. These children are integration responsibilities, not a mutually exclusive taxonomy of patients or clinical care.

element.name: Governed Asynchronous Activity Progression
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Approach > **Progress multi-stage operational activities through explicit, observable unit-of-work transitions coordinated with entity state, separating execution from boundary exchange.**
Complex healthcare integrations (e.g., closed-loop diagnostic ordering, multi-destination clinical document fan-out) span multiple distributed systems and cannot rely on brittle synchronous distributed transactions. This course of action establishes that: - Work progresses through discrete, observable units of work whose lifecycle state transitions are explicitly tracked and auditable. - Operational progression progresses in lockstep with governed entity state (`AX-16`), preserving explicit uncertainty (`AX-15`) when external responses are pending or failed. - Execution progression is strictly decoupled from boundary transport and exchange mechanics: activity execution determines *that* an external interaction is needed, but does not own transport protocols or wire-level retries.
#### Motivational Grounding & Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: - `AX-10` (Distribution & Normal Failure): Systems fail normally; activity progression must be resilient, idempotent, and restartable. - `AX-15` (Preserve Uncertainty): Never assume success or failure; pending, timed-out, or ambiguous outcomes must be explicitly modeled. - `AX-16` (Activity & State Progress Together): Operational activity and managed information state advance in coordinated lockstep. - **Strategic Drivers & Goals**: Resilient Regional Integration, Asynchronous Clinical Decoupling, Bounded Workflow Recovery.
#### Capability Realisation & Configuration - **Primary Capabilities**: Shapes `EC-03` (Managed State & Lifecycle), `EC-09` (Event & Subscription), and `EC-10` (Activity & Execution). - **Component Boundary Impact**: Grounds the responsibility of **Ponos** as the execution engine for governed units of work, while strictly enforcing Guardrail G4 (Ponos progresses execution, but does not acquire transport adapters or wire protocols).
#### Downstream Direction (Domains 03–13) - Application Architecture (Domain 05) and Integration Architecture (Domain 06) realise governed work context, recoverable activity handoffs and explicit per-destination progression according to the applicable acceptance and delivery contracts (preserving Invariants 4 and 5). Established downstream constructs such as Pragma envelopes and Petasos messaging illustrate traceability; their APIs, queues, packaging and runtime mechanisms are not selected by this strategic responsibility.

element.name: Pragma Management
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** Mneme-associated information-management responsibility area with logical Aggregation of PragmaFactory C08 and Publishing C36, Subscription C37, Pattern C38 responsibilities, managing Pragma C07. [U02/U03/U05](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u05). Aggregation/management identifies responsibility, not Composition or a required process/service. - **Features/information:** creation/initialisation through PragmaFactory and governed management of Pragma representations and common process-management, assurance, reporting and platform integration associated with that information. Publishing/Subscription definitions, Pattern semantics/evaluation, matching, selection, semantic eligibility and eligible recipient/consumer relationships belong here; concrete persistent destination/handoff mechanics remain Petasos. Pragma expresses activity inputs/outputs; new Content is **Pragma Output**, distinct from changed Context working values. Mneme manages its subsequent consequences under [U10](../data-object/27ad143e7c784e378556af8a57c438f7.md). U18 distinguishes independently resulting Pragma from the Pathway-continuation role without transferring Praxis semantics or execution/routing to Mneme. Stimulus/Effector and candidate Dokimasia Pragma semantic roles reuse these facilities instead of requiring specialist equivalents. - **Persistence/collaboration:** active use/coordination through Mneme; authoritative durable establishment through Mnemosyne. Ponos executes, Petasos provides messaging/recoverable handoff and Ergon supplies bounded activity behaviour. - **Standing/exclusions:** candidate responsibility allocations established by U02/U03/U05; detailed management contracts and persistence structures remain unresolved. Execution of, behaviour upon, or handoff of managed information does not confer information-management responsibility for that information.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/pathways-journeys-and-handoff.md` — ## Dynamic information selection through Mneme. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
Defined Pathways and Publish/Subscribe are two distinct information-progression mechanisms. Pub/Sub does not require a predefined end-to-end Route or Pathway. Independent output-derived Pragma may enter this governed selection independently of the originating Praxis's [Pathway continuation](../data-object/27ad143e7c784e378556af8a57c438f7.md). Mneme / Pragma Management owns the logically aggregated responsibilities for **Publishing C36**, **Subscription C37** and **Pattern C38**. No separate deployment boundary is implied by these names.
| Construct / responsibility | Adjudicated meaning | | :--- | :--- | | **Publishing** | Governed provider-side eligibility/filtering: a provider may prevent egress Pragma from being made available through publication when its Pattern matches. It answers “What may leave / be made available by this provider?” | | **Subscription** | Governed consumer-side selection: a consumer requests that available Pragma matching a Pattern be made available/forwarded to its input queue or equivalent destination. It answers “What does this consumer want to receive?” | | **Pattern** | Common governed evaluation of characteristics associated with Pragma metadata, Information Unit Container and Content metadata, Topic, source and other established metadata. Final language, supported attributes/operators, precedence, query syntax, indexing and algorithms remain unresolved. | | **Mneme** | Manages definitions, Pattern semantics/evaluation, matching, selection and semantic eligibility; establishes eligible recipient/consumer relationships. | | **Petasos** | Establishes and manages the concrete persistent handoff obligation to the destination and reliably effects it; destination mechanics/state do not confer semantic selection responsibility. | | **Ponos** | Manages resulting execution and progression; subsequent execution does not confer Subscription matching responsibility. |
```mermaid flowchart TD E["Ergon EgressEndpoint"] --> PM["Mneme / Pragma Management"] PM --> P["Publishing: provider Pattern filter"] P --> B{"Blocked by matching Pattern?"} B -->|yes| X["Unavailable through publication"] B -->|no| S["Subscription: consumer Pattern selection"] S --> M{"Pattern matches?"} M -->|no| N["No handoff for this Subscription"] M -->|yes| D["Mneme determines semantic eligibility / eligible consumer"] D --> H["Petasos: concrete persistent handoff obligation to destination"] H --> Q["Consumer input queue / destination"] ```
Publishing and Subscription are deliberately asymmetric. Provider permission to publish does not require a consumer to be selected, and consumer interest does not override provider filtering or governed authorization. The diagram expresses those meanings, not an evaluation algorithm or transaction order. Themis governs applicable operations under established security context.
This Publishing mechanism concerns availability within Harmonia. An Ergon's EgressEndpoint does not itself end Harmonia management of the governed payload. Pylai's standards-facing external publication remains the separate AX-13 boundary, with non-destructive fail-closed projection of an emitted representation.
> **Mneme manages activity Context and Pragma, including governed semantic > selection, publication, subscription and availability. Execution of consuming > activities remains with Ponos.**
Internal Resource Harmonisation Manager may cause **new governed work** through the established work/execution contract and common Ponos execution; it does not execute harmonisation or embed a second framework. This refines the information/ execution seam without transferring handoff obligations from Petasos.

Resulting Pragma may play the continuation role or remain independently available for governed use | Mneme management distinct from Mnemosyne durable establishment; work/undertaking information remains O&A classification candidate; no automatic persistence of every field or continuation of every output | U10/U18 extend U01/U02/U06. No continuation subtype; construction/designation/representation CDG-53. Output/mapping contracts CDG-45; existing Task/representation CDG-02/03/10/12/13 preserved. |``. element.name: [CT2] Medication & Pharmacy Services
element.documentation:
Provide professional medication/pharmacy services under applicable controls.
This capability frames professional medication provision and medication-specific advice. Prescription dispensing, non-prescription provision, advice and dose administration aids answer different needs, even where exercised by one pharmacy. The decomposition keeps the authorised regimen, provision of medicine and actual administration separate so that a supply event is not mistaken for treatment performed.
**Intent**
Support safe, professionally controlled access to and use of medication within the established pharmacy responsibility.
**Boundary**
Advice does not confer prescribing authority, and dose aids do not establish a regimen. Whether specialised compounding/preparation warrants a separate capability remains unresolved under OI-BC-001.
## Qualified relationship assertions
These source predicates retain their recorded standing and currentness. Their native mapping remains unestablished; they are not inferred ArchiMate edges. The complete original assertions and qualifications are retained in this element’s metadata.

element.name: [Feature] Durable Clinical Record Preservation
element.documentation:
Durably maintain governed, vendor-neutral longitudinal clinical representation and preservation with verifiable integrity controls.
Durable preservation retains the governed longitudinal representation and the history of what Harmonia received or managed. Corrections establish changed knowledge without retrospectively rewriting that history, and preservation neither originates clinical facts nor automatically establishes legal qualification of the record.

element.name: [Feature] Mobile Service Capacity Management
element.documentation:
Represent mobile service capacity with travel, coverage, work commitment and availability context.
**Overview**
Mobile availability cannot be interpreted as a simple on-duty count because distance, assignments and suitable skills affect deliverability.
**Boundary**
Local responsibility retains its capacity meaning; Service Capacity Management consumes it without acquiring ownership or imposing one common capacity model.

element.name: [CT2] Care Access Management
element.documentation:
Establish and manage access to applicable care.
Care Access Management establishes the circumstances in which an individual seeks or enters care. Intake creates the access context, referral requests another participant's involvement, and eligibility determines whether applicable access conditions are met. These are separate contributions to access: a person can be eligible without having a booking, and a received referral can remain undecided.
**Intent**
Make entry requirements and referral disposition intelligible without implying that care has already been accepted or delivered.
**Boundary**
Eligibility does not allocate care, and referral receipt does not establish an assumption of clinical responsibility.

element.name: Manage Mobile Service Capacity
element.documentation:
Understands and manages available, committed and utilised mobile-service capacity in relation to workforce availability, geography, time, workload and applicable service demand.
Responsibility boundary: Staff presence and externally established assignments/visit progression contribute to capacity; they do not alone express it. Capacity coordination does not determine clinical work, own the source workforce roster or allocate underlying clinical duties.

element.name: [CT3] Authority & Constraint Governance
element.documentation:
Establish who may make, approve or govern organisational decisions/artefacts and the bounds within which authority may be exercised.
This capability establishes who may make or approve organisational decisions and the bounds within which that authority applies. It complements obligation governance by distinguishing required outcomes from legitimate decision powers. A participant can therefore be responsible for acting within constraints without being authorised to redefine the governing requirement.
**Boundary**
Authority allocation does not itself perform an operational decision or a runtime access-control evaluation.

element.name: [CT3] Health Innovation Evaluation
element.documentation:
Evaluate proposed/emerging innovation for suitability, value, implications and potential adoption.
Health Innovation Evaluation is the organisation's ability to form a considered view of a proposed or emerging innovation before treating it as suitable for use. Within Health Innovation it brings suitability, value and implications into the same evaluative context, so that potential benefit can be considered alongside consequences for the health-service or clinical setting. The outcome supports informed consideration of adoption rather than making adoption inevitable.
**Intent**
Give decision makers an intelligible basis for considering whether an innovation merits further adoption consideration.
**Boundary**
Evaluation does not establish adoption, authorise a clinical change or create an implementation responsibility. The single established child does not imply a complete innovation lifecycle.

element.name: [CT2] Referral Administration
element.documentation:
Referral Administration receives referral material, associates the supporting clinical context and tracks the recipient's explicit disposition and outcome. Its purpose is to keep the request and its progression intelligible across care boundaries. It distinguishes a request for another participant's involvement from an order for bounded fulfilment and from actual acceptance of care responsibility.
**Overview**
Referral Administration receives referral material, associates the supporting clinical context and tracks the recipient's explicit disposition and outcome. Its purpose is to keep the request and its progression intelligible across care boundaries. It distinguishes a request for another participant's involvement from an order for bounded fulfilment and from actual acceptance of care responsibility.
**Intent**
Referral Administration receives referral material, associates the supporting clinical context and tracks the recipient's explicit disposition and outcome. Its purpose is to keep the request and its progression intelligible across care boundaries. It distinguishes a request for another participant's involvement from an order for bounded fulfilment and from actual acceptance of care responsibility.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Transport acceptance does not establish clinical acceptance. A referral need not universally produce an appointment, encounter, order or transfer of care.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Harmonia materially connects the referral, supporting information and reported disposition while the receiving service retains clinical and responsibility decisions.

element.name: [CT3] Diagnostic Data Management
element.documentation:
Manage acquired or produced diagnostic evidence as information, including identity, association, integrity, organisation, availability and lifecycle.
Diagnostic Data Management maintains acquired or produced diagnostic evidence as usable information. Its responsibility includes identity, association, integrity, organisation and lifecycle so that evidence can be found and understood in the right diagnostic context. It addresses the evidence record independently of the professional conclusion subsequently drawn from it.
**Boundary**
Managing diagnostic data neither interprets that data nor governs the authoritative expression of findings in a report.

element.name: Assurance Process Design
element.documentation:
• Canonical Name: Assurance Process Design.
• Owning Capability: Assurance Design (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#assurance-design).
• Process Purpose: Establishes and maintains how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be assured.
• Principal Performing Role: Service Assurance Modeller (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md#service-assurance-modeller).
• Participating Functions: Design Service Assurance (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#design-service-assurance) and Manage Assurance Criteria (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#manage-assurance-criteria). Manage Assurance Criteria retains ownership within Assurance Criteria Management; its participation does not subsume that Capability's criteria lifecycle or transfer its information responsibility to Assurance Design.
• Conceptual Output: Assurance Definition (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#42-assurance-definition--conceptual-modelling-output), retaining its conceptual Business Architecture output/boundary treatment.
• Boundary: Governance Authority establishes what is authoritative. Design does not grant Service Assurance Modeller approval authority. Detailed Assurance Definition lifecycle, approval/publication workflows, criteria lifecycle and information modelling remain unresolved. Participation of the two Functions does not establish a cross-capability lifecycle or a new exchange/Service between their owners.
Assurance design establishes a reusable basis for how satisfaction will be evaluated, rather than running the evaluation itself. Criteria-management participation retains its separate owner and does not create an exchange Service or a shared criteria lifecycle. An Assurance Definition can be reused, so each execution need not imply a freshly performed Design Process.

element.name: Practitioner Collaboration
element.documentation: - **Purpose**: Governs professional peer-to-peer clinical engagement, informal secondary consultations, multidisciplinary review panels, and clinical knowledge sharing across practitioner networks. - **Participating Roles**: `Practitioner`, `Clinician`, `Care Coordinator`, `Terminology Steward`. - **Governed Activities**: Peer review, diagnostic consultation, case conferencing, and shared clinical governance discussions.

element.name: Continuous and Resilient Regional Health Information Exchange (O2)
element.documentation:
### Outcome Definition Regional healthcare facilities operate within an uninterrupted, highly available, and fault-tolerant digital integration fabric that reliably exchanges clinical events across heterogeneous systems without data loss or performance degradation.
### Clinical & Operational Value - **Zero Silent Data Loss**: Admission notifications, emergency referrals, and diagnostic alerts are guaranteed to cross durable boundaries before positive transport acknowledgement, ensuring that integration failures never result in dropped clinical events. - **High Concurrency & Responsiveness**: Point-of-care clinical queries and vital notification streams remain highly responsive, unblocked by background batch synchronization or database transaction locks. - **Coordinated Inter-Facility Workflows**: Multi-stage clinical activities (e.g., patient transfers, regional lab dispatch, pharmacy updates) progress deterministically across multiple destination systems, preventing divergence of clinical state between facilities. - **Seamless Standards Interoperability**: Seamless bridging of legacy HL7 v2 systems and modern FHIR RESTful repositories without expensive, disruptive rip-and-replace software upgrades.
### Direct Contributing Goals - [Vendor-Independent Longitudinal Clinical Information Coherence](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 1) - [Durable Acceptance and Preservation of Clinical Events](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 3) - [Responsive Access to Managed Information](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 4) - [Coordinated Progression of Operational Activities and Associated Entity State](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) (Thread 7)

element.name: [Feature] Information Standards & Semantic Governance
element.documentation:
Govern canonical clinical data definitions, terminology bindings, and exchange profiles across regional systems.
Semantic governance provides canonical definitions, bindings and profiles through which regional representations can be understood consistently. Its purpose concerns meaning and constraints rather than a particular schema technology, and consuming a definition does not transfer its governing authority.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Charging & Claims Administration
element.documentation:
This capability supplies clinical activity summaries and charging records to billing contexts. It preserves a route from activity information to the systems responsible for financial processing without treating the export as a completed bill or claim. No Feature decomposition or comprehensive revenue-cycle responsibility is established.
**Overview**
This capability supplies clinical activity summaries and charging records to billing contexts. It preserves a route from activity information to the systems responsible for financial processing without treating the export as a completed bill or claim. No Feature decomposition or comprehensive revenue-cycle responsibility is established.
**Intent**
This capability supplies clinical activity summaries and charging records to billing contexts. It preserves a route from activity information to the systems responsible for financial processing without treating the export as a completed bill or claim. No Feature decomposition or comprehensive revenue-cycle responsibility is established.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Export of activity evidence does not confer pricing, billing, claim or accounting authority.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Its Adjacent standing reflects information supplied to financial systems while the financial activity remains externally governed.

element.name: [CT1] Health Service Operations Enablement
element.documentation:
Enable health-service operations through information about flow, care-places, capacity, workforce capability, operational work, logistics and discharge progression.
**Overview**
Enable health-service operations through information about flow, care-places, capacity, workforce capability, operational work, logistics and discharge progression.
**Intent**
Enable health-service operations through information about flow, care-places, capacity, workforce capability, operational work, logistics and discharge progression.
**Boundary**
Coordination owns only explicitly assigned operational activity. It does not originate clinical clearance, determine clinical work or take workforce and resource governance from their sources.

element.name: [CT2] On-Call Management
element.documentation:
On-Call Management resolves the active provider for a specialty, service or hospital at the relevant time. It turns changing coverage information into usable routing context so that operational communication can reach the intended capacity. This differs from authoring the roster or deciding who is professionally qualified for the requested activity.
**Overview**
On-Call Management resolves the active provider for a specialty, service or hospital at the relevant time. It turns changing coverage information into usable routing context so that operational communication can reach the intended capacity. This differs from authoring the roster or deciding who is professionally qualified for the requested activity.
**Intent**
On-Call Management resolves the active provider for a specialty, service or hospital at the relevant time. It turns changing coverage information into usable routing context so that operational communication can reach the intended capacity. This differs from authoring the roster or deciding who is professionally qualified for the requested activity.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Being on call does not by itself establish clinical privilege or assignment of a particular care responsibility.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Current provider resolution materially enables appropriate contact and routing across operational boundaries.

element.name: [CT2] Health Information Standards Governance
element.documentation:
Govern organisational adoption and use of health-information models and applicable standards.
This capability governs which information models and standards the organisation adopts and how their use is supported and evaluated. The model distinguishes discovering candidates, adopting models, educating users, addressing conformity and overseeing governance. Standards impact identification has a separate established place because its implications may extend into clinical practice, policy and obligations beyond information-system implementation.
**Intent**
Make organisational standards use deliberate and its consequences understandable.
**Boundary**
Oversight evaluates governance without performing every peer activity. Adoption includes its own model-impact consideration; the listed abilities do not establish a sequential adoption Process.
## Qualified relationship assertions

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Continuous Improvement
element.documentation:
Evaluate the established service and identify correction/improvement needs that may feed back into modelling and implementation support.
This capability evaluates an established service and identifies correction or improvement needs across its service-wide purpose. It allows experience of actual operation to inform reconsideration of the service model and implementation support. The scope is broader than reporting a clinical-quality finding, while remaining anchored to the service being improved.
**Boundary**
It does not establish generic Continuous Improvement placement or transfer the authority of specialist activities affected by improvement.

element.name: [CT1] Community Health & Wellbeing
element.documentation:
Support community health and wellbeing, including the bounded preventative-health abilities required for R1/R2. Wider environmental health, outreach and social determinants remain enterprise context without inferred additional decomposition.
Community Health & Wellbeing frames organised activity supporting health beyond a single person's episode of care. The governed decomposition focuses on preventative health: identifying needs, defining programmes and cohorts, educating, observing programme operation and reporting. Wider outreach, environmental and social-determinant concerns remain enterprise context rather than additional modelled children.
**Intent**
Support organised prevention with a clear relationship between the health problem, intended population and programme activity.
**Boundary**
Programme management does not acquire the clinical or appointment responsibilities needed to deliver a programme.
**Harmonia Architectural Relevance**
Programme and cohort distinctions materially shape the information, notifications and care enablement required. This supports the Relevant classification without assigning wider public-health operating authority to Harmonia.

element.name: [CT2] Clinical Communication Administration
element.documentation:
This capability manages secure clinical communication transactions, delivery and receipt evidence, and the required enduring audit trail. Verified provider and team endpoints support appropriate addressing while transaction correlation makes the communication history intelligible. The responsibility preserves separate meanings for transport delivery, recipient acknowledgement and clinical or business disposition.
**Overview**
This capability manages secure clinical communication transactions, delivery and receipt evidence, and the required enduring audit trail. Verified provider and team endpoints support appropriate addressing while transaction correlation makes the communication history intelligible. The responsibility preserves separate meanings for transport delivery, recipient acknowledgement and clinical or business disposition.
**Intent**
This capability manages secure clinical communication transactions, delivery and receipt evidence, and the required enduring audit trail. Verified provider and team endpoints support appropriate addressing while transaction correlation makes the communication history intelligible. The responsibility preserves separate meanings for transport delivery, recipient acknowledgement and clinical or business disposition.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Delivery or read receipts do not prove clinical review, incorporation, approval or acceptance. Audit evidence must remain governed without unmasked PHI in diagnostic streams.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Secure addressed communication and attributable transaction evidence are substantive platform responsibilities.

element.name: [CT2] Governance Framework Management
element.documentation:
Establish the authoritative WHAT and legitimate working parameters.
Governance Framework Management establishes what must be satisfied and the legitimate authority and bounds for organisational decisions. Its two children separate obligations attributable to source authority from the allocation and limitation of decision authority. Together they supply the authoritative reference against which operational arrangements and compliance assessments can be considered.
**Intent**
Keep required outcomes and legitimate decision parameters distinguishable and traceable to their authority.
**Boundary**
Interpreting an external obligation or engaging with a regulator does not transfer that body's authority. Operational means remain with management.

element.name: Coordinated Operational Activity and Entity State
element.documentation:
### Context & Pressure Healthcare integration is rarely a simple point-to-point message transmission. A single real-world clinical event—such as a patient admission or an emergency department transfer—triggers a cascade of multi-stage operational activities across multiple downstream systems (e.g., notifying pharmacy, updating bed management, triggering pre-admission lab orders, broadcasting HL7 ADT messages to billing and clinical portals).
When integration middleware treats these complex interactions simply as a stream of disconnected, fire-and-forget messages, failures in downstream destinations cause silent state divergence. The hospital's billing system may record the patient as discharged while the pharmacy continues dispensing medication.
### Architectural Imperative Harmonia must coordinate multi-stage operational activity in lockstep with the governed state of the real-world clinical entity. Activities must progress through explicit, observable state transitions, ensuring that fan-out status, acknowledgements, and retry progressions are fully trackable and recoverable.
- **Primary Stakeholders**: [Healthcare Delivery Organizations](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md), [Platform Operations & Integration Engineers](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/stakeholders/enterprise-stakeholders.md) - **Key Assessment**: [Unmonitored Destination Failure / Fan-Out Divergence](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md) - **Associated Goal**: [Coordinated Progression of Operational Activities & Associated Entity State](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/goals-outcomes/strategic-goals.md) - **Governing Axiom**: [AX-16 (Operational Activity & Entity State Progress Together)](../principle/de7e90f46127455a9ec9ad3b9b48ba54.md)

element.name: [Feature] Addressed Clinical Distribution
element.documentation:
Fan out clinical events and diagnostic reports to designated external and internal recipients with per-destination delivery tracking.
Addressed distribution sends information to explicitly designated recipients and tracks each destination's delivery separately. This preserves partial outcomes in a fan-out rather than collapsing several deliveries into a single success that hides a missing recipient.

element.name: [CT2] Therapeutic Services
element.documentation:
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for therapeutic services services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Overview**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for therapeutic services services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Intent**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for therapeutic services services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Therapeutic Services is retained as an Adjacent clinical delivery context, recognising care activity whose information may concern Harmonia without assigning treatment performance to it. The current model establishes no atomic Features for this context. The broad label is not used to invent therapy-specific Functions or reclassify clinical interventions as platform execution.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Information participation does not confer authority to select, perform or assess the clinical adequacy of therapy.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Adjacent standing preserves the contextual role while treatment remains the responsible service's activity.

element.name: Ponos
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** reusable execution framework/component pattern, peer to Energeia C39, for governed execution and observable activity progression. [U02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u02) adjudicates this role; [A02](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#a02) and [L02/L01/L23](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#l02) retain responsibility context and historical detail. - **Features/contained constructs:** work ingress and dispatcher, workflow/sequence resolution where governed control is established, activity invocation, execution concurrency/timeouts, execution retry/re-attempts, checkpoint coordination and administrative inspection. Applies Praxis-defined output-processing/continuation semantics and routing; not every output-derived Pragma continues that Praxis. [U18](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u18) establishes the distinction, leaving representation open. Subscription matching belongs to Mneme; handoff redelivery/recovery and dead-letter semantics belong to Petasos. Consumer loops/thread pools are documented mechanisms, not logical children. Ordinary semantic interest fan-out to different Ergon types is orthogonal to ActionableTask.ExecutionConcurrency permitting concurrent undertakings by instances of the same type, each through its own FulfillmentTask. DigitalTwin specialises execution with serial Behaviour processing within a Twin; common concurrency facilities do not permit intra-Twin Behaviour concurrency (U19). - **Information:** executes consumer undertakings using governed information/context resolved through Mneme; consults established control definitions and produces execution/progression observations contributing to Journey. Petasos handoff does not make an opaque payload into a Ponos-owned Pragma. - **Persistence:** coordinates recoverable handoff through Petasos and governed information change through Mneme/Mnemosyne. Does not establish durable state by completing an activity or writing a checkpoint to a cache. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** tightly coupled to peer Ergo/Ergon responsibilities, executing/managing bounded Ergon activity conforming to the Ergo contract; does not structurally contain Ergo or Ergon. Uses Praxis, Erga, Themis, Mneme Pragma Management and Petasos. DigitalTwin C19 and Dokimasia C20 specialise/ reuse this pattern; they are not children inside a Ponos runtime. Conceptual supertype language does not mandate literal implementation inheritance. Does not own Pragma information management, Publishing/Subscription/Pattern semantic selection, workflow definitions, concrete domain logic, broker lifecycle, external standards/transport or universal clinical-work determination. - **Standing:** specialisation relationships adjudicated for the candidate by U02; detailed model remains candidate. CDG-03/08/16–18 retain incomplete control and continuation semantics. Numerical worker/retry defaults are not baselined.

Mneme selects information; Petasos establishes concrete handoff; Ponos executes using Praxis without owning it. Detailed control contracts CDG-01/03/16 remain open. |``. element.name: [Feature] Active On-Call Provider Resolution
element.documentation:
Resolve currently active on-call specialists, registrars, and operational managers for a given specialty and hospital at any point in time.
Active on-call resolution identifies the current provider in the required specialty and hospital context. It supports correct routing at the relevant time without authoring the roster or treating current coverage as proof of qualification, privilege or responsibility acceptance.

element.name: Criterion
element.documentation:
A Criterion represents a **governed permitted combination** across applicable dimensions, using [Calliope-controlled nomenclature](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-nomenclature):
```text Criterion = Information.Compartment AND Information.Classification AND Function.Name AND Function.Scope AND applicable Temporal constraints ```
The four principal dimensions describe **what** is authorised; applicable temporal constraints describe **when**. Within an individual Criterion, applicable dimensions are **conjunctive**. Between Criteria, grants are **additive / UNION**: each Criterion independently contributes its permitted combination. Only explicitly governed combinations have authorisation meaning. Absence of a matching effective Criterion results in **DENY**.
**Explicit negative/DENY Criteria are not part of this Candidate Architecture.** Neither arbitrary Boolean policy expressions, deny-overrides semantics nor a general-purpose policy language is introduced by this model.

element.name: [CT2] Care Access Transaction Enablement
element.documentation:
Coordinate the intake, care-request disposition and appointment information through which a person accesses care.
**Overview**
Coordinate the intake, care-request disposition and appointment information through which a person accesses care. Its constituent abilities distinguish Client-Centred Administration; Referral Administration; Scheduling Administration.
**Intent**
Make an access request and its disposition traceable without confusing a booking with care responsibility or delivery.
**Boundary**
A referral requests care responsibility; an appointment concerns a booking. Neither establishes care delivery or host booking authority.

element.name: [BusinessObject] Search Result Set
element.documentation:
> **A search over Harmonia-managed information produces a governed > metadata-based Search Result Set referencing the Information Unit Versions > comprising that result. Search does not, by itself, duplicate or create new > versions of the returned managed information.**
**Search Result Set** names this managed metadata collection. It specialises the established [Collection meaning](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#21-semantic-classifications) and [membership distinction](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/containment-and-collections.md#3-collections-vs-containment-distinct-semantics) through search-specific Version-reference membership. It introduces no new semantic category or Information Concept-to-Information Unit equivalence. “Search Result Metadata-Set” describes the same concept rather than an additional concept or representation.
Management attaches to the result set's own governed search/result metadata and membership within its Information Unit boundary. The referenced Information Units / Versions retain their existing management boundaries, authority and history. Creating the result artefact SHALL NOT create copies of the returned Units, new Versions of those Units, a BLOB of duplicated managed information, or another authority for that information.
```text Harmonia-Managed Information | | search v Search Result Set (managed metadata collection) | +-- Search / Result Metadata | +-- Result Membership [0..*] | +-- Information Unit Version Reference ```
### 2.1 Information Unit Version Membership
Membership records the applicable **Information Unit Version**, expressing:
> **These were the managed Information Unit Versions comprising the result > of this search.**
It SHALL NOT resolve later to whichever Active Generation or current Version happens to exist when the result set is examined. For example, membership identifying Unit U's Version V7 continues to identify V7 after U progresses to V8 or has a different active manifestation. These labels establish no identifier scheme. The [closed Version / Active Generation semantics](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/metamodel/information-architecture-metamodel.md#651-version-and-active-generation) remain unchanged.
The set contains membership references, not copies of member content. The conceptual `0..*` membership permits an empty result. It establishes neither a reference encoding nor downstream retrieval, retention or manifestation mechanics, and implies no universal atomic observation of all members.
### 2.2 Search / Result Metadata
The set SHALL contain sufficient metadata to represent the search and its result as a governed information artefact. Semantic categories may include search context, search criteria, execution/result time, result-set identity, result membership and other metadata necessary to establish the governed meaning of the result.
These categories are not a complete metadata schema, mandatory field list, datatype or serialization. They prescribe no database, API or cache structure. Search context does not automatically persist operational security context as resource content; AX-07 remains applicable.
### 2.3 Search and Separate Self-Contained Artefacts
Version-specific membership preserves the meaning of a search result; it does not make ordinary search a generic snapshot mechanism. The Search Result Set is not a self-contained duplicated parcel of the referenced content.
Export, snapshot, document generation, archival package, transmission package or another self-contained information artefact requires a separate semantic act/capability. Such acts are not intrinsic to search and are not designed here. The existing [Assembly/View and snapshot distinctions](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/assemblies-views/assemblies-and-views.md#3-assembly-lifecycle-vs-constituent-lifecycle) remain applicable without an automatic Search Result Set-to-Assembly mapping.
Source standing: Adjudicated conceptual managed metadata collection; Search Result Metadata-Set is the same concept, not an additional element.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 1. Authority and Two Search Cases. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
The authorised 2026-10-10 search adjudication distinguishes:
1. **Harmonia-Managed Information Search** over existing managed Information Units / Information Unit Versions. 2. **External Information Search** intentionally performed as part of an Ergo activity.
These cases have different management semantics. A generic transition from observed information to accepted management SHALL NOT replace this distinction. The [Harmonia-managed information definition and Information Unit boundary](10284034c8534b639284386b064f2c54.md) continue to govern. Management responsibility remains distinct from originating information authority and authority over the underlying domain activity.
The established upstream responsibilities are [Search & Discovery (EC-05)](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/enterprise-capabilities.md#ec-05-search--discovery), [retrieval mediation and governed query/search (FEAT-ISE-05/08/09)](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#detailed-capability--feature-catalogue-intrinsic--shared-enablement), and Business [Health Information Exchange](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/05-intrinsic-enablement.md#22-health-information-exchange-hie) and [Health Information Access](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/05-intrinsic-enablement.md#23-health-information-access). The [Business ownership matrix](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/information-responsibility/information-responsibility.md#2-canonical-business-information-ownership-matrix) establishes Query Execution Context & Projection State without ownership of queried source records. Those sources establish search purpose and responsibility; the two-case management boundary below is the explicit Domain04 adjudication, not a claim that the upstream sources already specified result membership.
[AX-04](../../motivation/principle/54508cda80484a6caf95b901780eaf7d.md) preserves semantic authority independently of machinery; [AX-05](../../motivation/principle/0412a2084f0145babc4f022c71fea65f.md) preserves active/durable state distinctions; [AX-06](../../motivation/principle/952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md) and [AX-18](../../motivation/principle/b8cafe3cf5904d2bb9a9767260fddf78.md) preserve source and domain authority. [AX-07–09](../../motivation/principle/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) govern security context and meaningful evidence; [AX-13](../../motivation/principle/b6a55decfeec4f1bb3d7f18534a2ffea.md) preserves the external management boundary; [AX-14](../../motivation/principle/d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) and [AX-17](../../motivation/principle/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) preserve the distinctions and explicitly unestablished details below. No new axiom is required.
## Source-qualified contribution

## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 4. Search Result Information and Audit / Assurance. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
The Search Result Set establishes which managed Information Unit Versions comprised a search result. Audit / Assurance information may establish other meaning: requester/actor, applicable authority, access/control decisions, disclosure, operational evidence or assurance conclusions. These meanings SHALL remain distinct.
```text External Consumer | v Pylai | +----> Audit / Assurance information (according to policy) | v Harmonia-Managed Information Search | v Search Result Set ```
Overlapping metadata or references are legitimate; correlation does not make these artefacts equivalent and does not require eliminating the overlap. The result set SHALL NOT be collapsed into Audit / Assurance evidence. Its possible contextual evidentiary use does not redefine its information meaning or make every search operation audit evidence. Detailed Audit / Assurance semantics remain outside this adjudication.
An externally published search response remains governed by its applicable interoperability contract. AX-13 terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation, while internally retained managed information remains governed. This conceptual result set prescribes no external envelope or response format.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/patterns/search-results.md` — ## 5. Resolution and Retained Boundaries. Standing: Adjudicated search boundary; exact source qualifications retained.
This two-case adjudication resolves the former generic search-management question retained in the metamodel and Assembly/View guidance. It establishes the managed metadata result boundary and governed external acquisition without a generic management-acceptance transition.
Search APIs, indexing, pagination, result encoding, reference realization, cache/persistence structures, component allocation and manifestation mechanics remain downstream concerns. Result metadata detail, retention and separate snapshot/export capabilities are not designed here. Existing explicit TaskOutcome detail, ReportedTask, candidate-family and Audit / Assurance deferrals retain their standing under AX-17. This bounded decision does not declare Domain04 complete or authorise Domain05 derivation.

element.name: [Feature] Mandatory Significant Activity Audit Capture
element.documentation:
Capture required significant activity evidence using the specifically governed authoritative audit-capture boundary.
**Overview**
The actor whose action is recorded need not be entitled to persist the audit. Required capture uses its own established authority and failure can block the governed operation.
**Boundary**
Specific audit authority is not borrowed from the audited identity or generalised to other operations.
