element.name: [BusinessObject] Information Assertion
element.documentation:
In healthcare integration, clinical and demographic facts are rarely absolute, detached truths. Rather, they are statements made by specific practitioners, diagnostic systems, administrative staff, or patients at specific points in time. > **Information Assertion**: A formal statement about an entity, relationship, activity, event, or circumstance made by an identifiable source within a qualified context. ```mermaid graph TD AST["Information Assertion"] AST -->|"asserted by"| AUTH["1. Information Authority
(Clinician, Lab, System, Patient)"] AST -->|"governed by"| RESP["2. Information Responsibility
(Owning Domain 03 Capability)"] AST -->|"held / transported by"| CUST["3. Information Custody
(Host Node, Repository, Gateway)"] AST -->|"accessed by"| CONS["4. Information Consumption
(Dashboard, Workflow, Analytics)"] AST -->|"contextualised by"| QUAL["5. Qualification & Context
(Verification State, Confidence, Evidence)"] AST -->|"evidenced by"| PROV["6. Provenance & Lineage
(Time, Method, Originating Transaction)"] ``` ### Pragmatic Assertion Modelling While the assertion concept provides rigorous semantic governance, **Domain 04 does not require every single atomic attribute to be modeled as a distinct, reified Assertion object**. - Where a fact carries its own independent legal liability, clinical attestation, or disputed confidence (e.g. an *Allergy Intolerance Finding*, a *Diagnostic Pathology Finding*, or a *Death Notification*), it is explicitly governed as an Assertion. - Where attributes form an indivisible, cohesive demographic or descriptive unit asserted under a single common authority (e.g. standard address elements on a profile), they are governed collectively under the parent concept. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/authority-custody-provenance.md` — ## 2. The Four Pillars of Information Governance. Standing: Canonical information governance; originating authority preserved. Harmonia enforces strict separation across four distinct governance dimensions: ```text Information Responsibility ≠ Information Authority ≠ Information Custody ≠ Information Consumption ``` | Governance Dimension | Definition | Owning Context | Key Architectural Guardrails | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Information Responsibility** | Architectural ownership, semantic definition, and lifecycle governance of an information asset. | Derived strictly from **Domain 03 Capability responsibility**. | Non-transferable. Transits, queries, or presentations never shift responsibility. Architectural responsibility is distinct from the `Information Steward` role. | | **Information Authority** | The legal, clinical, professional, or organisational actor that authoritatively makes, signs, or attests to a specific assertion or relationship. | The **asserting/attesting legal entity, clinician, or registered system**. | May attach at granular assertion and relationship levels. | | **Information Custody** | The operational holding, durable persistence, caching, or physical storage of information instances. | The **Harmonia subsystem, database node, or cache cluster** hosting the data. | Custody implies security and preservation obligations, never semantic ownership. | | **Information Consumption** | The reading, querying, evaluating, aggregating, or rendering of information by a consuming service or user. | The **consuming Capability, presentation tier, or external subscriber**. | Consumption grants no authority to alter originating facts or re-author source semantics. | ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/authority-custody-provenance.md` — ## 3. Granular Assertion-Level and Relationship-Level Authority. Standing: Canonical information governance; originating authority preserved. A major limitation of traditional health informatics models is assigning authority exclusively at the composite document or aggregate record level. In a regional integration environment, a patient's **Longitudinal Health Record** or **Encounter Summary** is an aggregated composite containing clinical assertions and relationships originating from dozens of distinct authorities: - An attending general practitioner asserts a chronic condition (*Type 2 Diabetes*). - An independent pathology laboratory asserts an abnormal blood glucose result. - An emergency physician refutes a previously suspected drug allergy. - A patient asserts an OTC herbal supplement intake. ```mermaid graph TD LHR["Longitudinal Health Record (Composite Assembly)"] LHR --> A1["Assertion 1: Chronic Diabetes
Authority: Dr Jane Doe (GP Clinic)"] LHR --> A2["Assertion 2: Fasting Blood Glucose
Authority: Regional Pathology Lab"] LHR --> A3["Assertion 3: Penicillin Allergy Refutation
Authority: Dr John Smith (ED Specialist)"] LHR --> A4["Assertion 4: Herbal Supplement Use
Authority: Healthcare Subject (Self-Reported)"] ``` ### Core Invariant > **Information Authority SHALL be capable of attaching directly to individual assertions and relationships rather than requiring an entire composite object to share a single monolithic authority.** ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/authority-custody-provenance.md` — ## 4. Provenance & Lineage Framework. Standing: Canonical information governance; originating authority preserved. Provenance describes where/how governed information arose, its derivation and its relationship to originating assertions, activities and requests. Provenance / derivation ≠ Audit Evidence ≠ Assurance Evidence. Kleio retains audit information responsibility and Dokimasia retains assurance responsibility; derivation does not transfer either responsibility or automatically make transient mechanics durable evidence (AX-08/09). The [Metabolē progression pattern](c34b4929f71946708d37dbe6c1da920a.md) applies this distinction to accumulated information without creating another evidence manager. ### 4.1 Provenance Scope Provenance attaches to: - **Assertions**: Who asserted what fact, based on what diagnostic or observational evidence, at what recorded timestamp. - **Relationships**: Who created, confirmed, or severed an association between concepts. - **Corrections & Retractions**: The authorising party, rationale, and timestamp for an erratum or status refutation. - **Transformations & Derivations**: The algorithm, translation map, or synthetic rule that derived a secondary concept from source inputs. - **Fulfilments & Outcomes**: The performing practitioner and device recording a clinical delivery or result. - **Assemblies**: The assembly definition, generating system, and snapshot timestamp of a composite view. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/governance/authority-custody-provenance.md` — ## 5. Semantic Qualification Dimensions. Standing: Canonical information governance; originating authority preserved. An Information Assertion or Relationship may be qualified across several semantic dimensions: 1. **Verification State**: The epistemic certainty of the assertion (*Confirmed*, *Provisional*, *Refuted*, *Entered-in-Error*). 2. **Confidence / Epistemic Strength**: The degree of clinical or algorithmic confidence (*Definite*, *Probable*, *Suspected*, *Uncertain*). 3. **Quality & Completeness Assessment**: Metadata assessing source record completeness, calibration status, or image resolution. 4. **Evidentiary Basis / Reason**: The diagnostic test, clinical observation, legal certificate, or patient report providing the foundation for the assertion. 5. **Qualifying Authority**: The credentialed supervisor or secondary sign-off authority validating the assertion. 6. **Effective Context**: Clinical setting or situational bounds under which the assertion applies (e.g. *Post-Operative Recovery*, *Fasting State*).

element.name: [CT3] Assurance Evaluation Criteria Governance
element.documentation:
Establish and maintain criteria against which sufficient assurance can be determined.
This capability establishes and maintains the criteria against which assurance sufficiency is judged. It makes the evaluative basis of confidence explicit across the different concerns that can affect service delivery. Criteria can draw on clinical, workforce, technology, information or other contexts without turning those subjects into independent assurance capability trees.
**Boundary**
Criteria governance is distinct from applying criteria to evidence and does not remap the existing assurance BEC responsibilities.

element.documentation:

Patient Movement Coordination concerns the person's physical transit and the mobility constraints relevant to it. element.name: Entity-Centred Operational Coordination
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Approach > **Coordinate governed information, state and operational activity around real-world healthcare entities where those entities are operationally significant in their own right and require active management, without requiring every managed entity to maintain a permanently active execution construct.**
Healthcare operations naturally center around authentic real-world entities: patients, practitioners, care teams, wards, and beds. This course of action establishes that: - Harmonia organizes the coordination of state and ongoing activities around the operational identity of the real-world entity itself. - **The Digital Twin is the architectural construct** through which this entity-centred coordination strategy is realised. A Twin coordinates information, state, and activity across the Mneme/Ponos seam for a specific real-world entity. - **Demand-Driven Lifecycle**: A managed entity does not require a permanently running execution thread or process. Twins are activated when entity-centred operational activity or active monitoring is required, and become quiescent when work concludes. - **Representation $\neq$ Twin**: Simply possessing a database record or FHIR resource does not justify or constitute a Digital Twin. Coordination is justified only when the entity is operationally active and evolving in state.
#### Motivational Grounding & Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: - `AX-01` (Health-Information Centric): Architecture aligns with genuine healthcare entities and clinical relationships. - `AX-11` (High Availability & Responsiveness): High concurrency is achieved by isolating entity coordination without central serialisation bottlenecks. - `AX-16` (Activity & State Progress Together): Entity state and active operational workflows are coordinated dynamically. - **Strategic Drivers & Goals**: Holistic Patient-Centric Care, High Concurrency without Serialization, Real-Time Healthcare Coordination.
#### Capability Realisation & Configuration - **Primary Capabilities**: Shapes `EC-01` (Managed Entity & Relationship), `EC-02` (Context Management), and `EC-10` (Activity & Execution). - **Component Boundary Impact**: Validates the **Digital Twin** as an active management construct bridging the **Mneme ↔ Ponos** boundary, while asserting that the Twin is an architectural construct rather than an independent deployable platform component.
#### Downstream Direction (Domains 03–13) - Application Architecture (Domain 05) must model Twin archetypes using composite context (combining multiple resources such as Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Location) rather than equating twins to single FHIR resources or permanent background threads.

Reference standing is preserved; no direct platform supervision responsibility is established.

element.name: [CT3] Operational & Clinical Calendar Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate projections of operational and clinical calendars and correlate temporal events without taking ownership of source bookings or rosters.
**Overview**
Coordinate projections of operational and clinical calendars and correlate temporal events without taking ownership of source bookings or rosters. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Coordinate projections of operational and clinical calendars and correlate temporal events without taking ownership of source bookings or rosters.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: [Topic] Care
element.documentation: **Description**: Information establishing the contexts within which healthcare occurs, including encounters, episodes, care-place associations, progression events and longitudinal relationships that provide continuity and context across care interactions.

element.name: Care-Team Collaboration
element.documentation: - **Purpose**: Governs the active, multidisciplinary clinical team assembled around a specific patient for an acute episode, chronic disease management programme, or inpatient stay. - **Participating Roles**: `Clinician` (Lead & Consulting), `Care Coordinator`, `Patient`, `Carer`, `Performer`. - **Governed Activities**: Shared care planning, real-time longitudinal health record (LHR) review, multidisciplinary ward rounds, clinical messaging, and transition-of-care handovers.

element.name: [CT2] Ambulatory Care
element.documentation:
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for ambulatory care services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Overview**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for ambulatory care services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Intent**
Identify and track the operational and infrastructure dependencies necessary for ambulatory care services to function, retaining each dependency provider's responsibility.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Ambulatory Care is an established Adjacent delivery context retained for understanding information used around care without inpatient admission. The RAD establishes no atomic enabling Feature decomposition for it. The entry therefore locates the context without claiming a separate scheduling, treatment or clinical progression mandate for Harmonia.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
The contextual entry does not allocate BC tiers or require a distinct platform function for every ambulatory activity.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Adjacent standing preserves contextual participation while clinical service delivery remains external.

element.name: [CT3] Health Service Implementation Support
element.documentation:
Support establishment of the framed service through applicable organisational preparation and programmes of work.
Health Service Implementation Support assists establishment of the framed service through organisational preparation and programmes of work. It connects the service model to practical readiness for introduction while recognising that recruitment, training, equipment and technology changes retain their own owners. Support therefore contributes to establishment without becoming an all-purpose implementation authority.
**Boundary**
It does not absorb HR, facilities, procurement or ICT responsibilities or establish operational-readiness ancestry.

element.name: [Feature] Governed Identity Correction
element.documentation:
Apply administrative identity updates, linked-record corrections, and split/merge notifications propagated from authoritative sources.
Governed correction applies externally authoritative identity updates and their consequences to Harmonia-managed associations. Administrative review concerns the legitimate application of the source outcome; it does not grant Harmonia an EMPI merge engine or authority to select a golden person record.

element.name: [CT3] Primary Care Coordination
element.documentation:
Definition unresolved in the baseline. No definition has been synthesised from the name.
---
## History
### Capability Overview — predecessor explanation
Primary Care enables information continuity between general practice and other care settings through shared-record ingestion and notifications of acute events. A GP's notes, summaries and immunisation records can contribute to the longitudinal view, while admission and discharge information can return to the registered practitioner. The enabling responsibility is the connection between contexts, rather than practice management or primary clinical care.
### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Receiving a summary or dispatching a notification does not perform consultation, clinical review or follow-up.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
These flows materially support continuity across primary and acute care without assigning general-practice authority to Harmonia.
## Qualified relationship assertions

element.name: [CT3] Clinical Device Inventory Management
element.documentation:
Establish what devices exist and their managed asset identity, specification, ownership/custody and inventory context.
Clinical Device Inventory Management establishes the managed identity and inventory context of the device estate. Specification, ownership and custody make it possible to distinguish which devices exist from their current release, deployment or use. That stable asset context supports subsequent technology-management responsibilities without claiming their different outcomes.
**Boundary**
Inventory presence does not establish readiness, functional release state or current assignment to a care requirement.

The Maintenance membership discrepancy is preserved under Unresolved Business Capability matters; no eighth CT3 is inferred."}]

element.name: [CT3] Care-Place Allocation
element.documentation:
Allocate an applicable care place to a care requirement.
Care-Place Allocation associates a care requirement with an applicable care place. Its outcome is the allocation itself, distinct from defining the place or establishing its readiness. This separation supports reasoning about reserved, allocated and usable places without assuming that an apparently empty location is fit for the requirement.
**Boundary**
Allocation does not establish clinical suitability beyond the applicable context or make an unready place ready.

Care Resource Deployment consumes availability, role, qualification, engagement and privilege context without changing authoritative rosters, qualifications, employment or privilege records. It establishes no Harmonia authority over clinical work, enterprise assets or hospital-wide logistics. Operational capacity is distinct from strategic/tactical capacity planning and from collective service readiness (OI-BC-002)."}]

element.name: [Feature] Clinical Handover Context Assembly
element.documentation:
Collate current ward patient lists, active medical concerns, and pending tasks for nursing shift handovers.
Handover context assembly brings patient lists, current concerns and pending tasks together for the participants conducting a shift handover. Assembly is the established responsibility: it does not perform clinical review, decide pending clinical work or manage the handover itself.

element.name: [CT3] Care Responsibility Transition
element.documentation:
Establish and coordinate who has actually assumed applicable care responsibility.
Care Responsibility Transition establishes who has actually assumed applicable care responsibility and coordinates that transition. Its purpose is to prevent physical movement or exchanged information from being mistaken for accountable acceptance. It gives care continuity a responsibility meaning that a transport checkpoint or delivered referral cannot establish alone.
**Boundary**
Patient arrival, message receipt and departure do not by themselves demonstrate accepted responsibility.

element.name: [CT2] Ward Operations
element.documentation:
Ward Operations coordinates ward occupancy and care-place context and assembles the information needed around shift changes. Its responsibility includes the ward-specific meaning of capacity and patient flow rather than a generic resource counter. It can make pending concerns and tasks visible without becoming the authority managing clinical handover.
**Overview**
Ward Operations coordinates ward occupancy and care-place context and assembles the information needed around shift changes. Its responsibility includes the ward-specific meaning of capacity and patient flow rather than a generic resource counter. It can make pending concerns and tasks visible without becoming the authority managing clinical handover.
**Intent**
Ward Operations coordinates ward occupancy and care-place context and assembles the information needed around shift changes. Its responsibility includes the ward-specific meaning of capacity and patient flow rather than a generic resource counter. It can make pending concerns and tasks visible without becoming the authority managing clinical handover.
**Boundary**
Information administration does not confer authority over the represented person, organisation, service, place, device or clinical activity.
---

### Boundary — predecessor explanation
Handover information assembly is distinct from performing or managing handover. Context-specific capacity remains with Ward Operations.
### Harmonia Architectural Relevance — predecessor explanation
Correlated ward state and contextual information materially support operational continuity.

element.name: [CT3] Care Support Work Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate authorised operational support work: what needs doing, who performs it and how progression, completion or escalation is coordinated.
Care Support Work Coordination organises authorised operational support work around care: what needs doing, who will perform it and how progress, completion or escalation is coordinated. It gives supporting activity an explicit progression responsibility, rather than assuming that issuing a request means the work occurred. The work remains bounded by applicable authority and resource constraints.
**Boundary**
Dispatch does not establish worker availability, qualification or privilege, and support coordination does not determine clinical work.

element.name: Energeia
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** discrete Software Component owning Harmonia operational management: “Is Harmonia itself operating as expected?” It observes work-to-be-done, work-being-done and work-done, outstanding ActionableTasks, FulfillmentTask activity, Journey progression, stalled/incomplete activity, Praxis context, abnormal behaviour and operational information for reporting/assurance. - **Candidate services/features:** **Praxis Management Services** (F11) and **Journey Management Services** (F38), plus operational observation and reporting (F39). Detailed Feature/Service/internal-construct/subordinate- Component decomposition remains unresolved (CDG-39); service-set names do not manufacture independently deployable components. - **Information:** owns Praxis C06 and Journey C35 at the application level. Mneme manages their governed information and retains ActionableTask, FulfillmentTask and Pragma management. Observing operational significance does not transfer management of that information or referenced clinical facts. - **Persistence:** Mnemosyne C&G provides Praxis/configuration durability; Mnemosyne O&A provides Journey/operational-assurance durability, through Mneme governed management. Energeia application ownership is distinct from durable persistence responsibility; physical structures remain unresolved. - **Collaboration/relationships:** associated execution/activity responsibilities retain U02 specialisation/reuse. Praxis aggregates Pathway [0..1] and has a working Aggregation relationship to Journey with cardinalities unresolved. Dokimasia uses Praxis as assurance basis and Journey as observed evidence subject, preserving independence and terminal rules. Iris presents operational views; presentation does not own Harmonia operational management. - **Release boundary:** for **R1.x/R2.x, Observe → Report**. Energeia SHALL NOT autonomously change execution, redistribute workload, modify Routes, Pathways, Pub/Sub or Praxis, intervene in resilience or adjust capacity merely from workload, failure, Journey, capacity, assurance or anomaly observations. Existing explicitly governed execution/recovery behaviour retains its own authority; observation grants no new adaptive authority. - **Separate management plane:** external IT/Ops manages infrastructure, network, containers/Kubernetes, JVM/runtime, databases, technical health/capacity and platform resilience. Energeia manages/observes Harmonia as Harmonia. This distinction selects no deployment topology or infrastructure integration. - **Deferred direction:** **R3 Adaptive Load and Resilience Service** (F40): Observe → Analyse → Decide → Adapt, with feedback to observation. R1.x/R2.x observability should permit later capability without embedding it now. Policy/control loops, algorithms, mechanisms, infrastructure integration and AI decision architecture are deliberately undesigned (CDG-41). - **Standing:** U06 adjudicated these candidate responsibilities; it did not itself establish whole-candidate acceptance or Step B. Current A4/B1 standing is recorded in the [orientation](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/README.md). Possible upstream omissions require later review, without deriving Business Architecture or capability demand here.

element.name: [Topic] Encounter
element.documentation:
**Status: RESOLVED — APPROVED, with explicit unresolved further authority/evidence details.**
**Description**: Information describing a bounded interaction in which healthcare is delivered or healthcare-related activity occurs for an individual within a particular context.
**Definition** An Encounter may provide the care-interaction context within which zero or more Healthcare Service Deliveries occur. A Healthcare Service Delivery may occur without an associated Encounter.
Encounter and HealthcareServiceDelivery are distinct Information Concepts. A single Encounter may contextualise multiple HealthcareServiceDelivery instances [0..*], and delivery may exist independently of Encounter context.
- Encounter ≠ HealthcareServiceDelivery. Encounter existence does not establish that any service was delivered. - The relationship is optional contextual association, not mandatory lifecycle progression, identity, containment or a component/state of Encounter. - The approved [0..*] multiplicity concerns deliveries contextualised by an Encounter; no further reverse cardinality is inferred. - Package1's DeliverableHealthcareService → optional Order → HealthcareServiceDelivery → ServiceOutcome semantics remain unchanged. Encounter is not made mandatory anywhere in that chain. - Further source/correlation qualification and universal delivery/outcome ownership are not established by this decision.
**Review consequence:** G2-Q05's Encounter/delivery existence, basic meaning and multiplicity questions are resolved. Further qualifications and the Referral portion remain unreviewed; no Referral Disposition review is commenced.
Source standing: Explicitly APPROVED G2 decision only; G2 remains candidate/open and all residual qualifications remain unresolved.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/episode-encounter.md` — ### 3.1 Encounter — G2-D02/D03 approved meaning; remaining classification/tracking boundary B. Standing: G2 candidate contribution with only the explicitly recorded decisions approved; semantic classifications and residual questions remain qualified.
- **Semantic Classification**: Activity / Contextual Binding — exact metamodel classification and administrative tracking/Assembly boundary remain under G2-Q03; actual care-interaction/context meaning is established by G2-D02/D03. - **Definition**: Information identifying and contextualising an actual bounded care interaction between a healthcare subject and participating healthcare providers, distinct from scheduling context and from actual Healthcare Service Delivery/performance. - **Necessity**: EC-IR1 and EC-IR2 require continuity of encounter tracking across planning, arrival, active care and discharge information. G2-D02/D03 establish the represented care-interaction meaning; how administrative planning/tracking relates to that actual interaction and the Assembly remains [G2-Q03](../../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/reviews/package2-g2-block1-review.md#g2-q03). - **Characteristics**: Source/namespace-qualified encounter identity, subject reference, attending participant, clinical class, admitting diagnosis/context as supplied, and attributable administrative state. These are governed characteristics/relationships, not automatically separate Concepts. - **Boundary**: Planned tracking information does not prove an actual Encounter occurred. Appointment existence is not occurrence evidence, and an actual Encounter does not prove a prospective Appointment existed. An Encounter may contextualise zero or more deliveries, but neither proves delivery nor owns/contains it; delivery may occur without Encounter context. Encounter identity remains distinct from Person, Appointment and Episode identity.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/episode-encounter.md` — ## 1. Purpose & Semantic Boundary. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval.
Episode & Encounter Administration requires identifiable patient/provider encounter contexts, administrative progression and historical care-place associations. Encounter denotes actual care interaction/context; its administrative tracking may include planning without proving an actual interaction occurred. G2-D03 establishes that an Encounter may contextualise zero or more HealthcareServiceDelivery instances, and a delivery may occur without an Encounter. G2-D01 establishes Episode as longitudinal treatment context for one or more Problems/Conditions across related Encounters, providing an assurance, workflow and financial perspective.
```text Longitudinal / episode context ≠ bounded encounter context Appointment ≠ Encounter ≠ HealthcareServiceDelivery Encounter administrative progression ≠ clinical service performance Care-place association ≠ Care-Place Definition ≠ operational bed state ```
The owner name includes Episode, but the reconciled Functions, Services and ownership-matrix asset are encounter-specific. G1 K5 still prohibits using owner-name correction to infer Episode ownership. G2-D01 supplies Episode's approved meaning directly; it does not allocate an upstream owner, new Feature or Service. Longitudinal record synthesis remains with Patient Clinical Record. Episode is not merely a Collection of Encounters; Encounter association contributes to its longitudinal treatment meaning without establishing ownership or containment.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/episode-encounter.md` — ## 6. Temporal & Lifecycle Characteristics. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval.
Encounter progression requires transition/occurrence time distinct from asserted/recorded time. Care-place movement requires effective association periods to explain where a subject was accommodated over time. Planned timing and actual arrival/care/discharge timing remain distinguishable where evidenced; neither scheduled time nor a last-known state establishes actual service start/end.
G1 K10 preserves independently established Strategy ON_LEAVE and the Behaviour/Process progressions. Their applicability and transition correspondence remain unresolved (G1 U8). The Process's triage, documentation finalisation, coding and legal-closure conditions remain local; they do not become every Encounter's lifecycle. ON_LEAVE is neither omitted nor mapped to another state.
Information lifecycle governance, real-world care progression and Business Process progression may correlate but are distinct. Information corrections preserve the Foundation's history/provenance rules without changing history of the actual encounter. The [Discharge Management responsibility](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/04-health-service-operations.md#215-discharge-management) and [Discharge Progression Process](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md#413-discharge-progression-process) now establish the preparation versus confirmed-exit distinction: applicable information may be prepared, published or communicated earlier, while FEAT-HSO-29 departure notifications, updated bed-state communication and finalised-summary dispatch are triggered by confirmed physical exit. Earlier preparation does not satisfy that trigger. This supersedes only that portion of G1 U9; detailed applicability and timing, the relation between summary signing and finalisation, discharge-authorisation workflows, universal Encounter closure and downstream transitions remain unestablished. No additional publication event, universal lifecycle, atomic transition linkage or FHIR status mapping is inferred.
Episode is longitudinal treatment context under G2-D01. No start/end criteria, episode closure state, Encounter-association effective rules or common lifecycle with its related Encounters are established. G2-D02's retrospectively established Appointment must not be mistaken for prospective scheduling; G2-D03's contextual association does not create an Encounter-to-delivery lifecycle.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/episode-encounter.md` — ## 8. Explicit Boundaries, Unresolved Semantics & Downstream Realisation. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval.
G2-Q03 retains metamodel classification and the administrative tracking/Assembly boundary after approval of actual care-interaction meaning. Episode is established; G2-Q04 concerns only unresolved authority/responsibility, detailed identity, association rules/evidence and temporal/lifecycle details. The [prior Episode Context suggestion](../../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/reviews/package2-g2-block1-review.md#7-non-authoritative-suggestions) is historical and superseded by G2-D01, not a current D suggestion. No Episode = Collection of Encounters rule, membership mechanism, hierarchy or universal lifecycle is added.
G2-Q05's Encounter/delivery optional contextual association and [0..*] multiplicity are resolved by G2-D03; additional authority/evidence qualifications and the unrelated Referral portion remain unreviewed. G2-Q06 retains the Assembly boundary. G1 U4's universal delivery/outcome authority, U8's ON_LEAVE correspondence and U9's discharge applicability/timing beyond the established preparation/confirmed-exit distinction remain unresolved. No clinical responsibility transfer is inferred from movement or discharge, and no operational bed model is derived.
No FHIR mapping, application component, class, persistence entity, schema, API, integration message, cache model or implementation allocation is created. [AX-17](../../../motivation/principle/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) governs the derivation itself.

element.name: REQ-FND-004: Explicit Indeterminate Outcome
element.documentation:
### Normative Requirement Statement > **Where Harmonia cannot establish the outcome of a managed operation with sufficient certainty, the outcome shall be represented explicitly as indeterminate and shall not be interpreted as either success or failure without subsequent reconciliation or another authoritative determination.**
### Architectural Intent & Rationale In distributed networks, communication timeouts, socket disconnects, and unacknowledged dispatches leave the status of remote operations uncertain. In the presence of a network partition or destination crash, a client cannot know whether an update was processed and the ACK was lost, or whether the update was never received.
A frequent architectural failure mode is "binary collapsing": assuming an unconfirmed operation failed (triggering duplicate side effects on blind retry) or assuming it succeeded (ignoring unperformed clinical orders). Harmonia mandates that uncertainty must be preserved and explicitly represented as `INDETERMINATE`.
### Reconciliation & Retry Semantics - This requirement does **not** prohibit automated retries or resilient recovery. - It mandates that retry mechanisms must be safe, idempotent, and reconciliation-aware. An indeterminate outcome must be resolved through explicit reconciliation (such as querying destination state or verifying idempotency tokens) rather than blind, speculative assumption.
- **Primary Motivation**: [Silent Data Loss via False Acceptance](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/assessments.md), [Continuous Clinical Service Availability](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md) - **Governing Principle**: [AX-15 (Uncertainty Is Preserved Until Resolved)](../principle/ef8abbaec37e4890ad78b9f263e67906.md) - **Historical Identifier Reference**: `REQ-UNCERT-001`

element.name: Meaning-Centric Provenance and Traceability
element.documentation:
#### Strategic Approach > **Preserve provenance, authority, attribution and traceability for information-significant and business-significant actions and state changes, while avoiding unnecessary elevation of transient operational mechanics into enduring business evidence.**
Healthcare integration requires undeniable accountability without overwhelming storage or logging systems with low-level operational noise. This course of action establishes that: - Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where required by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction, security or assurance needs. Routine technical activity SHALL NOT automatically require durable evidentiary recording. - Required semantic attribution records who, what, when, why and under whose authority. Telemetry, operational facts, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct; being evidence is contextual, not intrinsic to every recorded fact. - Transient operational mechanics (e.g., thread switches, socket retries, queue polling, network pinging) represent operational telemetry, not business or clinical evidence. - Strategy sets the architectural requirement for semantic attribution and non-repudiation without dictating specific implementation mechanisms (such as cryptographic signatures, write-once ledgers, or specific storage engines) at this layer.
#### Motivational Grounding & Traceability - **Architectural Axioms**: - `AX-06` (Explicit Authority): Information authority and credibility remain explicit and independent of technical transport or persistence. Required attribution preserves the applicable source or actor authority without making every access evaluation durable evidence. - `AX-07` (Intrinsic Security): Security, authorization, and provenance are embedded within operations, not bolted on. - `AX-08` (Meaning over Machinery): Record semantic and business meaning, not transient technical machinery. - `AX-14` (Preserve Distinctions): Distinguish enduring clinical/business evidence from transient technical logs. - **Strategic Drivers & Goals**: Regulatory Accountability, Clinical Governance, Legal Auditability, Evidentiary Integrity.
#### Capability Realisation & Configuration - **Primary Capabilities**: Shapes `EC-06` (Policy & Control) and `EC-07` (Provenance & Traceability). - **Component Boundary Impact**: Governs how all logical components emit evidence, ensuring that audit trails capture governed business assertions rather than unmasked PHI or low-level machine noise (supporting Invariants 6 and 7).
#### Downstream Direction (Domains 03–13) - Security Architecture (Domain 08) and Information Architecture (Domain 04) define the governed audit and provenance representations (with Kleio as established downstream evidence traceability), preserving PHI-safe capture and verifiable integrity according to applicable obligations. Strategy does not select a verification technology.

element.name: Harmonia.Sylloge
element.documentation:
- **Role/responsibility:** **Binary Content Management subsystem** responsible for governed association, resolution, retrieval and assembly of binary content associated with Harmonia-managed information. [U17 canonical view](feea742463b84021b66853d287d8916f.md). - **Feature/information:** F31/D15; binary-content metadata, Information Unit associations, location/resolution knowledge, retrieval, on-demand assembly from one or more payloads and knowledge of Harmonia-managed versus externally managed content. Logical information and binary payload remain distinct. - **Custody/persistence:** physical custody may remain external; management does not require copying every payload into Harmonia. Where applicable, Mnemosyne provides Harmonia persistence services without acquiring Binary Content Management. Sylloge is not a generic persistence manager. - **Collaborations/exclusions:** Mneme remains Context and Pragma Manager with its established service boundary; applicable processing components may obtain/resolve content through Sylloge. Agora retains native collaboration media and the record/reference/activity concerning formal binary content; Sylloge retains that content's Binary Content Management. Omilia acquires no such responsibility. Source information/domain authority and external physical custody are preserved. - **Standing:** U17 adjudicated Candidate Architecture; former A2 responsibility question CDG-25 closed. [Storage, representations, APIs, algorithms and lifecycle mechanisms](feea742463b84021b66853d287d8916f.md) remain non-blocking later design. No module, dependency or deployment allocation.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sylloge-binary-content-management.md` — ## Application responsibility. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
> **Harmonia.Sylloge — Binary Content Management subsystem responsible for the > governed association, resolution, retrieval and assembly of binary content > associated with Harmonia-managed information.**
Sylloge is an Information Systems Layer application subsystem/component. Its Candidate Architecture responsibility includes:
- Management of binary-content metadata. - Management of associations between Harmonia Information Units and associated binary content. - Knowledge sufficient to locate and resolve binary content. - Retrieval of binary content. - Assembly on demand where required logical content is represented by, or constructed from, one or more binary payloads. - Knowledge of whether applicable binary content is Harmonia-managed or externally managed.
This establishes **Binary Content Management** as an application information responsibility. F31 allocates the behaviour and D15 records the associated information responsibility; neither a storage product nor an upstream Information Concept is introduced by that allocation.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sylloge-binary-content-management.md` — ## Management and physical custody. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
```mermaid flowchart TB IU["Information Unit"] -->|"associated with / references"| S["Harmonia.Sylloge: Binary Content Management"] S -->|"metadata association; location / resolution; retrieval; assembly; custody knowledge"| B["Binary payload"] B --- H["Harmonia-managed"] B --- E["Externally managed"] ```
**Sylloge's responsibility for binary content does not imply that Harmonia must physically persist every binary payload.** Physical custody may remain with an external authoritative/source system. Knowledge of and governed access to that content do not require copying it into Harmonia. External management and originating information/domain authority remain explicit.
Where Harmonia takes physical custody, Sylloge retains Binary Content Management responsibility without becoming a generic persistence manager. Logical clinical information and its binary payload remain distinct; an Information Unit reference does not itself establish physical custody or make the payload an Information Unit.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sylloge-binary-content-management.md` — ## Mneme and Mnemosyne. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
**Application information responsibility is distinct from persistence responsibility.** Mnemosyne remains Harmonia's Persistence Manager. Where Sylloge-managed content or metadata requires Harmonia persistence, Mnemosyne may provide the applicable persistence services under the established [Mneme/Mnemosyne boundary](7985e647bf9e4ca3ba70faf9e3e4ae02.md). That service relationship does not transfer Binary Content Management to Mnemosyne or confer durable-state establishment on Sylloge.
Mneme remains the **Context and Pragma Manager**, with its four principal exposed services and established managed-information access boundary. Sylloge is not absorbed into Mneme and creates no alternative raw cache/database access path. Where processing needs binary content, Mneme, Ponos, Ergo or another applicable component may interact with Sylloge to obtain or resolve it. This is a minimal responsibility relationship; detailed calls, routing and contracts are deferred. No Mneme service, Mnemosyne responsibility or persistence domain is redesigned.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sylloge-binary-content-management.md` — ## Agora and Omilia. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
Agora-native collaboration media may remain **Agora-managed collaboration information**. Omilia performs collaboration operations under the established [Agora/Omilia architecture](d1c4053e68384080b8eb79d2008632ba.md).
```text Formally managed clinical/operational binary content | v Sylloge ^ | reference | Agora-managed Room ```
When a Room presents, links to, discusses, notifies about or captures activity concerning formally managed binary content, Agora retains the collaboration record/reference/activity. Sylloge retains Binary Content Management for that content; Agora does not thereby become its custodian. Omilia acquires no Binary Content Management responsibility. The originating logical information owner and any external physical custodian retain their respective responsibilities.
## Source-qualified contribution
Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sylloge-binary-content-management.md` — ## Deliberate deferred design. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.
The application responsibility is established, rather than deferred out of the Candidate Architecture. The following remain later design matters under [CDG-25](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#binary-custody-question):
- Object storage, filesystem, database BLOB, PACS/VNA and content-addressable storage technology or architecture. - Streaming, caching, replication, binary sharding, compression, encryption mechanisms and physical storage topology. - FHIR Binary, DocumentReference, Media and DICOM representations. - Detailed retrieval APIs, assembly algorithms and external repository adapters. - Lifecycle, retention and binary versioning mechanisms.
No assumption that all content is copied into Harmonia accompanies these deferrals. The Logical Data ↔ Application Features ↔ Application Components triad and the distinction between Logical Data, Application Data Objects, Persistence Data Structures and Technology Platforms remain. Themis governance, Kleio audit, originating authority and AX-05/06/07/13/14/15/17/18 constraints apply without a new security, audit or persistence mechanism. No build, process or deployment boundary is selected.

element.name: [CT3] Prescription Medication Dispensing
element.documentation:
Professionally prepare and provide medication according to an applicable authorised prescription/order and dispensing requirements.
Prescription Medication Dispensing is the professional preparation and provision of medication against an applicable authorised prescription or order. It fulfils a pharmacy responsibility grounded in the prescribed intent and dispensing requirements. The resulting dispensing event provides different evidence from the prescribing decision and from later administration to the individual.
**Boundary**
Dispensing does not establish that medication was administered; unresolved specialised compounding must not be silently assigned here.

element.name: Kleio
element.documentation: - **Role/responsibility:** **Harmonia's authoritative Audit Information Management component.** Kleio owns authoritative Audit Capture, creation/management of authoritative audit information, canonical FHIR **AuditEvent** representation, preservation/retrieval of audit history, semantically significant user/system audit activity and provision/preparation of historical audit context for operational and assurance use. [U07](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u07), [AX-08](../../motivation/principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md). - **Audit Capture:** clients report semantically significant auditable occurrences and necessary context through a **Kleio-provided contract/library/API**. **Clients SHALL NOT be required to construct FHIR AuditEvent resources.** Kleio constructs and manages the authoritative representation; client API and mapping details remain unresolved. - **Information:** FHIR AuditEvent is the authoritative audit-event representation, without requiring every internal Kleio structure to be an AuditEvent. Indexes, correlation structures and prepared historical context may support management. **Authoritative audit evidence SHALL remain distinguishable from derived, correlated, contextualised or prepared historical views.** Existing meaningful provenance responsibilities remain; AuditEvent does not redefine all evidence. - **User activity:** semantically significant access/view, governed search, create/change/delete, submit/approve/reject, disclosure/export, operational action and relevant denied activity may require capture. These are examples, not a universal event taxonomy; “delete” grants no physical managed-information DELETE. Generic UI telemetry/clickstream is outside Kleio; UI security assurance and governance remain **Somebody Else's Problem (SEP)**. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** **Audit is not Governance. Audit is not Assurance.** Kleio may consume Journey information and Dokimasia outputs and provide historical audit context back to Dokimasia, without evaluating assurance or governing the subject. Dokimasia's governed record/result remains authoritative evidence of its assurance activity; its [terminal rules](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#dokimasia-terminal-boundaries) prohibit a separate own-execution AuditEvent and recursive assurance. Consumption of its outputs does not circumvent those rules. #### Mandatory capture authority and the audited Identity > **Subject of audit evidence ≠ authority performing audit capture.** Kleio performs mandatory authoritative audit capture under **intrinsic platform authority** associated with its established architectural audit responsibility. The originating/acting Identity remains evidence recorded by Kleio; it is not the authority under which the mandatory AuditEvent is persisted. Kleio does not borrow that Identity's PEP-Criteria merely to record its activity, including activity denied to that Identity. Identity-derived authority granted to human/system Identities remains resolved and enforced through Themis. Kleio capture executes within established security context and remains governed by Harmonia security policy, with Themis retaining policy evaluation ownership. Mandatory capture is neither a security bypass nor a policy exception. [AX-07](../../../../docs/markdown/governance/architectural-axioms.md#kleio-mandatory-capture-authority) incorporates this adjudication. Where authoritative audit capture is required for a governed operation and Kleio cannot exercise that platform authority sufficiently to capture the required evidence, the governed operation **SHALL fail closed**. Durable target availability remains necessary; authority alone establishes no successful capture. This authority applies specifically to Kleio mandatory authoritative audit capture. It grants no equivalent authority to other components or other Kleio activities. Any proposed equivalent responsibility requires separate architecture adjudication; representation, policy/enforcement mechanics and transaction coordination remain [CDG-43](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#kleio-detailed-contracts). #### Immutable history and longitudinal evidence Authoritative AuditEvents are immutable. An existing AuditEvent SHALL NOT be corrected, amended, overwritten or silently replaced. Correction or qualification SHALL create a **new AuditEvent**, preserve the earlier event unchanged and refer back to it as appropriate. The earlier assertion remains part of historical record. Journey is the governed representation of observed Harmonia activity/progression; AuditEvent is the authoritative audit representation of a significant auditable occurrence. Journey is an important audit source, **not the audit boundary**. A Journey may relate to many AuditEvents; an AuditEvent may exist without Journey. **Journey participation SHALL NOT be a prerequisite for Audit Capture.** > **Reference by default; replicate only where necessary to preserve longitudinal > audit evidence.** Kleio SHALL NOT duplicate authoritative source information merely because it is audit-relevant. Where historical state can be reliably resolved longitudinally, Kleio references it with sufficient **identity, version, provenance and temporal detail**. Version identity alone is not assumed to supply all temporal detail. Only where the authoritative source cannot guarantee retrieval of the information as it existed at the audited point in time may Kleio clone/replicate the necessary source information within or in association with the authoritative AuditEvent to preserve required longitudinal evidence. Detailed FHIR attachment/reference mechanisms remain unresolved. #### Auditability and R1.x/R2.x availability > **Harmonia SHALL NOT perform an auditable activity unless the required audit > information can be authoritatively and durably captured.** > > **If Kleio cannot authoritatively capture required audit information, Harmonia > is DOWN.** Audit Capture is not best-effort and SHALL NOT be assumed reconstructable later from logs, Journey information or incidental operational state. Transaction, retry/failover and health/readiness mechanisms are deliberately unresolved. Kleio retains audit application ownership; Mneme provides governed Context/Pragma access and Mnemosyne **Harmonia Operations & Assurance** establishes durable audit state. For R1.x/R2.x, multiple **independent authoritative audit persistence targets** through Mneme/Mnemosyne are permitted. At least **one configured target capable of durably establishing the required audit information** is sufficient for continued Harmonia operation. If none can establish it, Harmonia is unavailable and fails closed. Target count, selection and whether one/some/all receive an event are unresolved; targets SHALL NOT be called replicas without established replication semantics. > **For R1.x/R2.x, audit data harmonisation between independent Mnemosyne audit > persistence targets is outside Harmonia scope — Somebody Else's Problem (SEP).** R1.x/R2.x guarantees neither identical histories, complete copies of all AuditEvents, automatic convergence, reconciliation after disconnection nor unified cross-target longitudinal history. Different targets may expose different histories; an immutable AuditEvent remains authoritative without its target holding the whole corpus. No future harmonisation/convergence mechanism is selected. - **Standing:** U07 resolves responsibility, representation, immutability, longitudinal evidence, availability and release scope; [CDG-43](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#kleio-detailed-contracts) retains detailed capture/query/correlation/retention/processing and persistence mechanisms. Historical FHIR/operational storage structures remain provenance, without competing with the established O&A semantic alignment. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/candidate-feature-map.md` — ``table assertion: | F15 | Authoritative Audit Capture, immutable audit history and historical context preparation/retrieval | [Kleio C03](component-register.md#c03); clients report significant occurrences through Kleio contract; Kleio constructs FHIR AuditEvent; Mneme/O&A supplies management/durability | AuditEvent distinct from Journey, Provenance and derived/prepared historical context. Reference authoritative source history by default; necessary replication only when audited historical state cannot be retrieved | U07/U15; AX-07/08/09. Mandatory capture uses Kleio-specific governed intrinsic platform authority; originating Identity is evidence, not capture authority. Required durable capture is a precondition of Harmonia operation; one capable independent configured audit target suffices, none means DOWN/fail closed. Harmonisation SEP. Audit is neither Governance nor Assurance; no UI clickstream/security assurance. Dokimasia terminal rules remain; detail CDG-43. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | F15 | Authoritative Audit Capture, immutable audit history and historical context preparation/retrieval | [Kleio C03](fefda110e2274884ad58906733606efd.md); clients report significant occurrences through Kleio contract; Kleio constructs FHIR AuditEvent; Mneme/O&A supplies management/durability | AuditEvent distinct from Journey, Provenance and derived/prepared historical context. Reference authoritative source history by default; necessary replication only when audited historical state cannot be retrieved | U07/U15; AX-07/08/09. Mandatory capture uses Kleio-specific governed intrinsic platform authority; originating Identity is evidence, not capture authority. Required durable capture is a precondition of Harmonia operation; one capable independent configured audit target suffices, none means DOWN/fail closed. Harmonisation SEP. Audit is neither Governance nor Assurance; no UI clickstream/security assurance. Dokimasia terminal rules remain; detail CDG-43. | ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/data-and-persistence.md` — ``table assertion: | D12 | Authoritative FHIR **AuditEvent**; provenance/transition references; supporting indexes/correlation/prepared historical context; governed Dokimasia assurance record/result | Kleio owns authoritative Audit Capture/management/history; clients report occurrences, Kleio constructs AuditEvent; derived/prepared views remain distinguishable | Kleio → Mneme → Mnemosyne O&A. AuditEvents immutable: new linked event corrects/qualifies, earlier unchanged. Reference source history by default; replicate necessary evidence only when historical retrieval cannot be guaranteed | U07, AX-08/09 and U02 terminal rules. Journey participation not required; no separate Dokimasia own-execution AuditEvent. Required authoritative durable capture essential; one capable independent audit target suffices, cross-target harmonisation SEP. Mechanisms CDG-43. |``. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved. | D12 | Authoritative FHIR **AuditEvent**; provenance/transition references; supporting indexes/correlation/prepared historical context; governed Dokimasia assurance record/result | Kleio owns authoritative Audit Capture/management/history; clients report occurrences, Kleio constructs AuditEvent; derived/prepared views remain distinguishable | Kleio → Mneme → Mnemosyne O&A. AuditEvents immutable: new linked event corrects/qualifies, earlier unchanged. Reference source history by default; replicate necessary evidence only when historical retrieval cannot be guaranteed | U07, AX-08/09 and U02 terminal rules. Journey participation not required; no separate Dokimasia own-execution AuditEvent. Required authoritative durable capture essential; one capable independent audit target suffices, cross-target harmonisation SEP. Mechanisms CDG-43. |

element.name: [CT3] External Task Coordination
element.documentation:
Coordinate work entering or leaving the Harmonia execution boundary with the system or actor responsible for undertaking and completing that work.
**Overview**
Coordinate work entering or leaving the Harmonia execution boundary with the system or actor responsible for undertaking and completing that work. The reviewed hierarchy assigns this enduring ability to its stated business-enabling context.
**Intent**
Coordinate work entering or leaving the Harmonia execution boundary with the system or actor responsible for undertaking and completing that work.
**Boundary**
Information administration and coordination preserve the authority of the responsible source, clinical actor and governed domain; they confer no additional real-world management authority.

element.name: Establish Assurance Context
element.documentation:
• Canonical Name: Establish Assurance Context.
• Definition: Establishes the governed subject, applicable assurance purpose and criteria, relevant temporal context, and contextual association of sufficient trustworthy source information as evidence required for an assurance activity.
• Scope: Includes the evidence-assembly responsibility previously described as Assurance Evidence Assembly; no separate evidence-assembly Function is established. Sufficiency is required for conclusion, not assumed merely because context is established; unavailable or insufficient evidence remains explicit.
• Information Boundary: Source information remains owned by its responsible source Capability. Its use as evidence does not transfer ownership or originating authority. Governed Assurance owns the contextual association that particular information constitutes evidence for a particular assurance purpose. Evidence association and applicable criteria may each be temporal and version-specific; association distinguishes the information state relevant to assurance from its current state.
• Realisation Boundary: Uses generic EC-02 context-management capability together with EC-14 assurance-specific semantics as documented in §4.1 (https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md#41-context-management-contribution). Establishment of Assurance Context prescribes no copying, persistence, aggregation, caching or other technical mechanism.
---
## History
### Function Overview — predecessor explanation
Context establishment makes particular source-owned information evidence for a particular assurance purpose, with applicable subject, criteria and time identified. It includes evidence assembly without assuming sufficiency or prescribing copying and storage. This contextual evidentiary association is the assurance responsibility; ownership of the source material remains unchanged.

Individual Care Delivery is the organisation's ability to understand an individual's health and act on that understanding through purposeful care. Its six constituent abilities distinguish establishing findings, interpreting their clinical meaning, choosing a response, performing care, observing change and evaluating care against its objectives. These distinctions describe responsibilities and outcomes rather than a compulsory sequence: a consultation or continuing episode may revisit several of them.
The same ability can be exercised in a hospital, a general practice, a home or a virtual consultation. Setting and time pattern affect the circumstances of care without changing the responsibility represented by this capability.
\cataloguefield{section}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
Assess, clinically determine, plan, intervene, monitor and review individual care independently of setting, mode, time pattern or organisational arrangement.
\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}
Support clinically meaningful care whose intent, performance, observed effects and continuing appropriateness can be distinguished.
\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}
Care access, appointments and operational coordination enable care but do not establish that it has been performed. Clinical judgement and the authority to deliver care remain with the responsible participants; possession or coordination of their information does not transfer that authority to Harmonia.
\cataloguefield{section}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}
Harmonia supplies and connects information used in individual care. The approved Health Information Access support trace is bounded: records can inform care, but direct assessment can establish findings independently, and access to a proposed intervention does not authorise its performance.

ameref{cap:bc-individual-care-delivery} & Linked responsibility references; historical records do not assert current ancestry.\\hline Harmonia relevance & Unresolved in the semantic baseline & Independent of element/placement status; never inherited from an ancestor.\\hline Evidence & \hyperref[rad:business:160]{business:160} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:160}); \hyperref[rad:business:162]{business:162} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:162}); \hyperref[rad:business:316]{business:316} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:316}); \hyperref[rad:business:320]{business:320} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:320}); \hyperref[rad:business:330]{business:330} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:330}) & Source standing does not approve the derived assertion.\\hline \end{longtable}\endgroup \cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}
Assessment establishes what is currently known about an individual's health through history, examination and measurement. Within Individual Care Delivery it supplies assessed findings, including findings obtained directly from the person rather than retrieved from an existing record. Its three children distinguish ways of establishing knowledge, rather than professions, clinical specialties or locations.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
The capability to establish an understanding of an individual's current health state through the collection, consideration and evaluation of relevant clinical, health and contextual information.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}
Give subsequent clinical interpretation a defensible account of the person's current state and relevant history.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}
Finding an abnormal measurement is distinguishable from deciding what it means clinically. Diagnosis, prognosis, selection of care and performance of care belong to adjacent abilities.

ameref{cap:bc-individual-care-delivery} $ightarrow$ 
ameref{cap:bc-individual-health-assessment} & Linked responsibility references; historical records do not assert current ancestry.\\hline Harmonia relevance & Unresolved in the semantic baseline & Independent of element/placement status; never inherited from an ancestor.\\hline Evidence & \hyperref[rad:business:324]{business:326} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:324}); \hyperref[rad:business:322]{business:322} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:322}); \hyperref[rad:business:330]{business:330} (p.\,\pageref{rad:business:330}) & Source standing does not approve the derived assertion.\\hline \end{longtable}\endgroup \cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Capability Overview}
Health History Assessment establishes clinically relevant understanding from a person's history and its surrounding context. Within assessment it contributes knowledge that a current examination or measurement alone may not reveal, while requiring consideration of the relevance of historical information to the present situation. Access to previous records can assist, but the responsibility is the assessment of history rather than retrieval itself.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
Establish relevant health knowledge from the individual’s history and applicable historical/\allowbreak{}contextual information.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}
Historical information does not become a current clinical conclusion merely because it is available; interpretation of the assessed findings remains Clinical Determination.

It distinguishes directly acquired clinical knowledge from the historical account and the measurement-focused contribution of its assessment siblings. Its outcome is a set of examination findings that can inform clinical interpretation, irrespective of the setting or profession exercising the ability.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
Establish health findings through clinical examination.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}
An examination finding is not itself a diagnosis, care plan or performed treatment.

Health Status Measurement establishes observations or measurements of an individual's health. Its contribution to assessment is evidence about the measured state, with a purpose distinct from developing a view over time or deciding the clinical meaning of a result. Measurements can inform both present assessment and later monitoring without collapsing those abilities.

Establish individual health observations or measurements.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}
Obtaining a value does not establish a temporal trend or the clinical significance of that value.

Clinical Determination turns assessed findings into clinically interpreted understanding of a person's condition, risk or prognosis. It represents the professional responsibility for deciding what the findings mean in the individual's clinical context, including the significance of changes identified through monitoring. This is the interpretive responsibility within Individual Care Delivery, rather than another method of collecting evidence.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
The capability to interpret assessed health information and establish clinically meaningful conclusions about an individual's health state, condition, risk or prognosis.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}
Establish clinical conclusions on which an intended response can be based.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}
Determining clinical meaning does not itself select the care response. No CT3 taxonomy has been adjudicated; diagnosis and prognostic judgement illustrate this responsibility without becoming additional catalogue elements.

Individual Care Planning establishes the intended course of care in response to assessed and clinically interpreted health information. It connects clinical understanding to objectives, intended interventions and monitoring needs. Its outcome is an expression of what should happen, allowing intended care to remain distinguishable from requests, operational arrangements and actions subsequently performed.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
The capability to establish the intended clinical response to an individual's assessed and clinically interpreted health state, including the objectives, interventions and monitoring required to progress their care.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}
Make the clinical response and its objectives explicit enough to guide care and later evaluate its effectiveness.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}
Prescribing can express clinical intent without establishing dispensing or administration. Scheduling or allocating resources does not perform the planned intervention. No CT3 decomposition is established.

Clinical Intervention is the ability to perform a clinical action under an established care intent. It marks the transition from intended care to care actually performed, whether the action seeks to alter, maintain or otherwise manage health. Its exercise can establish that treatment occurred even when the desired clinical result was not achieved.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
The capability to perform clinical actions intended to alter, maintain or otherwise manage an individual's health state in accordance with an established care intent.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}
Put the intended clinical response into practice through appropriately authorised care.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}
Orders and appointments express or arrange future activity; they are not evidence that the intervention occurred. Therapy, medication and procedural examples do not constitute an approved three-child taxonomy: that proposed decomposition remains provisional.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Preserved v0.1 Review Matters}
DN-BC-010 retains the intervention candidate as provisional pending a coherent peer taxonomy.

Monitoring develops a view of an individual's health over time so that change, stability or deviation can be recognised. Health State Monitoring establishes the aggregate temporally situated view; Care Response Monitoring considers that view in relation to a particular condition and treatment. Together they distinguish observation over time from a single measurement and from the clinical judgement prompted by a trend.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
The capability to observe and evaluate an individual's health state over time in order to identify clinically meaningful change, stability or deviation from an expected state or trajectory.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}
Make relevant trajectories visible while preserving what was observed and what still requires interpretation.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}
Monitoring does not establish the clinical significance of a change or judge whether care achieved its objectives. Those responsibilities remain Clinical Determination and Individual Care Review respectively.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Preserved v0.1 Review Matters}
Canonical BC evidence/\allowbreak{}context/\allowbreak{}consumption semantics are preserved in Markdown; the current governed RADS relationship types do not establish their machine-readable encoding. No stronger runtime or structural relation is substituted.

Health State Monitoring brings applicable monitored data into an aggregate view situated in time. Its purpose is to make the individual's changing or stable health state intelligible across observations, rather than leaving each observation isolated. Within monitoring it provides the broader view that can also be considered in relation to a particular treatment or condition.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
Establish an aggregate, temporally situated view of the individual’s health from applicable monitored data.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}
Aggregation is not clinical interpretation. Care Response Monitoring uses the established view rather than independently recreating it.

Care Response Monitoring considers the monitored health-state view in relation to a particular problem or condition and the treatment applied. It makes a response trajectory visible in its treatment context, helping distinguish a general change in health from a change relevant to the care being followed. It consumes the aggregate view established through Health State Monitoring.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
Scope that health-state view to a particular problem/\allowbreak{}condition and the treatment applied to it.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}
Identifying the response does not judge treatment effectiveness against objectives or determine a replacement treatment.

Individual Care Review asks whether care is achieving its intended objectives and whether the existing care intent remains suitable. Its children separate effectiveness from appropriateness: an intervention may have an effect yet no longer be suitable to continue, or remain a reasonable choice despite an inadequate response. Review therefore evaluates the relationship between care, outcomes and intent rather than simply repeating assessment.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
The capability to evaluate the progress and effectiveness of an individual's care against its intended objectives and establish the continuing appropriateness of the current care intent.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}
Establish whether continuing the current approach is justified and whether reconsideration is needed.
\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}
Recognising a need to change care does not establish the replacement plan. Monitoring supplies relevant observations; planning establishes revised intent.

Care Appropriateness Review evaluates whether the current care intent remains suitable for the individual in their present context. Its question concerns continuing suitability rather than whether treatment has produced a measurable effect. That distinction permits a review to recognise that effective care may no longer be appropriate to continue.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}
Evaluate whether the current intended care remains suitable in the individual’s current context.
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}
An appropriateness judgement can identify a need to reconsider care; establishing revised intent remains Individual Care Planning.
